rows.title: Atmospheric pressure - pressure belts; planetary, periodic and local winds; jet streams
sub: Group-II S2-10: Atmospheric pressure, planetary and local winds, jet streams

secs.t: Pressure belts → latitude, alternate names, seasonal shift

x: The
equatorial low-pressure belt
, also called the doldrums or ITCZ, is characterised by rising air, calm conditions and the convergence of trade winds.
The
subpolar low-pressure belt
, located approximately at 60°–65° in both hemispheres, is where westerlies meet polar easterlies and storms are common.
The equatorial low has calm rising air; the subtropical high has sinking dry air; the subpolar low is a meeting zone of westerlies and polar easterlies; and the polar high has cold sinking air.

secs.t: Planetary winds - trade winds, westerlies, polar easterlies

x: Westerlies flow from the subtropical high-pressure belt towards the subpolar low-pressure belt, generally between 35° and 60° latitudes.
The predominance of oceans and the relatively small amount of land friction in the Southern Hemisphere allow the westerlies to be stronger and steadier.
Trade winds and polar easterlies are directed towards low-pressure belts, while Southern Hemisphere westerlies have a north-westerly direction.

secs.t: ITCZ - location, seasonal migration, link to monsoon

x: The modern monsoon theory of 1957 considers the northward shift of the ITCZ together with jet streams, the Tibet Plateau and ENSO.
In winter, the ITCZ moves south of India and high-pressure cells develop over Tibet and Siberia, setting up the
north-east monsoon
The southward shift of the doldrums brings heavy rain to the southern states during the north-east monsoon and contributes to India’s bimodal rainfall pattern.

secs.t: Jet streams - subtropical westerly, tropical easterly, altitude, influence, polar vortex

x: Although first identified by Wasaburo Ooishi, jet streams became widely known during World War II through high-flying aircraft and bomber pilots.
The polar vortex is a year-round cold, low-pressure region, becomes strongest in winter and its anticlockwise circulation confines cold air near the poles.
Sudden stratospheric warming can weaken or split the polar vortex, allowing cold air to move southward and cause cold spells.
Halley proposed his theory in 1686, Ooishi identified jet streams in the 1920s, their wartime significance became widely known during World War II, and the modern monsoon theory dates to 1957.

secs.t: Wind controls - pressure gradient, isobars, Coriolis, friction, geostrophic wind, barometer

x: Coriolis force deflects winds right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere, is zero at the equator, maximum at the poles and increases with wind speed.
Ferrel’s law
states that winds are deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere due to Earth’s rotation.
A geostrophic wind is an upper-air wind blowing parallel to isobars when the pressure gradient force and Coriolis force are balanced and friction is negligible.

secs.t: Local winds and storms → region and effect

x: Foehn occurs in the Alps, while Chinook occurs in the Rockies; both are warm, dry descending winds capable of melting snow.
Sirocco originates in the Sahara and moves towards Italy or the Mediterranean; after picking up moisture, it may produce ‘blood rain’.
Leveche is associated with Spain, Brickfielder with south-east Australia, Blizzard with polar regions and North America, and Shamal with Iraq and the Persian Gulf.
Nor’westers or Kaal Baisakhi are violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms occurring mainly in
Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam

secs.t: Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Shrieking Sixties

x: In the Hadley cell, air rises near the Equator, moves poleward aloft, sinks near 30° and returns as trade winds.

secs.t: Periodic winds - land and sea breeze, mountain and valley breeze, monsoons

x: The nocturnal mountain or katabatic breeze carries cold air downhill, where it accumulates in valleys and may produce
temperature inversion and frost
Edmond Halley
explained the monsoon in 1686 as a land-and-sea breeze operating on a large scale.
The modern explanation connects monsoon circulation with the seasonal movement of the ITCZ, jet streams and heating of Tibet, in addition to land–sea thermal contrasts.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: the Subtropical Westerly Jet carries the disturbances eastward, and they were associated with intensified weather extremes and possible flash floods in Nepal and Tibet.
El Nino was expected to contribute to below-normal southwest monsoon rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, although short and intense low-pressure spells could partly offset the deficiency.

rows.title: Humidity, evaporation, condensation, clouds and forms of precipitation
sub: Group-II S2-11: Humidity, condensation, clouds and forms of precipitation

secs.t: Clouds → appearance and altitude class, rain-bearing clouds, cloud-seeding chemicals

x: Cirrostratus is a thin milky sheet that can produce a halo, while cirrocumulus consists of small globular masses or ripples.
Cirrocumulus
clouds form small globular masses or ripples commonly referred to as a mackerel sky.
Silver iodide
is used in cloud seeding because its crystal structure mimics that of ice and assists ice-crystal formation.
Silver iodide, dry ice and common salt may be used for cloud seeding, and silver iodide resembles ice crystallographically.

secs.t: Instruments and isolines → what they measure or join

x: When air is fully saturated, no further evaporative cooling occurs, so wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures are equal.
The Mauryan Arthashastra described a state rain gauge whose measurement was expressed in
drona
, approximately 13.2 kg of water.
The Mauryan Arthashastra description predates Korea’s Cheugugi of 1441, which in turn predates Castelli’s rain gauge of 1639.

secs.t: Precipitation types - convectional, orographic, cyclonic/frontal

x: Convectional precipitation develops when intense heating causes air to rise, cool and condense, commonly producing afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
Cyclonic or frontal precipitation occurs when warm air rises over cold air along fronts or when air rises in a cyclone’s low-pressure centre.
Equatorial and summer-interior afternoon showers are convectional, Western Ghats rainfall is orographic, and Bay of Bengal cyclones produce cyclonic precipitation.

secs.t: Hydrological cycle - processes that belong and those that do not; hydrometeorology

x: Evapotranspiration, sublimation and groundwater flow are components of the hydrological cycle.
Hydrometeorology studies
the transfer of water and energy between the land surface and the lower atmosphere
, including rainfall, floods and droughts.
India receives about 4,000 BCM of precipitation annually, of which approximately 1,139 BCM is utilisable, including 690 BCM of surface water and 449 BCM of groundwater.

secs.t: Optical phenomena - sun halo, rainbow

x: A sun halo is typically a ring of about 22° produced when sunlight is refracted through millions of hexagonal ice crystals in thin, high cirrostratus clouds.
A corona consists of coloured rings close to the Sun or Moon and is produced by
diffraction by small water droplets in thin clouds

secs.t: Rain shadow areas and relief-related precipitation terms

x: The eastern side of the Western Ghats is in the rain shadow and receives scanty rainfall.
The Sileru and Sabari valleys receive about 140–152 cm of rainfall owing to the southwest monsoon and the orographic effect of the Eastern Ghats.
Orographic lifting raises moist air over the Himalayas, encouraging the development of towering cumulonimbus clouds capable of producing cloudbursts.

secs.t: Forms of condensation and precipitation - dew, frost, fog, mist, smog, sleet, hail

x: Hail consists of layered ice balls developed within cumulonimbus clouds where strong updrafts repeatedly carry water and ice particles upward.
Clear and calm nights allow surfaces to cool efficiently, while high humidity and long cold nights favour dew or frost formation.
Silver iodide, potassium iodide, sodium chloride, dry ice and liquid propane are all listed as cloud-seeding substances or condensation nuclei.
Acid rain is mainly associated with
sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
, which contribute to the formation of acidic compounds in the atmosphere.

secs.t: Humidity and evaporation - absolute, specific, relative, dew point, saturation, latent heat

x: Absolute humidity is the actual amount of water vapour per unit volume of air, generally expressed in grams per cubic metre (g/m³).
Saturation occurs when relative humidity is
100 per cent
, meaning that the air contains the maximum moisture it can hold at that temperature.
Water vapour may constitute up to about 4 per cent by volume in warm, humid tropics, but remains below 1 per cent in deserts and polar areas.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Cloudbursts are associated with
cumulonimbus
clouds, which are vertically developed clouds capable of producing intense convective precipitation.
The 16th Finance Commission recommended the addition of
heatwaves and lightning
to the nationally notified disasters.
North Coastal Andhra Pradesh receives the highest rainfall, approximately 140–152 cm, due to the South-West monsoon and the orographic effect of the Eastern Ghats.

rows.title: Air masses and fronts - classification and associated weather

secs.t: Air masses - source regions and classification

x: An air mass is a very large body of air with nearly uniform horizontal temperature and humidity, acquired by remaining over a homogeneous source region.
Cold, dense cP and cA air masses build polar anticyclones, which are cold-core highs and strongest near the surface.
Polar anticyclones are associated with
clear skies, fog, frost and sharp night cooling

secs.t: Air mass modification and associated weather

x: Cold air moving over a warmer surface is heated from below, becomes unstable and promotes convection, cumulus clouds and showers.
Warm air is cooled from below over a colder surface, becomes stable and produces
fog, stratus and drizzle
The transport of warm air masses into the Arctic by a meandering jet stream drives
Arctic amplification

secs.t: Fronts - cold, warm, stationary, occluded

x: In a cold front, advancing cold air forms a steep wedge and lifts warm air sharply, producing cumulonimbus, heavy short showers, thunder, squalls and a sudden temperature fall.
A warm front has a gentle slope because warm air rides up over retreating cold air, producing a wide belt of layered cloud and prolonged light-to-moderate rain ahead of the front.

secs.t: Frontogenesis vs frontolysis

x: Frontolysis occurs when a front weakens and dissolves because temperature contrast is lost; frontogenesis involves formation or sharpening through convergence of contrasting air masses.

secs.t: Cloud and rain sequence at passage of a front

x: A warm front brings falling pressure and steady widespread rain, the warm sector brings warmer humid conditions with easing rain, and the cold front is followed by cold clear air.
Cumulonimbus, heavy showers, thunder and a wind shift
accompany the passage of a cold front, followed by cold clear air.

secs.t: Polar front theory - origin and proponents

x: The theory was put forward by
Vilhelm and Jacob Bjerknes of the Bergen School
in Norway around the end of World War I.
The theory states that temperate cyclones form along the polar front where cold polar air meets warm westerly air.
Western disturbances reach north-west India at the
occluded-front stage
of the temperate cyclone life cycle.

secs.t: Air masses affecting India - winter vs summer sources

x: The Himalayan barrier makes north India about
warmer than places on the same latitude during winter.
The winter anticyclonic cell produces
clear skies, light northerly winds, low humidity and a large daily temperature range
The south-west monsoon is produced by moist maritime air from the Indian Ocean, supplied by the low-level Somali Jet.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh experiences the dual influence of the south-west monsoon and the north-east monsoon, the latter involving winter air returning over the Bay of Bengal.
An Antarctic high extending unusually far north brought snow to Chile's Atacama Desert for the first time in over a decade.
A stalled high-pressure heat dome drove
a record early heatwave in Western Europe

rows.title: Atmospheric disturbances - tropical cyclones, temperate cyclones, anticyclones, thunderstorms, tornadoes
sub: Group-II S2-12: Cyclones - tropical and temperate; other atmospheric disturbances

secs.t: Tropical cyclones - formation, limits, structure, circulation, threshold

x: Tropical cyclones require a large warm ocean surface, generally with sea-surface temperature above about 26.5–27°C. Moisture and low wind shear are also favourable conditions.
Tropical cyclones do not normally form in the
South Atlantic and south-east Pacific
, where cool waters and strong vertical wind shear are unfavourable.
A super typhoon has sustained winds of about
240 km/h
, equivalent to approximately 150 mph.
The
eyewall
is the ring of towering cumulonimbus clouds surrounding the eye and contains the strongest winds and heaviest rain.
Landfall cuts the cyclone off from the warm ocean and its moisture supply, causing the system to lose energy and weaken.

secs.t: Recent cyclones → year, basin and coast hit

x: The 1999 Odisha Super Cyclone was a Bay of Bengal storm that struck
Odisha, including the Paradip region
Cyclone
Phailin
occurred in 2013 in the Bay of Bengal, affected Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, and led to the evacuation of over one million people.
Idai affected Mozambique in 2019; Shakti was an Arabian Sea cyclone named by Sri Lanka in 2025; and Ditwah was linked with Operation Sagar Bandhu in November 2025.

secs.t: Measurement scales

x: The Fujita and Enhanced Fujita scales classify tornadoes from EF0 to EF5 according to the
damage caused
Tornadoes are small, funnel-shaped and usually short-lived, while hurricanes may be hundreds of kilometres wide, last for days and form over warm oceans.
A super typhoon has sustained winds of about 240 km per hour and is comparable to a strong Category 4 or Category 5 storm.

secs.t: Temperate / extra-tropical cyclones

x: Temperate or extra-tropical cyclones develop
along the polar front in the middle and higher latitudes
Temperate cyclones possess a clear frontal system, including warm and cold fronts; an occluded front may also develop.
Western disturbances
bring winter rainfall of about 10–15 cm to north-western India, which is beneficial for rabi cultivation.

secs.t: Thunderstorms and local storms → region

x: Kaal Baisakhi or Nor'westers occur in
Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam
and approach from the north-west.
The lightning-monitoring system includes 104 lightning detection locations, while the Damini app issues alerts in 15 languages.
A cloudburst refers to roughly 100 mm of rainfall in an hour over 20–30 square kilometres, commonly affecting the Himalaya during June–August.

secs.t: Regional names of tropical cyclones

x: The term hurricane is used for tropical cyclones in the North Atlantic and north-east Pacific.
Baguio is a regional name used in the Philippines; the North Indian Ocean and South Pacific use the term cyclone.
Tornadoes are small, violent funnels generally associated with land, while hurricanes, typhoons and cyclones form over oceans.

secs.t: Bay of Bengal vs Arabian Sea

x: Higher sea-surface temperatures, the enclosed funnel-shaped basin and the regeneration of Pacific typhoon remnants favour cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.
Arabian Sea cyclones are rarer than Bay of Bengal cyclones, but recent storms such as Tauktae and Biparjoy illustrate their increasing intensity.
The coastline was remeasured as
, an increase of 47.7 per cent attributed to the finer 1:250,000 GIS scale.

secs.t: Anticyclones - pressure pattern and weather

x: An anticyclone has high pressure at the centre, with winds diverging outward from it.
Anticyclonic winds move clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and anticlockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
Sinking and diverging air in a high-pressure system generally produces clear, dry, calm and settled weather.

secs.t: Cyclone naming, IMD scale, warning colours

x: The
World Meteorological Organization
divided the oceans into basins; cyclone naming is carried out through six RSMCs and five TCWCs.
Depression corresponds to 31–49 km/h, Deep Depression to 50–61 km/h, Very Severe Cyclonic Storm to 118–166 km/h and Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm to 167–221 km/h.
The Indian cyclone warning colour codes are green—no warning, yellow—be aware, orange—be prepared and red—
take action

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The low over the Andaman Sea around 19–21 September 2026 was expected to become the first cyclone of that South-West monsoon season and head towards the Odisha coast.

All four statements describe the cited Cyclone Montha response: 15 deaths, automated evacuations through RTGS AWARE 2.0, 423 drones, alerts to 3.60 crore people and ₹341.48 crore of additional NDRF aid.

rows.title: Elements and factors of climate; world climatic classification (Koeppen)
sub: Group-II S2-13: World climatic types and elements and factors of climate

secs.t: World climatic regions and biomes → location and vegetation

x: The
equatorial
region, including the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, has dense evergreen hardwood forests and almost daily rainfall.
Tropical monsoon forests in India and South-East Asia include
teak and sal
; the trees shed their leaves during the dry season.
Temperate deciduous forests contain trees such as
oak
, beech, maple and birch, which shed their leaves in autumn.
Taiga or boreal forests of northern North America and Eurasia are dominated by
evergreen conifers such as spruce, fir and pine
The tree line is the altitude or latitude beyond which
trees cannot grow
; alpine tundra lies above it.
China type has summer rain, British type has year-round rain from westerlies, hot deserts receive under 25 cm of rain, and equatorial regions are hot and wet throughout the year.
Tropical rainforests occur in the equatorial belt, receive about 50–260 inches of rain, and have dense canopies, epiphytes and lianas.
Tundra occurs mainly along Arctic coasts and above the tree line in high mountains, not in central tropical Brazil or the Congo Basin.
Tundra supports mosses, lichens and bearberry; taiga has evergreen conifers; savanna has grasses with scattered trees; deserts support xerophytes.

secs.t: Grasslands → continent/country

x: Exam angle: "Prairies are found in" - USA
and
Canada (not USA alone, not Mexico).
Llanos
is a tropical grassland of the Orinoco basin, whereas Pampas, Steppes and Veld are temperate grasslands.
Temperate grasslands have hot summers, chilly winters, annual rainfall of about 25–50 cm, and grasses with few trees.
Savanna vegetation includes tall grasses such as elephant and guinea grass, along with baobab and acacia; it is naturally prone to fire.
All four pairs are correct: Steppes are Eurasian, Pampas occur in Argentina and Uruguay, Veld is associated with South Africa, and Downs occur in Australia.

secs.t: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

x: Exam angle: "Distance from river" is
not
a control of climate.
The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
The Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and help retain the monsoon winds, thereby influencing the climate of northern India.
Relief causes windward rainfall and leeward rain-shadow conditions, while the Himalayas moderate winter temperatures in northern India.
Cold currents cool and dry adjacent coasts, particularly on the western margins of tropical continents.
Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones
are atmospheric circulation features associated with winds and pressure systems.

secs.t: Climatic extremes and limits

x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
Hot deserts commonly occur between
15° and 30° north and south
, especially on the western margins of continents.
Subtropical high pressure, offshore trade winds and cold currents
reduce moisture and favour hot-desert formation in this belt.

secs.t: Peoples → natural region

x: Bedouins are traditionally nomadic people of the hot deserts of Arabia and the Sahara.
The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are associated with the grasslands and steppes of Central Asia.
The Yakuts are associated with Siberia and the taiga or Arctic environment.
The Tuareg are traditionally associated with the Sahara and its hot desert environment.

secs.t: Mediterranean climate

x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
Koeppen’s As climate, characterised by dry summers and winter rainfall, occurs on the
Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu
Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with
citrus fruits, grapes and wine
production.

secs.t: Identifying a climate type from a description

x: Hot wet summers and long dry winters are characteristic of savanna or monsoon climatic conditions.
Extreme heat, a large diurnal temperature range and rainfall below 25 cm indicate a
hot desert
climate.
The taiga climate has a long severe winter, a short cool summer and a very large annual temperature range.

secs.t: Koeppen classification and Thornthwaite basis

x: Exam angle: match-the-following of code, name and area (APPSC-G1 2024: Amw-west coast, As-Coromandel, Cwg-Ganga plain, BShw-NW India).
Wladimir Koeppen
proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
In Koeppen's scheme, A denotes tropical humid, B dry, C warm temperate, D cold snow-forest and E polar climates.
In the notation, 'w' indicates dry winter. 'm' denotes monsoon, 's' dry summer and 'f' no dry season.
Amw occurs on the west coast south of Goa, As on the Coromandel coast, BWhw in extreme western Rajasthan and Dfc in Arunachal Pradesh.
Aw denotes tropical savanna and covers most of the Peninsular Plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer.

secs.t: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
The IMD normal rainfall for June–September, based on the 1971–2020 base period, is
The 868.6 mm normal is the long-period average rainfall for the June–September southwest monsoon season.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
The projection concerns about 40 coastal districts warming by more than 1°C by 2040, while Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are expected to receive excess southwest-monsoon rain.
Araku, Lambasingi and Horsley Hills
are cited as examples of hill micro-climates in Andhra Pradesh.
The APSES 2024–25 table lists the six agro-climatic zones against
the 13 pre-2022 districts

rows.title: Climate change - evidence, natural and anthropogenic causes, global warming, IPCC assessments, impacts

secs.t: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5

x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with
Al Gore
The SR1.5 assessment indicated that global CO₂ emissions need to decline by about
from 2010 levels by 2030.
Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.

secs.t: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice

x: Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately
etres since 1935, with global warming identified as the cause of its melting.
All four statements describe the reported indicators: sea-level rise of about 11 cm, near-record-low Arctic sea ice, third-lowest Antarctic sea ice and a 65-year peak in energy imbalance.
The stated current-affairs fact is that
2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record

secs.t: Impacts

x: The uninhabited South Pacific islets
Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea
were reported to have been submerged in 1999.
The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and coral reefs require more than 15 years to recover.
Warmer and wetter conditions can expand the range of vectors and thereby increase the spread of diseases such as malaria and dengue.

secs.t: Climate science recognition and major reports

x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 estimates approximately
of warming under current policies.
All three statements are correct: the stated reductions are 35% for the 2°C pathway and 55% for the 1.5°C pathway, while a 1.5°C overshoot is considered very likely this decade.
The report described
climate indicators
as “flashing red,” signalling worsening climate conditions.

secs.t: Natural causes

x: Milankovitch cycles comprise changes in eccentricity, obliquity and precession, which help drive ice-age cycles.
The evidence indicates no net increase, not a continuous decline, in solar output since 1978.
Volcanic activity, continental drift and ocean currents are natural climate influences.
Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.

secs.t: Geoengineering proposals

x: In this proposal, sulphur dioxide forms sulphuric-acid aerosols that reflect sunlight, imitating the cooling effect of volcanic eruptions.
Cirrus cloud thinning seeks to reduce the insulating effect of high cirrus clouds and allow more outgoing heat to escape.
The cited study suggested that marine cloud brightening could weaken
a Super El Nino

secs.t: Universal angles

x: COP31 is scheduled to meet in
Türkiye in November 2026
The CMIP7 scenarios drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 pathway and place projected warming near 2.8°C by 2100.
Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are identified in connection with heatwaves.
Coastal erosion
at Uppada near Kakinada is identified as an Andhra Pradesh climate-related concern.
APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under
SDG 13

rows.title: Oceans - relief of the ocean floor, continental shelf, ridges, trenches
sub: Group-II S2-14: Ocean water - temperature and salinity; relief of the ocean floor

secs.t: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

x: Oceanic deeps or trenches are long, narrow and steep-sided, commonly occur at plate-convergence zones, and are associated with volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
The deep sea below 200 metres is described as the
oldest and largest biome
, occupying about 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.

The continental shelf is rich in fisheries and hydrocarbons; the slope has canyons and trenches; the deep-sea plain is the flattest surface; and oceanic deeps are associated with volcanoes and earthquakes.

secs.t: Depth mapping methods and units

x: Echo sounding measures the time taken by a sound pulse to travel to the sea floor and return; depth equals speed multiplied by half the round-trip time.
The sensors fitted to sharks were used to collect ocean data relevant to
hurricane forecasting
Lanternfishes and deep-sea shrimps
are characteristic organisms of the mesopelagic zone, which also contributes to the biological carbon pump.

secs.t: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

x: Terrigenous deposits are derived from land and are deposited mainly on continental shelves and slopes.
Calcareous ooze consists mainly of the lime shells of tiny organisms, including globigerina and pteropods.
Siliceous ooze is formed from the silica skeletons of organisms such as
diatoms and radiolarians
and is common in colder or deeper waters.

secs.t: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

x: Oceans cover about 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface, contain about 97 per cent of its water, and form the largest component of the hydrosphere.
About 2 per cent of Earth's water is represented as ice and about 1 per cent as usable fresh water in the stated broad division.
Groundwater far exceeds the amount of fresh water stored in lakes and rivers.

secs.t: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

x: A seamount is an undersea volcanic mountain whose summit does not reach the ocean surface.
A submarine canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley that cuts across the continental shelf and slope, often near river mouths.
All three statements are correct: the surveys covered about 25 seamounts, identified about 39 potentially new species, and found two active and two inactive hydrothermal vents.

secs.t: Trenches → ocean, deepest point of each ocean

x: Oceanic trenches commonly occur at subduction zones, where one plate descends beneath another.
The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean.
The Challenger Deep lies in the
Mariana Trench
in the Pacific Ocean and is about 11 km deep.
Both the Tonga and Kermadec trenches occur in the south-western Pacific Ocean.

secs.t: Ridges and plateaus → ocean

x: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is S-shaped, and Iceland and the Azores rise above parts of it.
The Telegraph Plateau lies south of Iceland in the North Atlantic and was used as a route for transatlantic cables.
India applied for the Afanasy-Nikitin Seamount, and its polymetallic sulphide licence on the Indian Ocean Ridge is valid up to September 2031.

secs.t: Continental shelf width - east vs west coast of India

x: Mumbai High lies on
the wide western continental shelf
, particularly in the Gujarat-Mumbai sector.
The Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976 vests minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ in the
Union
In 2025, India added about 10,000 square kilometres in the central Arabian Sea to its extended-shelf claim before the UN CLCS.

secs.t: Salinity - factors, average salinity, water bodies → salinity ranking (Lake Van, Dead Sea, Great Salt Lake, Red Sea, Baltic)

x: Exam angle: the APPSC G2 2023 key is
Lake Van > Dead Sea > Great Salt Lake
(NCERT figures).
Currents and winds
redistribute salinity, whereas evaporation, freezing, precipitation, river inflow and ice melt directly alter the salt concentration.
The Red Sea is among the saltiest seas, the Mediterranean has salinity of about 37–39 per mille, and the Baltic Sea is among the least saline water bodies.

secs.t: Temperature of ocean water - horizontal and vertical distribution, thermocline, western vs eastern tropical ocean

x: At higher latitudes, the usual tropical west–east temperature contrast is reversed, a pattern associated with the
North Atlantic Drift
Trade winds push and pile warm surface water towards the western sides of tropical oceans, making them warmer than the eastern sides.
In tropical oceans, the warm surface layer is about 500 m thick and has temperatures of roughly 20–25°C; the thermocline extends from about 500–1,000 m, below which the deep water is near 0°C.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India widened its claim by 10,000 sq km in the central Arabian Sea before the relevant UN Commission, using data from NCPOR, Goa.
The
Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology
(CMLRE) released the first National Report on Deep-Sea and Distant-Water Fishery Resources of the EEZ.
Indian scientists reached 5,002 m in an Atlantic dive, while the Varaha mining machine was trialled at 5,270 m in the Central Indian Ocean.

rows.title: Physical and chemical characteristics of ocean water - temperature and salinity distribution

secs.t: Salinity - controlling factors, source, unit, averages

x: The average salinity of ocean water is about
35 per mille
, equivalent to approximately 35 grams of dissolved salts per kilogram of water.
Ocean salts are supplied by weathered materials transported by rivers and by volcanic and hydrothermal emissions from the sea floor.
Evaporation and freezing concentrate salts, melting dilutes seawater, and currents and winds redistribute saline water.

secs.t: Distribution of earth's water

x: The descending order is oceans, polar ice caps and glaciers, groundwater, and rivers and streams.
Approximately
97 percent
of the Earth's water is stored in the oceans.
Rivers and streams
constitute the smallest share among the listed major water stores.

secs.t: Clines → gradient each denotes

x: A pycnocline is a zone of rapid change in water density.
Clines mark sharp vertical changes and impede the vertical mixing of water.
The Black Sea is a meromictic basin in which upper and lower layers rarely mix, and chemical differences such as oxygen and hydrogen sulphide are important.

secs.t: Dissolved salts - major constituents

x: Sodium chloride
accounts for approximately 77.8 percent of the dissolved salts in seawater.
By ions, chloride and sodium are the dominant constituents of seawater, followed by sulphate and magnesium.

secs.t: Horizontal salinity distribution

x: Subtropical regions generally have high evaporation and low rainfall, resulting in relatively high surface salinity.
Heavy equatorial rainfall lowers salinity near the equator, while melting ice and low evaporation lower salinity near the poles.
The Arabian Sea is saltier than the Bay of Bengal, where the discharge of the Ganga and Brahmaputra supplies substantial fresh water.

secs.t: Density of ocean water - factors

x: Temperature, salinity and pressure influence density, and density differences cause sinking and rising movements of water.
Cold polar water is denser and sinks; the resulting density-driven movement contributes to ocean currents and carries water towards the equator.
Warm currents generally move poleward from the equator, while cold currents carry polar water equatorward.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The OMNI deep-sea buoys record temperature, salinity and ocean currents in real time for cyclone and Indian Ocean Dipole forecasting.
NIOT's Nellore seafront facility tests deep-sea mining and LTTD desalination equipment, and its station has also started new deep-sea buoys.
NIOT operationalised an OMNI deep-sea buoy station at
Nellore
, measuring temperature, salinity and currents in real time.

rows.title: Ocean movements - waves, tides (types and causes), ocean currents of the world
sub: Group-II S2-15: Ocean movements - tides, waves and currents; El Nino and La Nina

secs.t: Ocean currents - warm or cold, and ocean (odd-one-out)

x: Exam angle: "which is not a warm/cold current", "which does not flow in the N. Atlantic", current-ocean matching.
Exam angle: "Which is NOT warm/cold?" questions.
Humboldt
is the odd one out among Agulhas, Brazil and Kuroshio.
Agulhas and Brazil
are the non-cold pair.
Solar heating, wind, gravity, the Coriolis force and density differences all influence ocean currents.
Mozambique is a warm Indian Ocean current; Falkland is a cold South Atlantic current; Oyashio and California are cold North Pacific currents.

secs.t: Indian Ocean currents - seasonal monsoon reversal, WICC

x: However, the association and seasonal reversal of the Findlater Current describe its behaviour; they do not by themselves constitute the direct explanation that coastal winds produce upwelling off the Horn of Africa.
During the southwest monsoon, the Findlater Current creates coastal upwelling off the Horn of Africa, producing favourable fishing conditions.
North Indian Ocean currents reverse with the monsoon winds, unlike the generally steady gyres of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

secs.t: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites

x: The bulge on the side facing the Moon is the direct tide, produced mainly by lunar gravitational attraction.
A storm surge is an irregular, weather-driven rise of sea level caused by winds and pressure changes.
Semi-diurnal tides have two highs and two lows; diurnal tides have one high and one low; mixed tides are unequal in height; spring tides have the highest range.
Perigean tides occur when the Moon is
closest to the Earth
, thereby increasing its gravitational tidal influence.
Tidal energy is harnessed through tidal-range systems, such as barrages across estuaries, and tidal-stream systems using underwater turbines.

secs.t: Sargasso Sea and gyres

x: In the Northern Hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects moving water to the
right
, contributing to clockwise gyre circulation.
The Sargasso Sea is bounded by the
North Atlantic Drift
in the north, the Gulf Stream in the west, the Canary Current in the east and the North Equatorial Current in the south.

secs.t: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog

x: The Atacama is associated with the Humboldt Current, Namib and Kalahari with the Benguela Current, Sonoran with the California Current, and Peru's fishery with Humboldt-related upwelling.
The
North Atlantic Drift
, an extension of the Gulf Stream, carries warm water towards north-western Europe and helps keep its coasts mild and ports ice-free in winter.

secs.t: Current-forming factors - winds, Coriolis, density, counter-current

x: Trade winds
push surface water westward and drive the equatorial currents.
Solar heating expands equatorial water and creates a slight surface slope.
Cold water sinks at the poles and moves slowly towards the equator.
The Equatorial Counter Current flows west to east between the North and South Equatorial Currents.

secs.t: Waves - parts, swell, breakers

x: Kallakkadal is a swell surge produced by long-period swells generated by storms in the southern Indian Ocean.
Kallakkadal involves 30–300-second swells generated by storms about 10,000 km away in the southern Indian Ocean and is most frequent during the pre-monsoon period.
A rip current is a narrow and fast-moving channel of water flowing away from the shore.

secs.t: ENSO - El Nino and La Nina definitions, Pacific region warmed/cooled, periodicity, Southern Oscillation, effect on Indian monsoon

x: Exam angle: "El Nino and La Nina are storms" is the false statement. They are climate patterns.
El Nino and La Nina describe the oceanic component of ENSO, while the Southern Oscillation describes its atmospheric pressure component.

Weaker easterlies allow warm western-Pacific water to move eastward; this further weakens the trades, disrupts Walker circulation and contributes to sinking air and high pressure over the Indian Ocean.
El Nino requires warming of at least 0.5°C for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods, while La Nina represents a half-degree cooling.

secs.t: Coastal hazard forecasting - Indian institutions → early-warning systems (tsunami, high waves, coastal risk)

x: ITEWS includes seismic networks, deep-ocean pressure recorders, coastal tide gauges, satellite communication and a Decision Support System;
mountain snow gauges
are not listed as a component.
INCOIS provides ocean forecasts and PFZ advisories, IMD issues cyclone and multi-hazard warnings, NIOT operates OMNI buoys, and ITEWS serves as the regional tsunami provider.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The satellite tracked an eastward Kelvin wave, meaning warm water moving east along the equatorial Pacific, an early El Nino signal.
An INCOIS study found that
El Nino may reduce post-monsoon cyclones in the Bay of Bengal during October–December
; the statement does not imply that all cyclones are eliminated.
The events occurred in the order: Kelvin-wave tracking on 4 June 2026, Kollam monitoring installation on 14 May 2026, the May 4 monsoon warning, and the July 7 cyclone study.

rows.title: Ocean-atmosphere interaction - El Nino, La Nina, ENSO, Indian Ocean Dipole, Walker circulation

secs.t: El Nino - where the SST anomaly forms, Peru current, recurrence, impacts

x: Exam angle: El Nino is a climate pattern,
not a storm
; statement sets on Peru warm current, 3-7-year recurrence and meaning of the name.
When nutrient-rich upwelling stops,
phytoplankton
decline and the marine food chain and fish catch are affected.
A weak monsoon during El Nino can reduce summer-crop yields, particularly
rice and sugarcane
, and contribute to food inflation.

secs.t: La Nina - conditions, contrast, regional impacts

x: La Nina is the cold phase of ENSO; stronger trade winds push warm water westward and enhance cold upwelling in the eastern Pacific.
La Nina is associated with
more floods and severe cyclones
in the Bay of Bengal, while El Nino is linked with fewer post-monsoon cyclones.
The material identifies 2025 as
the warmest La Nina year on record
, unusual because La Nina normally cools global temperature.

secs.t: Indian Ocean Dipole - positive vs negative phase

x: The IOD can develop independently of ENSO; a positive IOD may offset the effects of El Nino, as observed in 1997.
A positive IOD can enhance rainfall over India and partly offset the drought-inducing effect of
El Nino
The strong positive IOD in 1997 helped save India from drought even though a Super El Nino was present.

secs.t: Modoki El Nino vs normal El Nino

x: Canonical El Nino has its maximum warming in the eastern Pacific near Peru.
El Nino Modoki has central Pacific warming flanked by cooler waters on both the eastern and western sides, forming a tripole pattern.
The Japanese term Modoki means ‘
similar but different
’, reflecting its resemblance to but distinction from normal El Nino.

secs.t: Madden-Julian Oscillation

x: The MJO is an eastward-moving pulse of clouds, convection and rain that begins as a warm pool in the tropical Indian Ocean.
The MJO convection rises up to 10 km, weakens in the eastern Pacific while continuing aloft around the globe, and shifts the heavy-rain zone eastward.
By shifting the zone of heavy rain eastward, the MJO contributes to
active and break spells of the monsoon

secs.t: Walker circulation - normal vs El Nino

x: Normal Walker circulation has rising air over the warm western Pacific and Indonesia, sinking air over the cool eastern Pacific, and easterly trade winds at the surface.
El Nino weakens the Walker circulation and shifts it eastward, reducing convection over India.
La Nina strengthens the Walker circulation and is linked with unusual cold over East, Central and South India.

secs.t: ENSO monitoring - Nino 3.4, IMD/NOAA declarations

x: The Nino 3.4 region lies in the central equatorial Pacific between 5°N and 5°S and 120°W and 170°W.
The
Indian Ocean Dipole
is monitored through the Dipole Mode Index, or DMI.
The DMI value of –0.34°C in late May 2026 was assessed as neutral for the Indian Ocean Dipole.
NASA's Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich
tracks Kelvin waves, which can provide an early signal of El Nino development.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The IMD forecast projected a below-normal monsoon at 92% of the Long Period Average, whose reference value was stated as 87 cm.
The INCOIS study found that ENSO governs the number of post-monsoon, or October–December, cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.
Walker first described the Southern Oscillation in the 1920s, the Indian Ocean Dipole was identified in 1999, and the last El Nino mentioned was in 2023–24.

rows.title: Biological characteristics of oceans - marine ecosystems, coral reefs, bleaching, upwelling zones

secs.t: Coral reefs - types, growth conditions, composition, roles and epithets

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2024 paired "rainforests of the sea" with "breaks wave power" - both true but the second does not explain the first.
A fringing reef grows close to the shore, a barrier reef is separated from the coast by a lagoon, and an atoll encloses a central lagoon.
During bleaching,
stressed corals expel their symbiotic algae
, zooxanthellae, causing the corals to lose their colour.
Warm, clear, shallow and sunlit water with normal salinity and low sediment load provides suitable conditions for coral growth.

secs.t: Marine vs non-marine ecosystems

x: Marine ecosystems cover about
71 per cent
of the Earth’s surface.
Marine ecosystems hold approximately
97 per cent
of the Earth’s water.
Hydrothermal vent
s are marine ecosystems that support chemosynthetic life, unlike rivers and freshwater lakes.
Estuaries, salt marshes, mangroves and kelp forests are all marine or coastal marine ecosystems.

secs.t: Ocean zones - photic, aphotic, benthic, pelagic, neritic

x: The neritic zone extends from the high-water line across the continental shelf to about
200 metres depth
The neritic zone overlies the continental shelf, while the oceanic zone refers to the open ocean beyond the shelf.
The photic zone is the sunlit upper layer, approximately the top 200 metres, where photosynthesis occurs.

secs.t: Coral bleaching - symbiont, triggers, events

x: Pollution and runoff, disease, extremely low tides and crown-of-thorns starfish are all listed triggers of coral bleaching.
The fourth global bleaching event began in 2023, ended around mid-2025, and was the fastest and most extensive, affecting 84 per cent of reef areas in 83 countries.
Bleaching was reported in February 2025 in the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Gulf of Kachchh.

secs.t: Marine protected areas - coverage and targets

x: Aichi Target 11 set the goal of protecting
10 per cent
of coastal and marine areas by 2020.
The 30x30 target seeks protection of 30 per cent of land and 30 per cent of oceans by 2030.
Marine protected areas, no-fishing zones and sanctuaries reduce pressures on reefs and help them recover.

secs.t: Coral reef areas in India and the world

x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off north-eastern Australia, is about 2,300 km long, includes approximately 3,000 reefs and 900 islands, and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981.
Indian reef regions include the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Andaman and Nicobar, Lakshadweep and Malvan; the Andaman and Nicobar region has the highest diversity among them.

secs.t: Ocean acidification, algal blooms, red tides

x: Ocean acidification reduces carbonate ions, creating difficulty for calcifying organisms such as corals, plankton and shellfish in forming calcium carbonate structures.
Excess nitrogen and phosphorus from farm runoff and sewage cause eutrophication, which can produce harmful algal blooms.
Farm and sewage nutrients can cause algal blooms whose decomposition depletes oxygen, producing dead zones such as those associated with the Gulf of Mexico and Chesapeake Bay.

secs.t: Upwelling zones - coast, productivity and fisheries

x: Coastal upwelling occurs when winds drive surface water away from the coast, allowing cold, nutrient-rich subsurface water to rise.
Peru–Chile is associated with the Humboldt Current, California with the California Current, Namibia with the Benguela Current, and Somalia with the Findlater Current and southwest monsoon.
El Niño suppresses the Peru upwelling system, reducing phytoplankton abundance and thereby contributing to fishery collapse.

secs.t: Plankton - primary producers and oxygen

x: Phytoplankton, including diatoms, dinoflagellates and cyanobacteria, constitute the main primary producers of the ocean.
Diatoms, dinoflagellates and cyanobacteria are phytoplankton, and together phytoplankton form the principal primary-producer base of the ocean.
Oceans, chiefly through phytoplankton, produce about 50% or more of Earth’s oxygen, which is more than the combined contribution attributed to all rainforests.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A giant Pavona clavus, or potato patch coral, colony was reported near Kadmat Island in Lakshadweep.
The NGT clearance directed the Environment Ministry to protect and regenerate coral reefs; coral loss remained a central objection to the project.
The GCRMN 7th Status of the World's Coral Reefs report recorded a
decline in hard coral cover compared with the 1980–2009 period.

rows.title: Hydrological disasters - floods, flash floods, cloudbursts, droughts, tsunamis, storm surges
sub: Group-II S2-26: Natural hazards and disasters - classification and causes

secs.t: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event

x: Tsunamis may result from tectonic earthquakes, submarine landslides, volcanic eruptions and large asteroid or meteorite impacts.
As a tsunami enters shallow coastal water, its speed decreases and its wave height rises sharply, producing severe inundation.
Most tsunamis affecting India originate in the Indian Ocean, particularly from the Sunda-Andaman subduction zone; the Makran zone poses a threat to India’s west coast.

Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the very-high-risk zone; Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha are in the high-risk zone; Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat are in the moderate-risk zone.

secs.t: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees

x: Ordinary floods are generally slow-onset and often predictable in terms of region and season, unlike the sudden nature of flash floods.
Heavy rainfall, poor drainage, low infiltration, deforestation, dam failure and siltation from soil erosion are all recognised causes of floods.
Flooding in the Krishna-Godavari region can be especially severe when
Srisailam, Nagarjuna Sagar and Hirakud
release water together.
GLOF stands for
Glacial Lake Outburst Flood
, a sudden flood caused by the bursting of a glacial or proglacial lake.
Glacier retreat can enlarge proglacial lakes; when the lake bursts, the stored water produces a glacial lake outburst flood.
An ISRO study attributed the Dharali flash flood to the collapse of an ice patch on the
Srikanta Glacier

secs.t: Droughts - types, triggers, long-term consequences

x: Hydrological drought
is indicated by the fall of surface-water and groundwater resources such as rivers, reservoirs and aquifers.
Irregular or delayed monsoon, monsoon breaks, El Nino, and high temperature with enhanced evaporation are all drought triggers.
Droughts generally reduce farm output; they contribute to groundwater depletion, land degradation, desertification and distress migration.
Rayalaseema faces monsoon failure, crop losses, distress migration and severe groundwater depletion, aggravated by deep borewells.

secs.t: Coastal hazards - storm surges, tsunami-prone areas, coastline, mangroves

x: A storm surge is an abnormal rise in sea level caused mainly by cyclone winds and low atmospheric pressure.
Sea-level rise magnifies storm-surge impacts and may result in permanent inundation of low-lying land.
Mangroves and shelter belts anchor sediment and buffer storm surges, while dune stabilisation and seawalls strengthen coastal defence.

secs.t: Worst disasters in history - country
Disaster displacement - IDMC data, India's rank

x: The
Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre
, headquartered in Geneva, publishes the annual Global Report on Internal Displacement.
India lost approximately
of its GDP annually to natural disasters during 1990–2024.
More than 4,000 deaths were reported in India from climate-induced disasters in 2025, with the heaviest toll in
Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
Water-related disasters worldwide displaced approximately
8 million
people in 2025 and caused about 5,000 deaths.

secs.t: Cloudbursts - definition, Himalayan events

x: Dharali and Harsil in Uttarkashi experienced flash floods in 2025, which diverted the Bhagirathi.
The flash floods at Dharali and Harsil in Uttarkashi diverted the
Bhagirathi
River.
The HKH monsoon paradox refers to declining or erratic seasonal rainfall occurring alongside an increase in short, intense cloudbursts.
Cloudbursts in Andhra Pradesh's Eastern Ghats agency areas can rapidly generate flash floods in narrow valleys.

secs.t: Urban flooding - causes and cases

x: Urban flooding is associated with unplanned concretisation, blocked natural drains and canals, encroached lakes and extreme rainfall.
The City Flood Alert initiative involves RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar, provides 48-hour rain and six-hour flash-flood warnings, and began with Vijayawada.
The AI City Flood Alert platform was developed in association with the
Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
(APSDMA).

secs.t: Industrial and nuclear disasters - place, year, agent

x: Bhopal involved methyl isocyanate; Chernobyl involved the explosion of Reactor No. 4; Fukushima followed an earthquake and tsunami; improper disposal of radioactive waste is a separate nuclear hazard.
The HSDPR scheme provides for setting up
two tertiary and ten secondary CBRN medical management centres
during 2021–26.
The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli, Andhra Pradesh, prepares safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters.

secs.t: Vulnerability profile of India - hazard-prone states and area shares

x: Approximately
of the old 7,516.6 km coastline was considered exposed to cyclones and tsunamis.
The coastline was remeasured to 11,098.81 km by the Ministry of Home Affairs in December 2024.
Assam has approximately
31.05 lakh hectares
of flood-prone area.
The World Risk Index 2025 places India as the second most vulnerable country, after
the Philippines

secs.t: Landslides and avalanches - terrain, zones, rising frequency

x: Major landslide zones include the Himalaya, covering Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and the Northeast, and the Western Ghats, including Kerala, Konkan and the Nilgiris.
Unregulated construction on unstable slopes
is one of the factors increasing landslide frequency.
These figures are associated with road widening connected with the Char Dham project and its ecological and slope-stability concerns.

secs.t: Major disasters in India - year and place; hazard → region

x: The correct sequence is Latur earthquake in 1993, Odisha super cyclone in 1999, Bhuj earthquake in 2001 and Indian Ocean tsunami in 2004.
Cyclones are especially associated with the east coast, while drought is prominent in Rajasthan and the Deccan interior.
Tamil Nadu and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
were the worst-hit Indian locations during the Indian Ocean Tsunami of 26 December 2004.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh presents a three-way hazard pattern: coastal cyclones and storm surges, floods in the deltas and drought in Rayalaseema.
The stated figures are a 1,053.07 km coastline, third rank in India after the 2024 remeasurement and more than 62 cyclonic events in four decades.
Heat wave and lightning were listed as notified disasters, while Andhra Pradesh released Rs 479.01 crore under SDRF/NDRF and allotted Rs 521.17 crore under SDMF/NDMF in the stated period.

rows.title: Disaster management framework - hazard vs disaster, DM Act 2005, NDMA, early warning systems
sub: Group-II S2-27: Disaster management - DM Act 2005, NDMA, NDRF, mitigation and preparedness

secs.t: DM Act 2005 - NDMA, SDMA, DDMA, NIDM, NDRF: sections, chairs, ministry

x: NIDM is responsible for
training, research and capacity building in disaster management
The Act promoted a proactive approach centred on
prevention, mitigation and preparedness
instead of only relief after a disaster.
The NDRF 10th Battalion and the NIDM southern campus are near Vijayawada/Gannavaram; the southern campus is at Kondapalli.
The 2025 amendment provides for Urban Disaster Management Authorities in
every Municipal Corporation city except Delhi and Chandigarh
All four listed measures are features of the 2025 amendment, including disaster databases, statutory NCMC status, mandatory SDRF and stronger NDMA powers.
The sequence is NCDM in 1995, the Disaster Management Act in 2005, NDRF in 2006 and the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre in 2007.
The Disaster Management Act, 2005 reflected a shift from relief-centric administration towards
prevention, mitigation and preparedness
Section 2(d) focuses on a catastrophe causing substantial loss that exceeds the coping capacity of the
affected community
NDMA is headed by the Prime Minister, NEC by the Union Home Secretary, SDMA by the Chief Minister, and DDMA by the District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson.
The notified list includes lightning, pest attack and fire, but no man-made calamity is included in the stated list.

secs.t: Safety drills and awareness - safest actions, mock exercises, education

x: People should move to a safer shelter or cyclone shelter and should not go to sea, stand under trees or remain in weak houses.
Mock drills, Aapda Mitra volunteers and tsunami escape-route signage are preparedness tools; entering flowing floodwater is unsafe and is not a preparedness measure.
Mock exercises allow communities and institutions to practise evacuation and response procedures, thereby strengthening preparedness.

secs.t: Disaster management cycle - pre, during, post

x: Hazard mapping supports prevention or mitigation; search and rescue is a response activity; livelihood restoration is part of recovery; and Building Back Better incorporates post-disaster risk reduction.
During an earthquake, a person indoors should take shelter under a strong table and remain away from windows and balconies.
Mitigation includes embankments, mangroves and zoning; preparedness includes plans, warnings and drills; response includes rescue and relief; recovery includes restoration and rebuilding.

secs.t: Early warning systems - agency and location

x: The
India Meteorological Department
, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, issues warnings for cyclones, heavy rain, heat and lightning.
The
Geological Survey of India
is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility mapping and the Landslide Atlas.
The 24-hour cyclone track error declined from
93 km to 74 km

secs.t: Policy and institutional milestones

x: The four priorities are understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in disaster risk reduction, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and to Build Back Better.
The Sendai Framework sets the goal of universal access to multi-hazard early warning by 2030.
In the 1990s, a Disaster Management Cell was established under the
Ministry of Agriculture
in response to the UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
The 2009 policy emphasised prevention, mitigation, community participation and mainstreaming disaster risk reduction.

secs.t: Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation

x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.
Hazard-zonation maps are probabilistic; they do not guarantee that a disaster will occur at a particular location.
GSI’s Bhukosh portal hosts landslide-susceptibility maps covering about
4.3 lakh square kilometres
The maps are mirrored to the NDMA GIS portal through web map services.
CAP is used to integrate and disseminate public warnings through compatible alerting systems.
The Damini App provides lightning alerts.
The Lightning Detection System covers 104 locations.
INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR provide satellite-based support for cyclone tracking.

secs.t: Hazard vs disaster vs vulnerability vs risk

x: A disaster results when a hazard meets a vulnerable population; this relationship is expressed as
Hazard × Vulnerability = Disaster
Risk increases with hazard, exposure and vulnerability, while stronger
coping capacity
reduces it.
An earthquake in an empty desert represents a potentially damaging hazard, but without exposed vulnerability and resulting damage it need not be classified as a disaster.

secs.t: APSDMA - statutory functions and cyclone cases

x: Cyclone risk reduction measures include IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangrove protection or restoration.
Early warning, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves
are important cyclone-risk reduction measures.
APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates district authorities, operates early warning systems, and covers both pre-disaster planning and post-disaster restoration.

secs.t: NDRF - battalions, mock exercises, named exercises

x: NDRF is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces, with search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads, functioning under the superintendence of NDMA.
SDRFs have not yet been established in all states, increasing pressure on the NDRF when several disasters occur simultaneously.
The suggested measures are mandatory SDRFs and joint NDRF–SDRF training.

secs.t: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

x: All three statements are correct: the SDRF is associated with Section 48, serves as the first relief fund for notified disasters, and has a 75:25 Centre-State contribution ratio for general States.
The Finance Commission recommends the calamities covered and the allocation for each State; the Ministry of Home Affairs subsequently notifies them.

secs.t: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

x: The NDMP 2016 provided short-term, medium-term and long-term time frames of five, ten and fifteen years respectively.
The community-based disaster risk reduction programme through PRIs involves
Rs 507.37 crore
The project has an outlay of Rs 507.37 crore, involves the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA, covers 20 States and 81 districts, and includes 20 Gram Panchayats per district.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Their inclusion in the notified list opens the possibility of support from the SDRF, NDRF and disaster mitigation funds.
The initiative asks Union Ministries to prepare plans under
Sections 35 and 37
of the Disaster Management Act.
Andhra Pradesh released Rs 277.63 crore in 2025–26 and Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27 under SDRF/NDRF; Rs 521.17 crore was allocated under SDMF/NDMF.
About 13–14 Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems form annually; most originate in the northern Bay and can cause flooding in the Godavari–Krishna basins.

rows.title: Marine resources - fisheries, minerals, polymetallic nodules, EEZ, blue economy

secs.t: EEZ - extent, India's area, UNCLOS zones and coastal-state rights

x: The EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles and confers resource-related sovereign rights.
The continental shelf may extend up to
350 nautical miles
where the outer edge of the continental margin permits it.
The territorial sea is 12 nautical miles or about 22 km, it largely overlaps the productive shelf, and India's EEZ is about 2.37 million sq km.

secs.t: World fisheries - major grounds, favourable conditions, fishing and pearl nations

x: The Grand Banks lie
off Newfoundland in the north-west Atlantic
, where the Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current.
Norway, Japan and
Iceland
are fishing-dependent countries, but Iceland's exports lean most heavily on fish.
Japan is associated with cultured Akoya pearls, China leads by freshwater-pearl volume, India's Gulf of Mannar has pearl beds, and Pinctada radiata in the Persian Gulf has been affected by pollution.

secs.t: Polymetallic nodules, ISA licensing, Deep Ocean Mission

x: Polymetallic sulphides contain
copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum
, making them important for several strategic and clean-energy applications.
The Nellore seafront facility tests nodule-mining crawlers, riser pipes, slurry pumps, LTTD desalination and wave-energy units.
Samudrayaan involves the indigenous Matsya 6000 submersible, designed for a three-member crew, deep-sea mining and exploration, with a target depth of 6000 m.

secs.t: Indian fisheries - fishing zones, PMMSY

x: India's seafood exports were ₹62,408 crore in FY 2024–25, with frozen shrimp exports to the United States and China leading the sector.
Mechanised boats are barred in the 0–5 nautical mile inshore zone, although enforcement is weak.
PMMSY is the flagship programme of the
Blue Revolution
and supports cold chains, processing, harbours and deep-sea modernisation.

secs.t: Offshore minerals and energy - oil/gas basins, beach placers

x: The first tranche of 13 offshore blocks was auctioned on
28 November 2024
under a composite licence arrangement.
Lime mud had 3 blocks, heavy minerals 16, construction sand 9, and polymetallic crust/nodules 7.
Chavara is known for beach placer minerals, especially monazite and ilmenite, not as an offshore petroleum basin.
Monazite is associated with thorium, whereas ilmenite is an important titanium-bearing mineral found in beach placers.

secs.t: Blue economy - framework, sectors, SAGAR

x: The blue economy involves sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters to promote economic growth, employment and conservation.
All six listed areas—fisheries, aquaculture, ports and shipping, marine biotechnology, coastal tourism, offshore renewable energy, deep-ocean resources and maritime security—are included sectors.
SAGAR means “
Security and Growth for All in the Region
.” It was articulated as India's Indian Ocean vision in 2015 at Mauritius.

secs.t: Sea-bed hydrothermal sulphides and gas hydrates

x: Polymetallic sulphides form around hydrothermal vents located on mid-ocean ridges.
India explored the Central/Southwest Indian Ridge in 2016 and the Carlsberg Ridge in 2025.
Gas hydrates are methane ice deposits occurring in seabed sediments.
Gas-hydrate exploration under the National Gas Hydrate Programme covers the Krishna-Godavari basin, the Mahanadi region and the Andaman region.

secs.t: Marine resources of AP - harbours, basins, beach sands

x: The concessional aqua power tariff is
₹1.50 per unit
for units up to 10 acres in aqua zones; the tariff mentioned for other cases is ₹3.85 per unit.
All three associations are correct: the Krishna-Godavari basin has offshore oil and gas, the northern coast has beach sand minerals, and NIOT Nellore and CMFRI centres support marine research.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court directed Tamil Nadu to frame a “specified channel” through territorial waters so that purse-seine vessels can reach the EEZ.
The Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy is located at Vignan's University, Vadlamudi, in Guntur.
The stated criticism is that degradation of inshore areas pushes fishers offshore, while the FAO has described the increase from deep-sea resources as only marginal.

rows.title: Continental resources - land, forest, water, mineral and energy resources; conservation
sub: Group-II S2-29: Natural resources of India - land, water and forest resources and their distribution

secs.t: World mineral and energy regions → resource

x: Katanga is noted for copper and cobalt; Minas Gerais for iron ore, gold and diamonds; the Mesabi Range for iron ore; and Witwatersrand for gold.
India signed the first ISA contract for exploration of polymetallic sulphides on the
Carlsberg Ridge in the Arabian Sea
The International Seabed Authority is Jamaica-based and was created under UNCLOS; its role includes regulating seabed mineral activities in the international area.

secs.t: Traditional water harvesting systems → region

x: Exam angle: APPSC asked Eri (2024), Ahar-pyne (2024) and Zabo (2024) directly.
Ahar-pyne is practised in
South Bihar
; the ahar is a catchment basin and the pyne is a channel.
Kuhl consists of diversion channels in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu, Katta consists of temporary check dams in Karnataka, and Bawari or Baoli means stepwells in Rajasthan and Delhi.

secs.t: Irrigation and multipurpose projects → river and beneficiaries

x: Har Khet Ko Pani covers Command Area Development and Water Management, surface minor irrigation, repair-renovation-restoration of water bodies and groundwater development.
The National Perspective Plan dates to 1980, PMKSY was introduced in 2015–16, Per Drop More Crop moved under RKVY in December 2021, and the projection is reported for 2050 in the 2026 reference.

The proposal is associated with Sir Arthur Cotton, the National Perspective Plan dates to 1980, the plan contains 30 links divided into 14 Himalayan and 16 Peninsular links, and the NWDA is associated with it.

secs.t: Resource classification and conservation milestones

x: Forest
s, animals, plants and micro-organisms are biotic resources because they originate from living organisms.
Stock refers to resources that exist but cannot presently be used because suitable technology is unavailable.
Deep bore tubewells for irrigation contribute to groundwater depletion, brick production removes topsoil, and agricultural expansion causes loss of biodiversity habitats.
The Brundtland Commission report,
Our Common Future
, published in 1987, defined sustainable development.

secs.t: Land resources - land use, wasteland, watershed

x: The nine-fold classification includes forests, non-agricultural uses, barren and unculturable land, permanent pastures, miscellaneous tree crops, culturable wasteland, current fallow, other fallow and net sown area.
Indian Remote Sensing (
IRS
) data are used for wasteland mapping and National Wastelands Monitoring.
Soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation, nutrient depletion, falling water tables and soil pollution are causes of land degradation.

secs.t: Mineral legislation - MMDR Act, auctions, DMF

x: The DMF was created under the 2015 MMDR amendment for mining-affected districts and is funded through miners’ royalty-linked contributions.
The criticism refers to the 2024 nine-judge Supreme Court verdict in
Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL
The verdict held that royalty is not a tax and recognised State taxing powers over mineral rights under Entry 50 and mineral-bearing land under Entry 49 of the State List.

secs.t: Gemstones - composition and colour-giving elements

x: Ruby and sapphire are varieties of corundum, while emerald is beryl.
Sapphire is corundum coloured blue by the presence of
iron and titanium
Emerald is beryl, a beryllium aluminium silicate.

secs.t: Country → resource richness and producer rank

x: The top three refiners’ average share of critical minerals was about
in 2024, compared with 82% in 2020.
The Lithium Triangle comprises
Chile, Argentina and Bolivia
The Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is identified as the world’s leading source of
cobalt
US Project Vault is described as a
$12 billion mineral stockpile

secs.t: Forest resources - uses, terms, JFM

x: Silviculture is the science and practice of
raising and tending forest trees
, including regeneration, thinning and rotation.
Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock on the same piece of land.
The Forest Rights Act, 2006 gives
Gram Sabhas
authority over the management, protection and regeneration of community forest resources.
The Appiko Movement began in the Salkani forest near Sirsi in Karnataka on 8 September 1983.
Shifting cultivation in the north-eastern hill slopes is known as jhum.

secs.t: Watershed and water schemes - IWMP, Hariyali, JSA, Atal Bhujal, Namami Gange, NRCP

x: The Hariyali guidelines of 2003 provided for implementation of watershed projects through
Panchayati Raj Institutions
IWMP is now the
Watershed Development Component of PMKSY
, with WDC-PMKSY 2.0 covering degraded and rain-fed areas.

AIBP is handled by Jal Shakti for major and medium projects; HKKP covers new water sources under Jal Shakti; Watershed Development is under Rural Development’s Department of Land Resources; and PDMC was under Agriculture in PMKSY during 2015–2021.

secs.t: Water resources - world share, groundwater categories, per capita availability

x: India is the world’s largest groundwater user and accounts for approximately
one-quarter
of global groundwater extraction.
CGWB categories include safe, semi-critical, critical, over-exploited and saline. ‘
Perennial
’ is not one of the listed assessment categories.
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi
are identified as the regions worst affected by groundwater over-exploitation.
The
Central Water Commission
handles surface-water planning and flood control, whereas CGWB handles groundwater.

secs.t: Natural resource regions of the subcontinent - mineral, forest, water

x: The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland; the Himalaya and NE hills have forests, hydropower and jhum lands; the Indo-Gangetic plains have alluvium and groundwater; and the Thar/north-west has scarce water and traditional harvesting.
The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland and contains
iron ore, coal, bauxite and mica
The Indo-Gangetic plains are characterised by fertile alluvial soils, rich groundwater and comparatively few minerals.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The warning at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi concerned the weaponisation of
critical minerals
Pattiseema lift water was released into the Krishna delta canals at
7,158 cusecs
during the 2026 El Niño-related deficit.
Gandikota reservoir is on the Pennar and serves drought-prone Rayalaseema as part of the Telugu Ganga system; this explains Assertion A.
River interlinking has been criticised because monsoons and climate change can make supposedly surplus basins unreliable.

rows.title: World - continents, major mountain systems, plateaus, plains and deserts

secs.t: Mountain ranges → location, countries, bodies separated

x: All three statements are correct: the Urals are old fold mountains, the Alps are young fold mountains, and the Andes run along the Pacific side of South America.
The
Atlas
Mountains of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia separate the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastal areas from the Sahara.
The Taurus Mountains in southern Türkiye bound the Anatolian Plateau with the
Pontic ranges

secs.t: Continents and countries → area ranking

x: The descending order is Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
The order is Russia, Canada, United States of America, China, Brazil, Australia and India.
Bolivia and Paraguay
are the landlocked countries identified in South America in this classification.
Luxembourg borders Belgium, Germany and France.

secs.t: Deserts → countries and latitudinal belt

x: The Taklamakan is a cold, continental desert in Xinjiang, China, occupying the Tarim Basin.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert, the Namib is among the oldest, Great Victoria is Australia's largest desert, and the Thar lies in India and Pakistan.
Hot deserts commonly occur between about
15° and 30° north and south
, under subtropical high-pressure conditions.

secs.t: Highest peak of each continent (Seven Summits)

x: Aconcagua is the highest peak in South America and the
tallest mountain outside Asia
, at 6,961 metres.
Denali, Kilimanjaro, Elbrus and Vinson Massif are respectively the highest peaks of North America, Africa, Europe and Antarctica.
Richard Bass
was the first person to complete the Seven Summits, achieving the feat in 1985.

secs.t: Regional physiographic names → country/continent

x: The Terai is a marshy zone south of the Bhabar, occurring in Nepal and along India's Himalayan foothills.
The Levant includes the eastern Mediterranean region; Nullarbor Plain is in southern Australia; Guiana Highlands are in northern South America; and Lake Eyre Basin is in central Australia.
The Finke River or Larapinta in central Australia drains to the
Lake Eyre Basin

secs.t: Mountain superlatives - longest, oldest

x: The Himalayas and Atlas are young Alpine fold mountains, while the Appalachians and Urals are old mountain ranges.
The Aravalli Range is India’s oldest mountain system and is associated with Archaean rocks and Dharwar sediments.
Gurushikhar rises to approximately
etres and is the highest point of the Aravalli Range.

secs.t: Plateaus → type and location

x: The
Deccan Plateau
is a lava or continental plateau and is regarded as one of the oldest plateaus.
The Tibetan Plateau is the highest major plateau; Colorado is cut by the Grand Canyon; the Bolivian Altiplano lies within the Andes; and the Mongolian Plateau is in Central Asia.
The Anatolian Plateau lies in Turkiye between the Pontic and Taurus mountain ranges.

secs.t: Major plains of the world

x: World plains generally lie below 200 metres, are commonly formed by rivers and support dense populations because of their level and fertile land.
The Indo-Gangetic Plain is an
aggradational plain
formed through the accumulation of sediments.
The Indo-Gangetic Plain has a stated width of 70–500 kilometres, while the Tibetan Plateau figures are elevations rather than widths.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The year 2026 is the International Year for
Rangelands and Pastoralists
The
Finke River
has been confirmed as the oldest river.
The Indian expedition reported in February 2026 was associated with
Aconcagua
, the highest mountain outside Asia.
