rows.title: World - major rivers, lakes, seas, straits, canals and islands

secs.t: Rivers → source, mouth, countries, flow direction

x: The
Danube
crosses ten countries, including Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Serbia and Romania, making it the river crossing the most countries among these options.
The Rhine rises in the Swiss Alps near Lake Toma, flows northwards into the North Sea and forms part of the Germany-France border.
The
Elbe
originates in the Czech Republic, flows through Germany and reaches the North Sea; Hamburg is located on it.

secs.t: Lakes → country and superlatives

x: Lake
Victoria
, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, is the second-largest freshwater lake and is associated with the source of the White Nile.
Tanganyika, Albert, Edward and Kivu
lie in the western branch, including the Albertine or western rift region.
The Dead Sea is the lowest point on land and lies about
1,385 feet
below sea level according to the cited figure.

secs.t: Canals and straits → water bodies connected

x: The
Panama Canal
connects the Atlantic side, through the Caribbean Sea, with the Pacific Ocean and uses a lock system.
The
Malacca Strait
, between Malaysia and Indonesia, connects the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea.
The Kerch Strait connects the Black Sea and the
Sea of Azov
and lies between Russia and Ukraine.

secs.t: Seas → bordering countries and inflowing rivers

x: The
five
littoral states of the Caspian Sea are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
The Red Sea has no major river inflow, and the Dahlak Archipelago is associated with Eritrea on its western side.
The
Nile, Rhone, Po and Ebro
are listed as rivers flowing into the Mediterranean Sea.

secs.t: Cities → river

x: Kyiv
is located on the Dnieper River.
Budapest, Vienna and Bratislava are important cities located on the
Danube
River.
Belgrade is located at the confluence of the
Sava and Danube
rivers.
Cologne is situated on the Rhine, not the Danube.

secs.t: Great Lakes of North America

x: Lake Ontario is drained by the
St Lawrence River
, which flows towards the Atlantic Ocean.
Lake Ontario is easternmost, receives the Niagara River from Lake Erie, and is linked to Erie by the Welland Canal, which bypasses Niagara Falls.
St Marys River connects Superior and Huron, the Straits of Mackinac connects Michigan and Huron, and the Detroit River connects Huron and Erie.

secs.t: Islands and regions → country

x: Normandy is a region of France.
The Socotra archipelago is associated with
Yemen
and is identified as a UNESCO site.
All four pairs are correctly matched.
The order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo and Madagascar.
Greenland is the world's largest island and is associated with
Denmark
Indonesia is identified as the largest archipelagic country.

secs.t: Waterfalls → river, country, records

x: Victoria Falls
on the Zambezi is described as the largest sheet of falling water and lies between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Niagara is between Erie and Ontario, Iguazu is associated with Argentina and Brazil, and Tugela is in South Africa's Drakensberg.
Tugela Falls
, located in the Drakensberg of South Africa, is identified as the second highest waterfall.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Iran is not a party to UNCLOS; nevertheless, the principle of transit passage is binding as customary international law.
The MV OMORFI attack in the Black Sea killed
an Indian crew member
Pulicat, in Tirupati district, is the second largest brackish lagoon after Chilika and is separated from the sea by Sriharikota.

rows.title: India - location, extent, frontiers, standard meridian and neighbouring countries

secs.t: Neighbouring countries - land border ranking, sea neighbours, bordering states

x: India has land borders with seven countries: Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.
China
has the second-longest land border with India, extending for 3,488 km; Bangladesh ranks first.
India's border with Bhutan runs along
Sikkim
, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.
The international land frontier is 15,106.7 km long and passes through 92 districts of 16 States and 2 Union Territories.

secs.t: Tropic of Cancer → states

x: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight States, ending in the east with
Mizoram
after Tripura.

secs.t: Boundary lines and disputed tracts

x: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe during
the Partition of 1947
to demarcate India and Pakistan, including the later India-Bangladesh boundary context.
The Durand Line was the British India-Afghanistan boundary; the McMahon Line concerns India-China east of Nepal; the LoC is in Jammu and Kashmir; and the LAC is the India-China de facto line.

secs.t: Coastline and land frontier length

x: Exam angle: quote the survey year with the number - both figures are in circulation.
The approximately 47.7% rise resulted from improved measurement methodology, particularly
finer GIS tracing of creeks and inlets at a 1:250,000 scale
, not from a physical increase in coastline.
The coastal Union Territories are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Puducherry, and Daman and Diu.

secs.t: Interstate boundaries and UT enclaves

x: Karnataka
borders Goa, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, the maximum among the southern States.
Puducherry and Karaikal lie within Tamil Nadu, Mahe lies within Kerala, and Yanam lies within Andhra Pradesh in the Godavari delta.

secs.t: Water bodies separating India from neighbours; surrounding seas

x: The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives, the Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep group, and the Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar separate India from Sri Lanka.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie approximately
southeast of the Indian mainland.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The latitudinal extent of present-day Andhra Pradesh is approximately
. An extent reaching 22° N is not applicable to the present State of Andhra Pradesh.
The 2023–24 remeasurement places Andhra Pradesh's coastline at approximately 1,053.07 km, making it the third-longest after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
The APSES 2024–25 figure is 974 km, while the 2023–24 remeasurement gives 1,053.07 km.

rows.title: India - physiographic division: the Himalayas (ranges, regional divisions, passes)

secs.t: Regional divisions → bounding rivers

x: The standard Burrard boundaries are Indus–Sutlej, Sutlej–Kali, Kali–Teesta and Teesta–Dihang.
Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh
are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali and includes the lakes Nainital and Bhimtal.
Pindari, Milam and Kafni
glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.

secs.t: Parallel ranges → names, order, composition

x: Karakoram and Zaskar are Trans-Himalayan ranges, Ladakh continues as Kailash in Tibet, and the Kashmir Valley separates Zaskar from Pir Panjal.
The Himadri, or Greater Himalaya, is the loftiest and oldest Himalayan range, with an average elevation above 6,000 metres and a granite core.
The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest Himalayan range, about 15–50 km wide, with an average elevation of about 1,300 metres and simple folds formed from river deposits.

secs.t: Peaks → range, division, country

x: Kamet is a peak of the Himadri in the Kumaon or Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
Kanchenjunga belongs to the Himadri and lies on the India-Nepal boundary.
Godwin Austen or K2 is 8,611 metres high and belongs to the Karakoram.
Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya and is located in Tibet, China.

secs.t: Width, fold asymmetry, age, structure

x: The Himalayan arc extends for approximately
from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east.
The Himadri has asymmetrical folds; the Himalayan slope towards the plains is steeper, while the Tibetan side is gentler.
The Himalayas were uplifted from Tethys sediments during the Tertiary, broadly from the Eocene to the Pliocene, approximately 60 to 7 million years ago.

secs.t: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

x: The Himalaya makes a knee-bend at the
Dihang gorge
near Namcha Barwa and then turns southwards as the Purvanchal hills.
Garo, Khasi and Jaintia are the principal hill groups associated with the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya.
The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills generally run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills.

secs.t: Sub-divisions by relief and alignment (counts)

x: The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.
The counts are three northern-mountain groups, three longitudinal parallel ranges, four regional divisions and four structural zones.
Plains form the largest relief division of India and account for about
43 percent
of the country’s area.

secs.t: Mountain passes and tunnels

x: Banihal Pass has an elevation of about 2,833 metres, whereas Rohtang Pass has an elevation of about 3,978 metres.
Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana
are identified as avalanche-prone passes.
Nathu La connects Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley.

secs.t: Glaciers → range and position

x: Siachen lies in the Karakoram's Nubra region and marks Ladakh's northern limit, while Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar are in the Karakoram sector of Gilgit-Baltistan.
Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.
Siachen is in the Karakoram's Nubra region, Baltoro is in Karakoram in Gilgit-Baltistan, Gangotri belongs to the Greater Himalaya, and Pindari belongs to Kumaon.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Himalayas define India's northern boundary, act as a climatic barrier, and Shiwalik debris contributed to the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayas, while Namcha Barwa marks their eastern end.
Both the assertion and reason are true, and the debris carried and deposited from the Himalayan ranges explains the Shiwalik contribution to the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

src: Sources: APP (Geography Part 1 Northern Mountains: Himalayas, Trans-Himalayas, Purvachal; Location and Extent); UPSC (Indian Geography p.9, p.10, p.13); IYB 2026 p.16, p.575, p.657; CDI (Block14 Indian Rock System; Block06 Landslide and Avalanche)

rows.title: India - the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Coastal Plains and the Islands
sub: Group-II S2-16: India - major physiographic features and physical divisions

secs.t: Coastal plains - divisions, width, lagoons, emergent vs submergent

x: Emergent coasts result from land rise or sea fall and are associated with wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas.
Submergent coasts form when land sinks or sea level rises, producing narrow coasts, estuaries and rias.
The east coast is treated as emergent and includes the lagoons of Pulicat and Chilika, while the west coast is submergent and includes drowned Dwarka and estuaries.
The Malabar Coast extends from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari, is about 550 km long and is generally 10–30 km wide.
Kolleru was formerly a lagoon but became an inland freshwater lake due to coastal emergence.
The increase resulted from finer 1:250,000-scale GIS tracing that captured numerous creeks and inlets; the land itself did not grow.

secs.t: Islands - Andaman-Nicobar vs Lakshadweep

x: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, approximately 1,200 km south-east of the Indian mainland.
Lakshadweep comprises 36 islands, including 10 inhabited islands, while about 572 islands is a commonly cited count for Andaman and Nicobar.
Minicoy is the largest and southernmost island, while the Amindivi and Cannanore groups lie north and south of 11° N respectively.
Barren Island is India's only active volcano and last erupted in 2017; Narcondam is a dormant volcanic island.
The 2023–24 remeasurement counted 1,389 islands, comprising 1,298 offshore and 91 inshore islands.

secs.t: Peninsular Plateau - sub-divisions, rocks, Deccan Traps

x: The Peninsular Plateau is mineral-rich, the Nilgiris mark the meeting point of the two Ghats, and the Deccan Plateau is a stable inverted triangle.
The Deccan Traps formed through extensive
fissure eruptions of basaltic lava
The word 'trap' is derived from the Swedish term for
step
, referring to the step-like appearance of the basaltic landscape.

secs.t: Western vs Eastern Ghats - names, meeting point, passes

x: The Western Ghats are continuous south of the Tapti, whereas the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and eroded.
The Western Ghats are locally known successively as Sahyadri, Nilgiri, Anaimalai, Palani and Cardamom from north to south.
Papikondalu, Nallamala, Erramala, Seshachalam and Velikonda are associated with the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh.
The Cardamom Hills continue the Western Ghats, while the Eastern Ghats consist of khondalite and charnockite and have an average height of about 610 metres.
The Peninsular Plateau is the largest and oldest division, a Precambrian Gondwana shield and a triangular block of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
The Deccan Plateau covers about 7 lakh square kilometres and is made of horizontal lava sheets known as the Deccan Trap, which consists of basalt.

secs.t: Hills → state and peaks, height order

x: The correct descending order is Nanga Parbat, Kamet, Anaimudi and Doddabetta, with approximate heights of 8,126 m, 7,756 m, 2,695 m and 2,637 m respectively.

The heights increase as Doddabetta (2,637 m), Guru Shikhar (1,722 m), Arma Konda (1,680 m) and Anamudi (2,695 m) only if the figures are checked? The correct numerical order is Arma Konda, Guru Shikhar, Doddabetta and Anamudi; therefore the options require correction.
Nanga Parbat lies at the western end of the Himadri in the J&K–PoK region and is about 8,126 metres high.

secs.t: Indian Desert (Marusthali) and the Rann of Kutch

x: Exam angle: the APPSC GS 2025 key orders desert features as arid climate → dunes → thorny bushes → seasonal streams.
Luni is a seasonal river and ends in the Rann of Kutch; it does not reach the Arabian Sea as a perennial river.
Luni, Machhu, Rupen, Saraswati, Banas and Ghaggar drain into salt lakes or disappear in the sand, forming part of the inland drainage system.
Agariya communities are traditionally associated with salt farming in the Rann of Kutch.

secs.t: Northern Plains - Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, Khadar; regional plains

x: The
Bhabar
is a narrow belt of coarse gravel and pebbles along the foothills of the Shiwaliks.
The
Terai
lies south of the Bhabar and is marshy, waterlogged and forested because the streams re-emerge there.
The land surface of the Northern Plains declines by only about
200 metres
from Delhi to the Bay of Bengal over a distance of nearly 1,600 kilometres.
The Molassis Basin is located in
Mizoram in the Purvachal hills
and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.

secs.t: Himalayan ranges - Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks, Trans-Himalaya → composition, valleys, duns, karewas, regional divisions, north-south order

x: Exam angle: "Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu valleys" →
Himachal
range.
The Himachal contains the Kashmir, Kangra, Kullu and Lahul–Spiti valleys and includes hill stations such as Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital; Darjeeling is also associated with this range.
Karewas, also called Vudr, are lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces in the Kashmir Valley and form part of the Tertiary system.
The principal structural zones are arranged from north to south as the Indus–Tsangpo Suture, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault.

secs.t: Mountain passes → range and state (Bhor Ghat, Thal Ghat, Pal Ghat, Nathu La, Lipulekh, Bomdila, Zoji La, Shipki La)

x: Exam angle:
Bhorghat and Thalghat
are the Sahyadri pair.
Bhor Ghat and Thal Ghat are in Maharashtra, Nathu La is in Sikkim and Bomdila is in Arunachal Pradesh.
Both Bhor Ghat and Thal Ghat are passes of the Sahyadri, particularly the northern Western Ghats.
Zoji La was reopened by the BRO 32 days after its winter closure on 1 April 2025, and it lies on the Srinagar–Leh route.

secs.t: India's size and boundaries - area, world rank, extent, states with most neighbours, land frontier neighbours

x: India's mainland extends about 3,214 km from north to south and 2,933 km from east to west, entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
India’s land frontier touches seven countries: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh.
Uttar Pradesh
borders eight States and the National Capital Territory of Delhi, giving it the greatest number of neighbouring administrative units in the list.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Shipki La was opened to Indian tourists for border tourism, and the BRO is building a 120 km all-weather road to Lipulekh.
In Andhra Pradesh, the Eastern Ghats are called the Eastern Ranges in the north and Kadapa Ranges in the south; their lowest spur ends at Dolphin’s Nose, about 335 m high, near Visakhapatnam.
The 2023–24 remeasurement gives Andhra Pradesh a coastline of 1,053.07 km and third rank, while older figures cite 974 km.

rows.title: India - Himalayan drainage system: Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra basins

secs.t: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj

x: Exam angle: "south-based tributary" = Betwa/Son/Yamuna group; Burhi Dihing and Dhansiri are Brahmaputra tributaries, not the Ganga's (PYQ 2024: neither statement correct).
At Farakka, the Ganga divides into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly on the left and the Padma on the right, which enters Bangladesh.
The Padma joins the Brahmaputra and
Meghna
system and enters the Bay of Bengal as the Meghna.
The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary after the Yamuna and joins the Ganga near Maner, close to Patna.
The Gandak is referred to as Sadanira in the
Shatapatha Brahmana

secs.t: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT

x: The Indus rises at Singge Khabab in the Kailash range at approximately
5,182 metres
The Chenab is formed by the union of the
Chandra and Bhaga
rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh.
The Salal project is a 690 MW NHPC project on the
Chenab
and is identified as India’s first project in the region under the treaty.
The Indus flows northwest between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat through an antecedent gorge and meets the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

secs.t: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries

x: The Brahmaputra rises at the
Chemayungdung Glacier
in the Kailash range, east of Lake Mansarovar.
The river, known as the Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo in Tibet, turns south at
Namche Barwa
Dibang and Lohit
join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya, after which the combined river is called the Brahmaputra.
The Teesta is about 414 km long, rises at Tso Lhamo Lake and has the Rangeet as its largest tributary.
The Indus rises at Singge Khabab in the
Kailash range near Mansarovar
The river is called the Tsangpo in Tibet and becomes the Siang or Dihang on entering
Arunachal Pradesh

secs.t: Rivers originating near Mansarovar - which do and which do not

x: The Indus originates at Singge Khabab.
The
Sutlej
originates in the Mansarovar–Kailash region, near Rakas Tal.

secs.t: Himalayan drainage character - antecedent, perennial, plains patterns, river groups

x: Himalayan rivers are antecedent because they existed before the Himalayan uplift and continued to follow their courses by cutting deep gorges through the rising mountains.
Valley-in-valley topography, paired terraces and entrenched meanders are characteristic features associated with antecedent Himalayan rivers.
In the plains, the gentle gradient causes Himalayan rivers to meander, shift their channels and form ox-bow lakes and floodplains.

secs.t: Lakes of the Himalaya and north-east → state and water type

x: Pangong Tso is a high-altitude brackish or saline lake situated in Ladakh and extending into Tibet.
Loktak is a freshwater lake of Manipur known for floating phumdis and its association with Keibul Lamjao National Park.
Wular, located in Jammu and Kashmir, is
the largest freshwater lake of India and is fed by the Jhelum
River.

secs.t: River conservation - Namami Gange, NMCG, Global River Cities Alliance

x: The cited criterion treats a river stretch as polluted when its biochemical oxygen demand exceeds 3 mg/L.

COD covers biodegradable as well as non-biodegradable organic matter and its clean-water value is below 5.0 mg/L. Statement 3 is false because it incorrectly equates COD with BOD and excludes non-biodegradable matter.
The cited criterion for a polluted river is BOD greater than 3 mg/L. A BOD greater than 30 mg/L identifies a Priority-I stretch.

secs.t: Dams and canals → river

x: Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are projects on the
Chenab
River in Jammu and Kashmir.
The Sirhind Canal is drawn from the Sutlej at
Ropar
in Punjab.
The Rihand Project in Uttar Pradesh is on the Rihand, a tributary in the Son system, and its reservoir is called Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The total allocation under the 1973 Bansagar Accord is 7.75 million acre-feet, comprising 5.75 MAF for Bihar and 2 MAF for Jharkhand.
Nepal flash floods raised the
Narayani-Gandak
system, leading to alerts in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
Roads without adequate drainage, deforestation and silted channels are cited as partly man-made contributors to Brahmaputra flooding.

rows.title: India - Peninsular drainage: east-flowing and west-flowing rivers, river basins, watershed
sub: Group-II S2-18: India - drainage system: Himalayan and Peninsular rivers

secs.t: Tributaries → main river and bank

x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right bank.
Bhima is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna; Kabini and Hemavathi are tributaries of the Kaveri; and Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi.
Sheonath and Hasdeo are left-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi, while Purna and Indravati are left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
Pranhita is formed by the
Wardha and Wainganga
rivers before joining the Godavari.
Sileru is a tributary of Sabari, is known as Machkund in its upper course, and joins Sabari at the AP–Chhattisgarh–Odisha tri-junction.
Manjira, a right-bank tributary of the Godavari, joins it near
Nizamabad
Tungabhadra is a right-bank tributary, joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram in Nandyal, and has Vedavathi and Handri among its tributaries.
Vedavathi, also called Hagari, is a tributary of Tungabhadra and therefore belongs to the
Krishna
river system.
The Raichur Doab is the land tract lying between the
Krishna and Tungabhadra
rivers.

secs.t: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage

x: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and Mahi flow westwards towards the Arabian Sea.
Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys, but as west-flowing rivers they generally form estuaries rather than large deltas.
The
Mahi
crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and ultimately reaches the Gulf of Khambhat.
The Aravallis give rise to west-flowing Luni and Sabarmati, east-flowing Banas and north-flowing Sahibi; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
West-flowing rivers are generally short and swift, form estuaries rather than deltas and are suitable for hydropower.

secs.t: River origin → source hills/plateau

x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari are all listed as rivers originating in the Eastern Ghats.
The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the
Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri
river systems.

secs.t: Basin area and length ranking

x: The relative order is Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi, while the Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
The descending order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km) and Mahanadi (858 km).
Among these Peninsular basins, the order is Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi from larger to smaller.

secs.t: Waterfalls → river and region

x: Kunchikal is on the Varahi, Jog on the Sharavati, Dhuandhar on the Narmada and Hundru on the Subarnarekha.
Dudhsagar Falls lies on the Mandovi River near
the Goa–Karnataka border
Sivasamudram, Chunchanakatte and Hogenakkal are all waterfalls associated with the Kaveri River.
Dhuandhar Falls is situated on the Narmada near Jabalpur, close to the Marble Rocks, in Madhya Pradesh.

secs.t: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

x: Lonar in Maharashtra is a saline-alkaline lake formed in a meteorite-impact crater.
Chilika in Odisha is
Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon
and was India's first Ramsar site in 1981.
Wular is a freshwater lake on the Jhelum, situated between the Pir Panjal and Zaskar ranges.
Charaichung was established in 1633 by Pratap Singha and is called
Asia's first protected bird site

secs.t: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

x: Srirangam lies between the Kaveri and Kollidam, Aliabet is the largest island in the Narmada, and Shivanasamudram is a Kaveri riverine island.
Himalayan rivers are generally perennial and form deep antecedent gorges, while Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow through broad, shallow, graded valleys.
The listed Godavari distributaries include Gautami, Vasishta, Vainateya, Tulya, Bharadwaja, Kaushika and Athreya.

secs.t: Rivers in news - linking and recharge projects, urban rivers

x: The
Ken-Betwa
project links the Ken and Betwa rivers and involves Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
Par-Tapi-Narmada concerns Gujarat and Maharashtra; Tapti Basin Mega Recharge concerns Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; and Aghanashini-Vedavathi includes a 194-km pipeline to Vani Vilas Sagar.
Pandoh is situated on the Beas in Himachal Pradesh and feeds the Beas-Sutlej link.
The Srisailam project on the Krishna feeds the
Telugu Ganga and Veligonda
systems.

secs.t: Watershed programmes and inter-state water disputes and tribunals

x: The 2018 allocation mentioned for Karnataka was
284.75 tmcft
, while Tamil Nadu was allocated 404.25 tmcft out of the tribunal’s 740 tmcft framework.
Water is placed in Entry 17 of the State List, subject to
Entry 56 of the Union List
concerning regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
DRDA was the district organ responsible for implementing
Ministry of Rural Development anti-poverty programmes, beginning with IRDP

secs.t: Confluences and prayags → rivers forming them, doabs

x: Nandprayag is Alaknanda–Nandakini, Karnaprayag is Alaknanda–Pindar, Rudraprayag is Alaknanda–Mandakini and Devprayag is Alaknanda–Bhagirathi.
At Devprayag, the Alaknanda joins the
Bhagirathi
, after which the combined river is known as the Ganga.
The confluence at Prayagraj is traditionally described as the meeting of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical
Saraswati
The Sind Sagar or Thal Doab lies between the Jhelum and the Indus rivers.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Climate change can alter rainfall and river-flow patterns, thereby weakening the assumption of permanently surplus basins used in the interlinking paradigm.

All three statements are correct: Telangana opposed the Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link, the Cauvery basin has been projected to remain dry until 2050, and climate change challenges surplus-basin assumptions.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are allocated to India, while the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are mainly allocated to Pakistan.
The Godavari meets the sea at
Antarvedi
through seven distributaries forming the Konaseema delta.

rows.title: India - climate: mechanism of the monsoon, theories, seasons and their characteristics
sub: Group-II S2-17: India - climate and the monsoon mechanism; seasons and rainfall distribution

secs.t: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region

x: Exam angle:
Kaal Baisakhi
→ West Bengal.
Mango showers
Karnataka
Blossom or coffee-blossom showers
occur in Kerala and the nearby coffee-growing areas of Karnataka, where they aid coffee flowering.
Bardoli Chheerha
is a thunderstorm phenomenon of Assam and is also referred to as tea showers because of its importance to tea cultivation.
The Loo is a hot, dry and dusty afternoon wind of the northern and north-western plains and is also locally experienced in Rayalaseema.
Andhi or dust storms originate in Rajasthan, particularly the Thar region, and extend towards
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh
Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India and occurs just before the arrival of the monsoon.

secs.t: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks

x: Monsoons are seasonal or periodic secondary winds.
The monsoons are described as being confined to the tropics between
20°N and 20°S
The sudden onset of the south-west monsoon in the first week of June is called the
monsoon burst
Al Masudi
, a ninth-century scholar, noted the seasonal winds associated with the monsoon system.

secs.t: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches

x: Exam angle: both statements are correct: "Kerala receives the SW monsoon first" and "the Bay branch soaks Meghalaya". Monsoons lie mainly within
20 deg N-20 deg S
and relief governs SW-monsoon rain.
The southwest monsoon reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands at about
25 May
, before its normal onset over Kerala.
The IMD uses rainfall recorded over
five-day pentads
while fixing the onset of the southwest monsoon.
The onset criteria include rainfall of 2.5 mm for two days at 60 per cent of 14 stations and westerlies reaching about 600 hPa after 10 May.
The Arabian Sea branch first strikes the Western Ghats and Malabar Coast and subsequently advances northward along the west coast.
The Western Ghats force uplift on their windward side, leaving a rain-shadow region to their east.
Bay of Bengal cyclones
bring bimodal rainfall to the south during the October–November retreating monsoon season.

secs.t: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD

x: Sir Edmund Halley's thermal theory, proposed in 1686, attributes the monsoon to differential heating of land and sea.
In summer, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough.

The northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet is associated with onset, while its return south of the Himalayas accompanies withdrawal; the tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa.
El Niño generally weakens the Indian monsoon, while La Niña generally aids or strengthens it.
A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can partly offset the weakening influence of El Niño.

secs.t: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

x: Exam angle: the APPSC G1 2024 matching key is short dry season → west coast; dry summer → Coromandel; dry winter → Ganga plain; steppe → NW.
Western disturbances are temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region and reaching north-western India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
The retreating monsoon occurs mainly in October-November, brings clear skies and is associated with cyclones from the Bay of Bengal.
Mediterranean western disturbances bring about 10–15 cm of rain to north-west India, benefit rabi crops and produce snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

secs.t: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

x: The sequence is winter, pre-monsoon or summer, south-west monsoon and post-monsoon or north-east monsoon.
The IMD south-west monsoon season extends from
June to September
North-western and central India experience their hottest conditions from April to June, and heat waves generally peak in May-June.
The six traditional seasons are Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemanta and Shishira.

secs.t: Monsoon research - National Monsoon Mission, nodal ministry, IMD models

x: The Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System is
a dynamic ocean-atmosphere-land model introduced in 2012
SEFS was associated with 2007, the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System with 2012 and the Multi-Model Ensemble with 2021.
About Rs 1,000 crore was invested in the Monsoon Mission and HPC, while a third-party audit estimated a return of Rs 50,000 crore.
Mission Mausam was launched on
14 January 2025
along with IMD Vision 2047.
OMT is the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean down to the
26°C isotherm
OMT is measured during January-March and has been identified as a better predictor of monsoon rainfall than sea-surface temperature.

secs.t: Mascarene High and Somali jet roles

x: The Mascarene High is
a permanent high-pressure cell in the southern Indian Ocean near Madagascar
and helps drive cross-equatorial flow.
The Mascarene High drives the cross-equatorial flow that contributes to the formation of the south-west monsoon.
The Somali jet, together with the
Somalia Current
, intensifies the monsoon winds.

secs.t: Rainfall distribution - wettest places, highest and lowest rainfall states, rain-shadow zones, reasons for low rain in Rajasthan

x: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji are in Meghalaya, while Agumbe and Hulikal in Karnataka are notable wet locations on the Western Ghats crest.
The Coromandel coast receives little southwest-monsoon rainfall and depends substantially on the northeast monsoon; its position is associated with a rain-shadow effect during the southwest monsoon.
The leeward Deccan lies in the Western Ghats’ rain shadow, Ladakh lies behind the Great Himalaya and is a cold desert, and the Hagari valley has the lowest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, below 51 cm.
The leeward Deccan
includes parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and interior Tamil Nadu and receives low rainfall because of the Western Ghats’ rain shadow.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
Indian Ocean Dipole
was being monitored as a possible offset to the influence of El Nino.
The forecast was about 90% of the long-period average, and the 43% June deficit led to contingency planning.
Annamayya
recorded the greatest stated deficit at 75.9%, followed by Prakasam at 67.5% and Chittoor at 65%.
The Sileru-Sabari valleys are the wettest parts of Andhra Pradesh, receiving about 140–152 cm, while the Hagari valley is the driest, receiving less than 51 cm.

rows.title: India - rainfall distribution, variability, El Nino linkage, drought and flood-prone areas

secs.t: Drought-prone areas - thresholds, share of land, chronic regions

x: About
68 percent
of India’s agricultural or cultivable land is drought-prone in varying degrees.
Chronic drought-prone regions include western Rajasthan, Gujarat, the rain-shadow Deccan, Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam.
Flash drought is a rapidly developing drought associated with sudden heat and lack of rainfall.
The Manual for Drought Management uses
rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators
for declaring drought.

secs.t: Flood-prone areas - share of area, basins and states, mitigation

x: The Brahmaputra valley, the Kosi and Ganga plains, and several eastern and southern coastal deltas are major flood-affected areas.
Embankments, drainage channels, sea dykes and real-time flood forecasting are recognised mitigation measures.
Himalayan rivers swell during the monsoon, and cloudburst-induced flash floods are increasing in the Himalaya and the north-east.

secs.t: Rainfall gradient - monsoon duration north vs south, cities

x: The southwest monsoon lasts for more than 120 days in
the south-western peninsula
, whereas it lasts for less than 75 days in western Rajasthan.
Rainfall decreases eastward to westward across the northern plains in the sequence Kolkata, Patna, Prayagraj, Delhi and Bikaner.
All three statements correctly describe the path and rainfall effect of the Bay of Bengal branch.

secs.t: El Nino linkage - ENSO, La Nina, deficient years, IOD offset

x: El Niño is defined here as
warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific by at least 0.5°C for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods
Six out of ten El Niño years are associated with weak Indian monsoons
, although the relationship is not absolute.
La Niña generally strengthens the monsoon and is associated with colder winters and more Bay of Bengal cyclones.

secs.t: Rainfall variability - coefficient of variation

x: Western Rajasthan, Kutch and Ladakh
generally have a high rainfall coefficient of variation above 50 percent.
There is large inter-annual variability in both the onset and withdrawal dates of the monsoon.

secs.t: IMD rainfall categories - departure bands

x: Rainfall departure of +60 percent or more is classified as
large excess
for a state or district.
A departure of -20 percent to -59 percent is classified as
deficient
The all-India seasonal sequence is deficient below 90 percent of LPA, below normal at 90–95 percent, normal at 96–104 percent, above normal at 105–110 percent and excess above 110 percent.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: In 2024–25, southwest monsoon rainfall was 681.6 mm with an 18.6 per cent increase, northeast monsoon rainfall was 278.7 mm with a 2.3 per cent decrease, total rainfall was 960.3 mm with an 11.7 per cent increase, and 2023–24 had a 16.5 per cent deficit.
The highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh occurs in
the Sileru–Sabari valleys
, where it ranges from about 140 to 152 cm.

rows.title: India - natural vegetation types and their distribution; forest cover (India State of Forest Report)
sub: Group-II S2-20: India - natural vegetation and forest types; protected areas

secs.t: Forest types → distribution and species

x: Tropical wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm of rainfall and occur in the Western Ghats, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Moist deciduous forests include teak, sal and mahua; dry deciduous forests include teak, sandalwood and Terminalia; thorn forests include Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis; tidal forests include Rhizophora and Avicennia.
Sholas are temperate forest formations of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills, generally occurring as stunted evergreen patches with grasslands in the Western Ghats.

secs.t: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

x: ISFR 2023 reported forest cover of 7,15,343 sq km or 21.76%, tree cover of 1,12,014 sq km or 3.41%, and combined forest and tree cover of 25.17%.
ISFR 2023 reported 7,15,343 sq km of forest cover and 1,12,014 sq km of tree cover, together amounting to
All three statements are correct: the total increase was about 1,445 sq km, including 156 sq km of forest cover and 1,289 sq km of tree cover outside recorded forests.
Dry deciduous forest
s are especially vulnerable to fires because of their seasonal dryness and accumulation of dry biomass.
Andhra Pradesh had the largest fire-affected area in 2023–24, measuring about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.

secs.t: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

x: Tropical moist deciduous forests account for about 37%, tropical dry deciduous forests about 28.6%, and tropical wet evergreen forests about 8%.
Tropical moist deciduous and tropical dry deciduous forests together account for approximately
of India’s forest area.
Sub-tropical chir pine occurs around 1,000–1,800 metres.
Tidal or mangrove forests occur in deltas and creeks and also in the
Andaman and Nicobar Islands

secs.t: Mangrove and tidal forests → state/UT and sites

x: Mangroves possess specialised stilt and knee roots, occur in intertidal deltaic areas and may be submerged during high tide.
The Andhra Pradesh SES 2025–26 describes AP as having the second-largest mangrove cover, while ISFR 2023 places Gujarat second.
The older estimate gives West Bengal about 50%, Gujarat about 21% and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands about 14% of India’s mangroves.

secs.t: Grassland types → region

x: Sehima-Dichanthium
grasslands are associated with black soils in peninsular and central India.
Sehima-Dichanthium occurs on black soils; Phragmites-Saccharum in marshy localities; Deschampsia-Deyeuxia in alpine regions; and Bothriochloa in high-rainfall paddy tracts.
Banni is a vast tropical grassland situated in the Kutch region of Gujarat.
Sabai grass is used for making rope and paper.

secs.t: Legal classification - Reserved, Protected, Village forests (Indian Forest Act 1927)

x: Reserved forest
s have the strictest regime.
Activities in reserved forests are barred unless expressly permitted.
In Andhra Pradesh, approximately 85.8% of forests are Reserved, 13.6% Protected and 0.6% Unclassed.
Mining is banned inside National Parks and Sanctuaries, and the Supreme Court has barred mining within 1 km of every such area unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.

secs.t: Silvicultural terms - coppice, high forest, selection system

x: Coppice
regeneration arises from stool shoots after felling and is generally managed on a short rotation, particularly for fuelwood.
A high forest is raised from seed and is managed on a long rotation, usually for timber production.
High forest provides a seed-raised, long-rotation timber crop, while the selection system retains an uneven-aged forest by removing mature trees singly or in groups.

secs.t: Himalayan altitudinal zonation - sequence, north vs south slope

x: The sequence upward is tropical sal foothills, subtropical chir pine, temperate forests, subalpine birch-rhododendron forests and alpine meadows.
Temperate Himalayan forests include
oak, deodar, blue pine and silver fir
The southern slopes are generally windward slopes and receive greater moisture, resulting in denser forest growth than on the northern slopes.
Alpine tundra occurs above the tree line in high mountain systems such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps.

secs.t: Tree species → region; evergreen vs deciduous

x: Jackfruit is an evergreen tree associated with the Western Ghats, not with Himalayan alpine meadows.
Sal is a moist deciduous species with the listed distribution, while teak occurs in central and peninsular India, including the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh.
Sandalwood is associated with dry deciduous forests of South India.

secs.t: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

x: Keoladeo National Park is situated at Bharatpur in
Rajasthan
and is also a Ramsar site.
Madhav Tiger Reserve is situated in Shivpuri,
Madhya Pradesh
, and is the 58th tiger reserve.
Project Tiger began in 1973 with 9 tiger reserves covering 18,278 sq km.
Satkosia Tiger Reserve comprises
Satkosia Gorge and Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary
; Debrigarh is not part of its stated composition.
Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla was the 56th, Ratapani the 57th in 2024, and Madhav the 58th in 2025.
Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam is described as the largest Tiger Reserve, not merely a reserve with the name stated in option 4; it covers about 5,443 square kilometres.

secs.t: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

x: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is the second home for cheetahs and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve is the third.
The Great Indian Bustard is associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat, numbers fewer than 150, and is protected through the modified power-line directions.
Project Cheetah is described as the world's first
intercontinental translocation of a large carnivore

secs.t: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set a target of
of the total area under forest and tree cover.
The National Forest Policy, 1988 prescribed a target of
forest and tree cover in hills and mountains.
India’s forest and tree cover is stated as
, compared with the National Forest Policy target of 33%.
CAMPA
manages the compensatory afforestation funds.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh forests are mainly dry deciduous, and Nallamala is the biggest forest tract in the State.
Mangroves together with littoral vegetation account for
418 sq km
in Andhra Pradesh.
The plan proposes bringing
gaur from Central India and tigresses from Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
to NSTR.
Andhra Pradesh has three National Parks, thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries, one Tiger Reserve, one Biosphere Reserve and the Koundinya Elephant Reserve.
Sri Venkateswara National Park was the first, established in 1989; Papikonda is the largest and Rajiv Gandhi is the smallest among the three.
The eviction issue in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve has raised concerns regarding
tribal rights

secs.t: National parks → state/UT and landscape

x: Tadoba-Andhari National Park
is located in Maharashtra’s Chandrapur district and has a dry deciduous landscape.
Pench National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, inspired Rudyard Kipling’s
The Jungle Book
Dachigam National Park in Jammu and Kashmir is noted for the Hangul, or Kashmir stag.
Campbell Bay National Park
is located in Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

secs.t: FIRST and order of establishment

x: Nilgiri was established in 1986, Nanda Devi in 1988, Gulf of Mannar in 1989 and Pachmarhi in 1999.
Dibru-Saikhowa
is the smallest listed biosphere reserve by area, covering 765 square kilometres.
The Great Rann of Kutch is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve, with an area of approximately 12,454 square kilometres.

secs.t: Protected area counts - states with most NPs, PA share of area

x: India has 573
wildlife sanctuaries
, compared with 109 national parks, 127 conservation reserves and 75 community reserves.
The cited figure states that Tiger Reserves span about 84,488 square kilometres, approximately
2.6 per cent
of India’s area.
The National Parks covered 44,374 sq km, while Wildlife Sanctuaries covered 1,22,420 sq km.

secs.t: Natural World Heritage Sites of India

x: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 and is a mixed World Heritage Site.
The Western Ghats World Heritage property extends across six States, not seven.
Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks were inscribed in 1988; the property was extended in 2005.

secs.t: World-famous national parks → country and feature

x: Serengeti National Park is in Tanzania and is famous for the great wildebeest migration.
Banff National Park is in Canada and is located in the Rocky Mountains.
Kruger National Park is located in South Africa and is known as a Big Five savanna park.

secs.t: PA categories under WPA 1972 - NP vs WLS vs conservation and community reserves

x: Community Reserve land is private or community land voluntarily offered for conservation, and it must not be inside a National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary or Conservation Reserve.
Mining is banned inside National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries and within
1 kilometre
of their boundary, unless a larger Eco-Sensitive Zone has been notified.

secs.t: Species → protected-area habitat

x: The Great Indian Bustard is protected in Desert National Park of Rajasthan and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh.
The Great Indian Bustard population is stated to be below 150, Rollapadu is one of its habitats, and the 2024 Supreme Court order addressed underground power lines for its conservation.
The listed habitats of the snow leopard are the
Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve and Kibber

secs.t: Wildlife sanctuaries → state/district

x: Mahuadanr Wildlife Sanctuary is in Latehar district of Jharkhand, not Almora in Uttarakhand.
Askot in Pithoragarh lies north of Binsar in Almora; Mahuadanr in Jharkhand lies north of Sitanadi in Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Following the 2025 ruling in A. John Kennedy v. State of Tamil Nadu, Tamil Nadu issued eviction notices concerning forest land inside the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.
The Supreme Court ordered eviction of encroachers from Agasthyamalai in June 2026, and Tamil Nadu subsequently issued eviction notices after the A. John Kennedy case.

x: JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary/Surha Tal and Shekha Jheel are in Uttar Pradesh, Khichan and Menar are in Rajasthan, and Kopra Reservoir is in Chhattisgarh.
Glaw Lake lies within Kamlang Tiger Reserve, supports the white-bellied heron and is Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site.
The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran, for the
conservation and wise use of wetlands

secs.t: Ramsar Convention - purpose, host town, wetland definition

x: The Ramsar definition includes all four categories: marshes, fens, peatlands, natural or artificial water, waters of different salinities and qualifying shallow marine water.
The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites where ecological character has changed, is changing or is likely to change adversely.
India's wetlands listed in the Montreux Record are
Keoladeo and Loktak

secs.t: Important Bird Areas and bird mass-mortality events → species (Telineelapuram, Telukunchi, Sambhar)

x: Important Bird Areas are a BirdLife International designation, with the Bombay Natural History Society as its Indian partner.
Telineelapuram and Telukunchi in Srikakulam are Important Bird Areas for breeding
painted storks and spot-billed pelicans
The mass death of migratory birds at Sambhar Lake was attributed to
avian botulism
The Rushikulya mouth hosts the
olive ridley arribada
, the mass nesting congregation of olive ridley turtles.

secs.t: Bird sanctuaries → state/location - FIRST established

x: Vedanthangal
Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu is regarded as India's oldest water-bird sanctuary, established in 1858.
Bharatpur is Keoladeo in Rajasthan with both Ramsar and UNESCO World Heritage status; Pitti is in Lakshadweep and Sultanpur is in Gurugram, Haryana.
The Andhra Pradesh sanctuaries listed are
Nelapattu, Pulicat and Kolleru
; Pulicat and Nelapattu are associated with Tirupati, while Kolleru is associated with Eluru.

secs.t: Species-specific sanctuaries → key species (National Chambal, Bhitarkanika, Gahirmatha, Gir)

x: National Chambal Sanctuary, spread across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, is noted for the
Gharial and Gangetic dolphin
Bhitarkanika in Odisha is known for its saltwater crocodiles and mangrove ecosystems.
Gahirmatha in Odisha is a marine sanctuary famous for the
mass nesting of Olive ridley turtles
Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with the
Great Indian Bustard and blackbuck

secs.t: Migratory birds → migration pattern (Bar-headed goose, Amur falcon) and Central Asian Flyway

x: The Amur falcon migrates from southeast Siberia and northern China, stops in Nagaland and subsequently winters in southern Africa.
The Amur falcon undertakes
the longest raptor migration
, travelling from eastern Asia to southern Africa through its Indian stopover.
The specific October–November stopover around Doyang and Pangti establishes Nagaland's role in the Amur falcon's migration.

secs.t: Elephant reserves - Project Elephant, count, states with most reserves

x: Project Elephant was launched in
February 1992
Elephant reserves can overlap with Tiger Reserves, Wildlife Sanctuaries and reserved forests.
The 2017 count estimated India's elephant population at 29,964.
Odisha has three elephant reserves:
Mayurbhanj, Mahanadi and Sambalpur
Carbon stored in elephant reserves rose by
, with the increase attributed mainly to expanded protected forest.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A growing share of India's tigers is living outside notified reserves, which raises the possibility of conflict with human communities.
The correct chronological order is Corbett as the first Tiger Reserve in 1973, Chilika as the first Ramsar site in 1981, Project Lion in 2020, and Glaw Lake as the 101st Ramsar site in 2026.

rows.title: India - soil types, characteristics and distribution; soil erosion and conservation
sub: Group-II S2-19: India - soils: types, distribution and conservation

secs.t: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

x: Exam angle: "New alluvium is called..." (Khadar); which state has laterite.
Exam angle: Khadar = new alluvium, Bhangar = old. Pairing black soil with basalt and laterite with leaching is asked every year.
The classification recognises
eight
major soil types: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.
Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil, covers the Indo-Gangetic Plain, deltas and coasts, and is well suited to irrigated farming.
Black soil has more than 62% clay, retains moisture well, develops deep summer cracks and is known for its self-ploughing character.
Iron oxide
gives red soil its characteristic red colour; hydration may make it appear yellow.
Red and yellow soils develop mainly from crystalline igneous rocks, especially granite and gneiss, under relatively low rainfall conditions.
Laterite soil occurs in the Western Ghats, Rajmahal Hills and North-Eastern states, besides other regions including parts of Andhra Pradesh.
Reh, kallar, usar and thur are among the local names used for saline and alkaline soils; other names include rakar and chopan.
Peaty soils develop in waterlogged, humid conditions where heavy rainfall and high humidity promote the accumulation of organic matter.
Peaty and marshy soils are generally unsuitable for cultivation because persistent waterlogging restricts aeration.

secs.t: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

x: Black soil
has the highest moisture-retention capacity, owing largely to its high clay content.
Black soil is neutral to alkaline and rich in calcium, potassium and magnesium but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus; red soil is poor in lime, humus and phosphoric acid.
Laterite is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium and contains excess iron oxide and potash.

secs.t: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

x: Rills are small water-cut channels, wind erosion involves the three stated movements, and tunnel erosion removes soil below the surface and can form sinkholes.
Parts of Australia and Africa are associated with tunnel erosion, in which subsurface removal may create sinkholes, not sheet erosion.
The usual progression of increasing soil loss is splash, sheet, rill and gully erosion.
Wind erosion is worst where soil is bare, dry and fine-textured and winds are strong and frequent.
Sheet erosion
is the uniform removal of a thin surface layer by overland flow.
Straw checkerboards are used to
stabilise dunes
and control movement of desert sands.

secs.t: Soil conservation methods

x: Contour ploughing slows runoff along contour lines; terracing creates steps; check dams trap sediment and limit gully growth; shelter belts reduce wind speed.
Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-resistant crops, such as grass, with row crops to reduce wind- and water-induced erosion.
Conservation agriculture uses minimum or zero tillage, retains crop residues and uses mulch for soil stability.
IWMP began in 2009–10 and was merged in
into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY.

secs.t: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

x: Mining-led deforestation is associated with
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Climate change is a general additional driver of land degradation and is not confined only to Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
The assessment reported worsening sustainable practices in 58% of assessments and improvement in only about 10%.

secs.t: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

x: Rainfall intensity
matters more than total annual rainfall because intense bursts can exceed the soil’s infiltration capacity and generate runoff.
A 2026 study paired RUSLE with GIS for studying erosion in the hills of
North-East India
Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, whereas steep slopes are more prone to losing carbon-rich topsoil.

secs.t: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

x: Peaty and marshy soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity where waterlogging permits organic matter to accumulate.
Peaty and marshy soils occur in Kerala, the Sundarbans, coastal Odisha and Tamil Nadu, north Bihar and Almora.
Peaty soils are black, heavy and highly acidic, forming under waterlogged, humid conditions.

secs.t: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

x: Gypsum is used to reclaim alkaline or sodic soils, while lime is used for acidic soils.
Karewas are old lake-bed deposits of unconsolidated gravel and mud.
Karewas are famous for saffron cultivation around Pampore.

secs.t: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

x: Unscientific irrigation practices combined with inadequate drainage promote salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging.
The stated projection is that
of the world's arable land could be affected by 2050 if soil resources are not preserved.
The affected states listed are
Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Gypsum is used with water management to reclaim alkaline soil.

secs.t: Soil composition - components for plant growth, organic matter and water holding

x: A good soil is approximately composed of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air by volume.
Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, improves infiltration and supports microbial activity.
The reported decline in India's average soil organic carbon was from
over 70 years.

secs.t: ICAR/USDA classification - soil orders by area, soil profile horizons

x: The shares are Inceptisols 39.7%, Entisols 28.1%, Alfisols 13.6% and Vertisols 8.5%, giving the order
C, B, A, D
All six pairings are correct: O is organic litter, A is humus-rich topsoil, E is leached, B is the accumulation or subsoil horizon, C is weathered parent material and R is bedrock.

secs.t: Soil Health Card scheme and soil testing

x: The Soil Health Card tests nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron, pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon.
The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.
The programme targets 7,500 Village-Level Soil Testing Labs during 2023–26, provides ₹1.5 lakh assistance per laboratory, and is complemented by ICAR's pilot of rapid spectroscopic soil analysis.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Kurnool is promoting Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing on a target area of 92,000 acres along with Jeevamrutham to conserve soil moisture.
The approximate shares are red soils 60% or more, black soils 25%, deltaic alluvium 5–6%, and laterite soils about 1%, giving the stated descending order.
Deterioration in soil management reinforces, rather than eliminates, the need for sustainable agricultural practices.

rows.title: India - rocks and mineral belts; distribution of metallic and non-metallic minerals
sub: Group-II S2-30: Mineral resources of India - metallic and non-metallic; mineral belts

secs.t: Metallic minerals → leading states and mines - reserves vs production rank

x: Sukinda Valley is an important chromite area, but the option is not correctly matched because the stated mineral–area combination is incomplete in the context of the listed principal associations; Hassan is the Karnataka chromite area.
Hutti is a major Karnataka gold mine, Kolar is closed, and Ramagiri and Jonnagiri are important Andhra Pradesh gold areas.
Magnetite
is the best-grade iron ore, containing up to about 70–72 per cent iron, and is magnetic.
Magnetite has up to about 70–72 per cent iron, haematite about 60–70 per cent, limonite 40–60 per cent and siderite is the lowest-grade ore.

secs.t: Mineral belts - regions and their ferrous / non-ferrous minerals

x: The North-Eastern Plateau belt is rich in
coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper
The belt contains non-ferrous minerals such as copper and lead-zinc, along with gypsum, salt, limestone and Gujarat petroleum.
The Central belt covering Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh contains iron ore, including Bailadila, manganese including Balaghat, coal and limestone.
The Southern belt includes Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and is associated with iron ore, gold, manganese, chromite and lignite; Neyveli is a major lignite area.
Bauxite mining in areas such as Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli and Paderu raises issues concerning Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group rights and the ecology of the Eastern Ghats.

secs.t: Critical and strategic minerals - list, rare earths, lithium, overseas agreements (KABIL)

x: All three statements are correct: coking coal is a notified critical and strategic mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957, and over 90 per cent of its reserves are in Jharia.
KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Limited, Hindustan Copper Limited and Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.
KABIL holds 15,703 hectares in
Catamarca
, Argentina, for lithium exploration.
A total of 46 critical and strategic blocks were sold in six tranches; the seventh tranche, comprising 19 blocks, opened on 23 March 2026.
GSI’s ‘Uncover India’ project is being carried out with
Geoscience Australia
to probe deep-seated deposits.
The recent amendment removed captive-sale limits and also requires State approval for adding a critical mineral to a lease within 30 days.
The Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (
APMDC
) is to facilitate value addition following comprehensive mineral mapping.

secs.t: Mica - host rocks and associated minerals, top states and mines

x: Mica occurs in pegmatite veins hosted by granite, gneiss and schist.
Phlogopite and muscovite
are the main mica minerals; phlogopite is magnesium mica.
The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.
SPSR Nellore is associated with quartz, feldspar, silica sand and vermiculite;
bauxite
is not included in this listed association.

secs.t: Non-metallic minerals → states and uses

x: Limestone
is used in cement manufacture and as a flux.
Dolomite is used as a flux in steel production and in refractories.
The listed states and Kerala sands are noted occurrences of dolomite, sillimanite and kyanite respectively.
Mangampet in Kadapa is among the world's largest deposits of
barytes
A record 30 mineral blocks became operational in FY 2025–26, marking a first.

secs.t: State shares in value of mineral production - ranking of mineral states

x: Odisha
had the highest share, at 44.11%, in the value of mineral production in 2021–22.
Madhya Pradesh accounted for 2.96%, not 4.36%.
India exported approximately
46 million tonnes
of iron ore in 2023–24; the corresponding figure for 2022–23 was about 21 million tonnes.
Article 297 vests offshore minerals in the Union

secs.t: Types of mineral deposits - placer, veins/lodes, sedimentary beds

x: Placer deposits accumulate in alluvial sands in valleys and at the base of hills.
Gold, tin and platinum
are associated with placer deposits formed in alluvial sands.
All three pairs are correctly matched.
Veins or lodes are mineral deposits filling cracks and faults in igneous and metamorphic rocks.

secs.t: Ores → metal

x: Cinnabar is the ore of mercury.
Hematite, magnetite and limonite are iron ores, while ilmenite and rutile are titanium-bearing minerals commonly found in beach sands.
Monazite is an important source of
thorium and rare earths
and occurs in coastal sands, including those of Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

secs.t: Mining law - MMDR Act 1957 and amendments, National Mineral Policy 2019

x: Major minerals in the First Schedule are regulated by the Centre, whereas minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the States.
The Bill, passed in August 2026, sought uniform rates by restricting States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land.
The decision upheld the formula based on an Average Sale Price including royalty, DMF and NMET; royalty was held not to be a tax.
PMKKKY uses District Mineral Foundation funds for the welfare of mining-affected people and areas and provides for a yearly audit.

secs.t: Mines → mineral

x: Koderma is associated with mica, Bailadila with iron ore, Khetri with copper and Zawar with lead-zinc.
Turamdih in Jharkhand is a uranium mine.
All four pairs are correctly matched.
Thummalapalli in YSR Kadapa is associated with uranium.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Swarnagiri Gold Mine is in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool, covers 597.820 hectares, lies in the Jonnagiri greenstone belt of the Eastern Dharwar Craton and has a 30-year open-pit lease.

All three statements are correct: Geomysore developed the mine with Rs 405 crore, the royalty payable to Andhra Pradesh is 4 percent, and the mine lies in the Jonnagiri greenstone belt of the Eastern Dharwar Craton.
The Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt contains khondalite and charnockite and holds deposits of bauxite, manganese and graphite.
The Boksampalli blocks in Anantapur cover 1,740 hectares, contain gold, PGE and iron ore, and lie in the Ramagiri-Penakacherla greenstone belt.
The MMDR Amendment 2026 has been criticised for eroding state fiscal autonomy, and bauxite mining conflicts involve the FCA, FRA and PVTG rights.

rows.title: India - earthquake zones, landslide-prone areas, cyclone-prone coasts; seismic zoning map

secs.t: Seismic zoning map - number of zones, revisions after major earthquakes (Killari), zones merged

x: Exam angle: "zones merged" (I into II), and Zone VI as a proposed-then-withdrawn change.
The proposed BIS revision used
Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment
, abbreviated as PSHA.
The Centre rolled back the proposed revision in March 2026 after criticism concerning its methodology and cost; consequently, the four-zone map continued to apply.

secs.t: Cyclone-prone coasts - east vs west coast frequency, most vulnerable states, NDMA-IMD hazard-prone districts

x: Cyclones affect both coasts, but the east coast receives far more because the Bay of Bengal generates about four times as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea.

All three statements are correct: 13 coastal States and Union Territories, 84 coastal districts and seven cyclone warning centres are identified in the national profile; Visakhapatnam is among the warning-centre locations.

secs.t: Landslide hazard zonation - terms and most-prone regions

x: Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous units according to actual or potential susceptibility, hazard or risk.
The Himalaya
, including Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh, is highly prone because of young fragile geology and active tectonics.
The Western Ghats, including the Nilgiris, have steep escarpments and receive orographic rainfall, increasing landslide susceptibility.

secs.t: Major disasters in India → type and place

x: Koyna occurred in 1967, Killari in 1993, Bhuj in 2001 and the Indian Ocean Tsunami in 2004.
The 1993 Killari earthquake in Latur, Maharashtra, was an
intraplate earthquake
The snow avalanche at Badrinath-Mana resulted in the death of Border Roads Organisation workers.
The Badrinath–Mana stretch lies along
NH-7
, where settlement growth is increasing hanging-glacier and avalanche risk.

secs.t: Vulnerability profile of India - share of land prone to hazards

x: Approximately
59 per cent
of India’s land is exposed to moderate-to-severe earthquake risk.
Approximately 5,700 km of India’s nearly 7,516 km coastline is exposed to cyclone and tsunami hazards.
Approximately
68 per cent
of India’s cultivable area is drought-prone.
The relationship is expressed as
hazard multiplied by vulnerability equals disaster

secs.t: Natural hazards → region matching and reservoir-induced seismicity (Koyna)

x: All four associations are correct.
Koyna Dam
is the classic Indian example of reservoir-induced seismicity; significant tremors were associated with the reservoir in 1967.
The Geological Survey of India monitors crustal strain through 34 GNSS stations.

secs.t: Tsunami-prone coasts and warning centres (INCOIS)

x: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre is located at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Seismic monitoring, ocean buoys and sirens are used for tsunami warning.
India’s east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the most exposed areas to tsunami risk.
ISRO’s DMS maps coastal vulnerability and runs the NDEM database.

secs.t: Building codes and BIS seismic standards

x: IS 13920 covers ductile detailing, which improves the earthquake resistance of structures.
IS 1893 specifies seismic design criteria, IS 13920 covers ductile detailing, and the National Building Code is applicable to building safety provisions.
The Building Materials and Technology Promotion Council (
BMTPC
) publishes the Vulnerability Atlas.
Safer Himalayan building codes have faced delays because of the cost involved in implementing them.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The revised seismic map containing Zone VI was withdrawn in
March 2026
The project has an outlay of ₹507.37 crore, covers 20 States and 81 districts, and operates through panchayats.
APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister and runs the State Emergency Operations Centre
The debate concerns the use of probabilistic seismic hazard assessment for zoning and the associated cost implications for the built environment.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - location, extent, districts, physiographic divisions

secs.t: Area of AP - rank among states before and after bifurcation, share of India's area

x: Exam angle: read whether the question asks about "States" or "States and UTs".
Andhra Pradesh covers about
of India’s area.
Andhra Pradesh was eighth until 31 October 2019 and became the seventh-largest State after Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory.
Undivided Andhra Pradesh covered about
between 1956 and 2014.

secs.t: Districts - erstwhile vs post-2022 districts; largest/smallest; new district → HQ and mandal count

x: Markapuram
district was formed from the Markapuram and Kanigiri revenue divisions of western Prakasam district.
Polavaram district was created primarily for the
rehabilitation and resettlement of villages affected by the Polavaram project
The correct sequence is 20 districts in 1956, 23 districts after the 1970-79 additions, 13 districts in 2014, and 26 districts after the 2022 reorganisation.

secs.t: Regions - Coastal Andhra, Uttarandhra, Rayalaseema: districts in each

x: Uttarandhra, also called Kalinga Andhra, comprises
ASR, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam
Uttarandhra had 6 districts, the rest of Coastal Andhra had 12, and Rayalaseema had 8 districts.
Coastal Andhra comprises 18 districts, including the six districts of Uttarandhra.
Rayalaseema has low population density because of recurring drought conditions.
Rayalaseema borders
Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana

secs.t: Physiographic divisions of AP - coastal plains, Eastern Ghats, Rayalaseema plateau, oldest landmass

x: The Rayalaseema plateau forms part of the Deccan and consists of drought-prone uplands.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake of about 305 sq km between the two deltas, while Pulicat is a saltwater lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.
Archaean Dharwar rocks occur in
Anantapur, Chittoor and Kadapa
and are more than 2,500 million years old.

secs.t: Revenue divisions and mandals - counts
AP Reorganisation Act 2014 - territorial changes (Polavaram-affected mandals)

x: The seven transferred mandals were
Bhadrachalam, Kunavaram, Chintur, Velerupadu, Kukunoor, V.R. Puram and Polavaram
The seven mandals came from Khammam, the transfer followed the 2014 Polavaram ordinance and amendment, and Chinturu division is now in Polavaram district.
In 1960, the Pataskar award transferred most of Tiruttani taluk to Tamil Nadu and some villages of Tiruvallur to Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: Markapuram and Polavaram are the newest districts as of 31 December 2025, and both appear in APSDMA alerts covering 28 districts dated 6 June and 13 September 2026.
Coastal Andhra is characterised here by its river deltas, dominant share of farm output and highest population density.
The current 28-district structure includes the new districts of
Polavaram and Markapuram

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - coastline, deltas, hill ranges (Eastern Ghats, Nallamala, Seshachalam)
sub: Group-II S2-21: Andhra Pradesh - major physiographic features and coastline

secs.t: Eastern Ghats in AP - local names by district and northern/southern limits

x: Exam angle: "Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam are called ___" and "Seshachalam belongs to ___" are direct recall questions.
Papikondalu is associated with the Godavari gorge in the East and West Godavari and ASR-Eluru region.
The Godavari and Krishna separate the northern Eastern Ranges from the southern Kadapa Ranges.
In Andhra Pradesh, the Eastern Ghats begin with
Mahendragiri
in the north.
Beyond Andhra Pradesh, the Eastern Ghats pass through the
Javadi and Shevaroy hills
and join the Western Ghats near the Nilgiris.
Papikonda National Park covers 1,012.86 sq km.
Erramala, associated with Kurnool and Nandyal, divides the Krishna basin in the north from the Penna basin in the south.

secs.t: Coastline - recalculated length, rank among states, end points, coastal districts

x: Exam angle: "recalculated" questions want 1,053.07 km; "2nd longest" is the pre-2025 answer.
Exam angle: the 2025 paper offered both 1,068.69 and 1,053.07; the first is Tamil Nadu's figure.
The increase resulted from GIS retracing at 1:250,000 scale and does not represent an actual physical change in India's coastline.
The 1,053.07 km figure was obtained in the 2023–24 remeasurement associated with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

secs.t: Hill ranges → districts (Nallamala, Seshachalam-Tirumala, Velikonda, Palakonda, Erramala)

x: The Nallamala range lies between the
Krishna and Penna
basins.
The Chenchus, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group living in the Nallamala region, are associated with the ITDA at
Srisailam
Seshachalam is an Eastern Ghats range containing the Tirumala hills and red sanders forests, and it forms the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve.

secs.t: Eastern Ghats character - continuity, erosion, hills where they meet the Western Ghats

x: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and eroded hills, dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri rivers.
Khondalite and charnockite
are the characteristic rocks mentioned for the Eastern Ghats.
The
Vamsadhara, Nagavali and Sabari
rivers rise in the Eastern Ghats.
The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the
Nilgiris near Gudalur
through the Biligirirangan and Male Mahadeshwara hills.

secs.t: Coastal lakes, lagoons and barrier islands → district (Pulicat-Sriharikota, Kolleru, Uppalapadu)

x: Sriharikota Island
separates Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal.
Kolleru Lake is associated with
Eluru
district; it lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.
Uppalapadu is in Guntur district and is a bird sanctuary tank known for pelicans and painted storks.
Sambhar and Didwana are in Rajasthan, Vembanad is in Kerala, and Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh's major freshwater lake.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake of approximately
305 sq km

secs.t: Hill stations of AP → district

x: Lambasingi is in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, at Chintapalle.
Horsley Hills is located in
Annamayya
district near Madanapalle and the Karnataka border.
Maredumilli is associated with the Polavaram district arrangement through the Rampachodavaram agency division.
Talakona is in Tirupati district and lies in the Seshachalam Hills.
Ethipothala Falls lies on the Chandravanka near Nagarjuna Sagar in Palnadu district.

secs.t: Coastal plain name for the AP coast and coastal vegetation fringes (Coringa, Krishna estuary)

x: The AP coastal plain is approximately 950 km long, about 60 km wide on average, rises up to 150 metres and is called the Rice Bowl.
The Andhra coastal plain is an emergent, broad coast built by river deposition and characterised by large deltas.
Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary contains mangrove fringes near the Godavari estuary in Kakinada.
Dolphin’s Nose is a 335-metre feature of the Yarada Hills that shelters Visakhapatnam port.

secs.t: Deltas - Godavari and Krishna delta extent, delta districts

x: The Godavari delta is known as Konaseema; its central delta is about 150 km wide and is noted for coconut and banana cultivation.
The Godavari delta districts are
Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari and Kakinada
The Krishna delta is among India’s most fertile zones and includes Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.

secs.t: Highest peaks of AP

x: Jindhagada
, located near Araku, is identified in Andhra Pradesh publications as the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.
Arma Konda is 1,680 m, Galikonda is 1,643 m and Sintram Gutta is 1,620 m.
Mahendragiri is located in
Gajapati
district of Odisha.
Arma Konda, also known as Sitamma Konda, is recorded as 1,680 metres high and located in the ASR district of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: AP area and position

x: Andhra Pradesh covers about
4.96 percent
of India’s area, with a total area of approximately 1,62,970 square kilometres.
The 82.5° E meridian passes through
Kakinada
in Andhra Pradesh and is associated with Indian Standard Time.
Yanam, a Puducherry enclave of about 30 square kilometres, is located in
the Godavari delta
of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Physiographic regions of AP - districts in each

x: From east to west and from the coast towards the interior, the broad sequence is Coastal plains, Eastern Ghats and Western plateau.
All four statements correctly describe the Eastern Ghats hill region of Andhra Pradesh, including its districts, elevation, forests and tribal belts.
Chittoor, Kadapa and Annamayya
are identified as the Mysore plateau extension within the Western plateau region.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Gaur are to be translocated from Central India to NSTR and Nallamala from September 2026 with support from the Wildlife Institute of India.
NSTR was established in 1983, covers about 5,443 square kilometres, and extends across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
The NCCR finding places east-coast erosion at
, compared with 30% for the west coast.
Forest-fire alerts were issued for
Horsley Hills and the Chittoor–Annamayya ranges
, especially during the April–May period.
