rows.title: India - Scheduled Tribe population: distribution, major tribes and tribal regions
sub: Group-II S2-59: Tribal groups of India - distribution and characteristics

secs.t: Major tribes → state/UT and habitat (Gaddis, Jarawas, Onge, Shompen, Santhals, Bhutias, Bhils, Gonds, Todas, Changpa, Khasis, Birhors)

x: Exam angle: the APPSC 2023 match was Gaddis-HP, Jarawas-A&N, Santhals-Jharkhand, Bhutias-Sikkim. Jarawa and Onge = A&N.
Exam angle: 4-pair matching of tribe with state, and "odd one out" by region.
The classification given identifies the Sentinelese as likely the world's only surviving uncontacted Palaeolithic people, not as a Negrito group.
The Census 2011 count of about 1.7 crore out of roughly 10.4 crore STs is closer to 16%; the 38% figure appears in some sources but is not consistent with that Census calculation.
The Onge live in Little Andaman, the Shompen in Great Nicobar and the Sentinelese on North Sentinel Island.
The Sentinelese inhabit North Sentinel Island, which has been maintained as a tribal reserve with a no-contact policy since 1956.
All four associations are correct: Santhals are linked with Santhal Parganas, Gonds with Gondwana and Bastar, Bhils with the Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura belt, and Todas with the Nilgiris.
Changpas inhabit the Changthang plateau of Ladakh, practise nomadic pastoralism involving pashmina goats and yaks, and have ST recognition since 1989.

secs.t: Largest tribes by population and states with highest/lowest ST share or number

x: In Andhra Pradesh, tribal settlements are concentrated in the Eastern Ghats, the north coastal hill tracts, the Godavari basin and the Nallamala belt.
About 89.97 per cent of the Scheduled Tribe population was rural, and its sex ratio was 990 females per 1,000 males.
The literacy rate among Scheduled Tribes was about 59 per cent, compared with about
73 per cent
for the country as a whole.
All three statements are correct: 705 groups are cited across 30 States and Union Territories, Odisha has the most notified tribes, and Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population.
The stated figures are 705 notified ethnic groups, 10.45 crore persons, 8.6 per cent of the population and residence over 15 per cent of the area; Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population.
The tribal settlements of Andhra Pradesh mainly follow the forested uplands of
the Eastern Ghats and the Nallamala belt
, rather than the deltas.

secs.t: Committees on tribal status → chairperson and focus (Xaxa, Bhuria, Lokur, Dhebar)

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 asked the chair of the 2013 high-level committee - Virginius Xaxa.
The Virginius Xaxa Committee, whose report concerned 2013–14, suggested measures including
agro-based training institutions, labour-intensive processing, organic farming and eco-forestry

Verrier Elwin dealt with Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks; Dhebar examined tribal conditions and land alienation; Lokur dealt with ST criteria; and Dilip Singh Bhuria was associated with PESA 1996.
The Bhuria Committee of 1991 led to PESA 1996, whereas the Bhuria Commission of 2002–04 focused on tribal advancement, funds, land reform, and tribal women and children.
The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large and backwardness.
The correct sequence is Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953), Elwin Committee (1959), U.N. Dhebar Commission (1960–61) and Lokur Committee (1965).

secs.t: Constitutional framework - Fifth vs Sixth Schedule areas and states, Article 164 tribal welfare minister states, Article 342

x: The
94th Amendment Act, 2006
removed Bihar and added Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh to the relevant provision.
The Fifth Schedule concerns Scheduled Areas, while the Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous districts and regions in specified north-eastern States.
The Fifth Schedule provides for the Governor's special powers and a Tribes Advisory Council in relation to Scheduled Areas.
Article 244(2)
applies the Sixth Schedule provisions concerning autonomous districts to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Article 164(1), through its proviso, provides for a separate tribal-welfare minister in
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to the communities notified under
Article 342

secs.t: ST list amendments - Scheduled Tribes Orders and recent inclusions (J&K)

x: The stated criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.
Gujjar
s, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Sippis were added to the Jammu and Kashmir ST list in 1991.
The proposed ST (Valley) tier covered all six listed communities: Chutia, Koch-Rajbongshi, Matak, Moran, Tai Ahom and Tea Tribes.

secs.t: PVTGs - count, criteria, examples by state, PM-JANMAN

x: The four criteria include pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and declining or stagnant population.
Great Andamanese are from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chenchu from Andhra Pradesh, Toda from Tamil Nadu and Baiga from Madhya Pradesh.
Great Andamanese are associated with Strait Island, Onge with Little Andaman, Sentinelese with North Sentinel and Shompen with Great Nicobar.
Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge and Sentinelese are classified as Negrito groups, whereas Shompen is classified as Mongoloid.
Bharia
of Madhya Pradesh were the first PVTG to receive habitat rights, followed by Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: Tribal regions of India → tribes (north-eastern, central, southern, island zones; Bharmour, Nilgiris, Bastar)

x: Kadar
is a southern tribe associated with the Anamalai Hills.

The western group includes Bhil, Mina and Warli; the southern group includes Chenchu, Koya and Konda Reddi; island groups include Jarawa, Onge and Shompen; and Khasi, Garo and Naga belong to the North-East.
Korku is associated with the Satpura–Melghat region of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, not the Nilgiri Hills.

secs.t: Tribes → sub-groups and odd-one-out by region (Gond, Baiga, Korku, Muria, Kadar)

x: Muria and Maria are Gond sub-groups associated with the Bastar region, and Muria is known for the ghotul youth dormitory.
Kadar are forest foragers of the Anamalai Hills of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Gond, Baiga and Muria are associated with central or middle India, whereas
Kadar
is a southern tribe of the Anamalai Hills.

secs.t: States/UTs with no ST population

x: Punjab
, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have no notified Scheduled Tribe population.

secs.t: Tribal language preservation - dictionaries and tribal language initiatives

x: Santali was included in the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, and is written in the Ol Chiki script.
Adi Vaani is
India’s first AI translation platform for tribal languages
and covers Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santali.
Dictionaries are being compiled for the endangered
Mavila and Malaveduvan
languages of Kerala.

secs.t: Tribal culture → tribe (festivals, sub-groups, traditional livelihoods)

x: Among the
Khasi
, the youngest daughter traditionally inherits family property.
Raj, Madia and Dhurve are identified as sub-groups of the
Gond
tribe.
Niyam Raja and the Niyamgiri festival are associated with the
Dongria Kondh
The Munda are associated with the Magha/Ba festival and sasandiri burial stones.
Bison-horn headgear is associated with the
Bison Horn Maria
, a Gond sub-tribe of Chhattisgarh.

secs.t: Tribal development schemes - PM-JANMAN, EMRS, FRA 2006, PESA 1996

x: PMJVM is implemented by TRIFED and uses Van Dhan Vikas Kendras for
Minor Forest Produce
-related activities.
A total of 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras had been sanctioned under PMJVM as reported in August 2026.
PESA provides that Scheduled Tribes receive at least
50 percent
of the seats in the relevant local self-government arrangement.

PESA provides for representation in proportion to population, at least 50% ST representation, all chairperson posts for STs, and possible State nomination of unrepresented tribes to block and district bodies.

x: The Shompen first voted in the
2024 Lok Sabha election
, in the Andaman and Nicobar parliamentary constituency.
The debate concerns competing Jain and Santhal claims over the religious significance of Parasnath and Marang Buru.
The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh cover 16,267.63 square kilometres, amount to 10.15 percent of the State's area and extend across five districts.

rows.title: India - rural and urban components; level of urbanisation and its regional pattern

secs.t: Components of urban growth - natural increase, rural-urban migration, reclassification of settlements

x: Urban growth occurs through natural increase, rural-to-urban migration, reclassification of settlements and expansion of town boundaries to include villages.
Census towns increased from 1,362 in 2001 to 3,894 in 2011, indicating the importance of reclassification in urban growth.
In 2011, India had 7,935 towns, comprising
4,041 statutory towns and 3,894 census towns

secs.t: Drivers of urbanisation - industry, trade, rural push factors

x: Industrialisation and employment opportunities
attract people towards cities and therefore operate as pull factors.
Industrialisation, trade and commerce, better health and education
, and transport links attract people towards cities.
A failed monsoon can reduce rural employment and push people to seek livelihoods in cities, making it a
push factor
Rakesh Mohan identified metropolitanisation, commercialisation and rural or subsistence urbanisation.

secs.t: Villages - number of villages and rural population share

x: Of the 6,40,867 villages, 5,97,608 were inhabited, representing approximately
About
83.3 crore
people lived in rural India in 2011.

secs.t: Regional pattern - southern and western vs eastern and north-eastern states

x: The southern and western group of relatively more urbanised States includes
Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Gujarat
Low urbanisation is associated with the stagnant middle and lower Ganga plains, Telangana, unirrigated western Rajasthan, north-eastern tribal hills and flood-prone peninsular tracts.
The stagnant middle and lower Ganga plains are identified as a region of low urbanisation; Goa, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat are relatively more urbanised.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: EAC-PM satellite data suggested that India's urbanisation could have been 63% in 2015, considerably higher than the Census estimate of 31%.

The 16th Finance Commission projected 41% urbanisation by 2031, raised the urban bodies' share of local grants from 36% to 45%, and the 41% projection is lower than the EAC-PM satellite-based 2015 estimate of 63%.

rows.title: Racial groups of India - Risley and Guha classifications
sub: Group-II S2-58: Racial groups of India - classifications of Risley and Guha

secs.t: Racial type → region/community (Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals, Nordic; Dravidian label)

x: The
Onge, Jarawa, Great Andamanese and Sentinelese
are associated with the Negrito racial type in the Andaman Islands.
The
Proto-Australoid
type is described by a long head, depressed nasal root and wavy hair.
Yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height are characteristic descriptions associated with the
Mongoloid
type.
Negrito corresponds to the Andaman communities; Proto-Australoid to Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho; Mongoloid to the Himalayan and north-eastern peoples; and Nordic to north-western India.

secs.t: Racial elements in tribal groups (Andaman, north-east, central and south India tribes)

x: The
Santhal
is the standard example of a Central Indian tribe associated with the Proto-Australoid racial element.
South Indian tribal groups are described as having a Proto-Australoid base, with a Negrito strain among certain hill foragers; Risley classified the Paniyan as Dravidian.
Kadar and Irula are cited as Negrito traces in the southern hills, located beyond Andhra Pradesh in this classification.

secs.t: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

x: The Mongoloid type is characterised by yellowish complexion, oblique eyes with an epicanthic fold, high cheekbones, sparse hair, medium height, broad head and a flat face.
The Negrito type is described by dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and a broad flat nose.
The living-head ranges are 77–81.99 for mesocephalic and 82 or above for brachycephalic; the corresponding dry-skull ranges are 75–79.99 and 80 or above.

secs.t: Risley classification - racial types and regions

x: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for 1901 and wrote The People of India, published in 1908.
Risley was the exponent of
the racial theory of caste
, which treats caste as a by-product of racial difference.
The
Turko-Iranian
type was associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier region.
Paniyans and Santals are cited as representative examples of the
Dravidian
type in Risley's classification.

secs.t: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

x: Guha identified six main racial groups with nine sub-types, using 1931 Census data.
Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Tibetans of Sikkim represent Tibeto-Mongoloid.
Kadars and Irulas are associated with the Negrito group, while Santhals, Bhils and Chenchus are associated with the Proto-Australoid group.
Guha's listed order is Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals and Nordic.

secs.t: Anthropological Survey of India - role and headquarters

x: The Anthropological Survey of India was founded at
Varanasi
in 1945 and shifted to Kolkata in 1948.
AnSI moved to Kolkata in 1948, works under the Ministry of Culture, and had B.S. Guha as its first Director.
AnSI undertakes research and documentation in physical and cultural anthropology, including the study of communities.
Port Blair, Shillong, Nagpur, Mysore, Dehradun, Udaipur and Kolkata are the seven regional centres.

secs.t: Criticism of race classification and recent genetic studies

x: Modern evidence shows that humans share over 99% of their genetic material and all belong to Homo sapiens, making rigid racial divisions scientifically subjective.
The 2009 genetic research framework describes most Indians as having mixed ANI and ASI ancestry; the abbreviations mean Ancestral North Indians and Ancestral South Indians.
The study found differences in
gut microbiomes
, suggesting that environment rather than genes accounted for the observed difference.

secs.t: Other classifications - Haddon, Eickstedt, Hutton, Sarkar - basis

x: Eickstedt proposed the four main groups
Weddid, Melanid, Indid and Mongolid
on physical and regional criteria.
Griffith Taylor's theory holds that primitive races are pushed to peripheral areas, with the Andaman Islands cited as an example.
Haddon’s classification dates to 1924, Eickstedt’s to the 1930s, Hutton’s description to the 1931 Census, and Sarkar’s work followed these classifications.

secs.t: Census 1901 ethnographic survey - Risley's role

x: H.H. Risley
was the Census Commissioner for the 1901 Census and organised its ethnographic survey.
Risley mainly used the
nasal index
in his anthropometric ranking of castes.
Risley’s dictum stated an inverse relationship, not that a higher nasal index indicated higher social status.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The review was the first since 2007, CERD expressed grave concern, and India rejected the observations as politically motivated while maintaining that caste is not race.
The plea followed the killing of
Anjel Chakma
and concerned racial prejudice and slurs against people from the North-East.
The Rakhigarhi DNA findings showed no “Steppe Pastoralist” gene, challenging certain Aryan-invasion interpretations.

rows.title: Religious composition of India - distribution and change over decades
sub: Group-II S2-61: Religious groups of India and Andhra Pradesh - composition and distribution

secs.t: Religion-wise growth rates 2001-2011 - highest and lowest growing communities

x: Exam angle: "highest growth rate" = Islam. Jains are the slowest-growing community.
Exam angle: "lowest sex ratio" (Sikh) and "highest literacy" (Jain) are the recurring one-liners.
Sikhs recorded the lowest sex ratio among the listed communities, at 903 females per 1,000 males.
The literacy ranking was Jain, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, Hindu and Muslim, in descending order.

secs.t: Religious composition Census 2011 - shares of Hindus, Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains

x: Exam angle: match community to its share (Sikhs 1.7, Christians 2.3, Buddhists 0.7, Jains 0.4).
Exam angle: absolute Christian population (about 2.8 crore / 28 million), highest-growth religion (Islam), matching religion to % share, ascending/descending order.
Muslims
constituted 14.2 percent of India's population according to the cited Census 2011 figures and were the largest minority community.
The total population considered in the Census 2011 religious-composition data was
121.09 crore
The six major religions, ORP, Religion Not Stated and the newly added No Religion option were separately recognised in the stated Census classification.
The 1881 census recorded religions of Indian origin at about 79% of the population; approximately 95% of that group was Hindu.

secs.t: Distribution - state with largest number of each minority, map-based minority regions

x: Exam angle: "largest number of Buddhists" = Maharashtra. Map questions pair NE hills with Christians and Ladakh/Sikkim with Buddhists.
Buddhist share is highest in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; Punjab is the only Sikh-majority State; and Jain share is highest in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
Maharashtra's large Buddhist population is linked to Dr B. R.
Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956
Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods because of security concerns, cultural preservation and rental discrimination.
Islam arrived with Arab merchants and later spread through the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis.
The fuller eight-unit list is
Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab

secs.t: Change over decades - identifying a community from its decadal population series

x: The figures describe the Christian population: about 10.7 million in 1961 and 27.8 million in 2011.
The approximate 2011 populations were Sikhs 20.8 million, Buddhists 8.4 million and Jains 4.5 million.
The Hindu share has slowly declined, the Muslim share has steadily risen, and the Sikh and Buddhist shares have dipped over the long run.

secs.t: States/UTs where a national minority is the majority - which religion where

x: Christians are a majority in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya
Lakshadweep
has a Muslim majority of about 97 percent.
All three statements are correct according to the stated 2011 Census-based figures.
Christians are the largest single religious group in Arunachal Pradesh, but they constitute only about 30 percent and therefore do not form a majority.

secs.t: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

x: Christians
had the highest sex ratio among the listed religious communities in 2011, at 1,023 females per 1,000 males.
The order was Christians (1,023), Buddhists (965), Jains (954), Muslims (951), Hindus (939) and Sikhs (903).
The literacy order was Jains, Christians, Buddhists, Sikhs, Hindus and Muslims, with Jains at about 95 per cent and Muslims at the lowest position.

secs.t: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts

x: All three statements correctly describe the minority population of Andhra Pradesh in APSES 2024–25: it is mostly urban, has a large Below-Poverty-Line segment and has a low share in economic support schemes.
The highest Muslim shares in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Rayalaseema districts of
Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur

secs.t: Minority welfare schemes - PMJVK, scholarships, AP bodies (Wakf Board)

x: The Minorities Finance Corporation corresponds to post-matric RTF, the Christian Corporation to ₹150.92 crore and pilgrimage assistance, the Waqf Board to payments to Imams and Mouzzans, and the Haj Committee to 1,652 pilgrims.
The Board provided ₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans in 4,984 masjids at a cost of ₹45 crore, and surveyed 7,005 of 10,522 un-notified waqf properties.
The additional measures include six pre-matric hostels, ten post-matric hostels, six minority residential schools and Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Overseas Education, for which ₹21.50 crore was provided.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
The income ceiling for the post-matric scholarship is
₹2.5 lakh
, and the AP minority cell fast-tracked its DBT in April 2026.
The debates include the demography narrative in relation to fertility data and the fact that religious minorities constitute only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.

rows.title: Linguistic groups of India - language families, Eighth Schedule languages, bilingualism
sub: Group-II S2-62: Linguistic groups - language families, Eighth Schedule languages, languages of Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

x: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Gujarati
are Indo-Aryan languages concentrated mainly in northern, western and eastern India.
The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.
Santhali,
Munda
ri and Ho are associated with the Munda branch of the Austro-Asiatic family, especially in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.
Raghunath Murmu created the Ol Chiki script for Santhali in 1925.
The approximate 2011 shares were Indo-Aryan 78.05 per cent, Dravidian 19.64 per cent, Austro-Asiatic 1.11 per cent and Tibeto-Burman 1.01 per cent.

secs.t: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

x: Telugu had occupied third place in 2001, but Marathi overtook it in 2011; Telugu consequently stood fourth.
Among the stated world rankings, Hindi is second, Bengali is seventh and Punjabi is tenth.
Hindi
is the most spoken first language and functions as the lingua franca of northern and central India.

secs.t: Census language data - mother tongues across censuses, scheduled vs non-scheduled, Mother Tongue Survey

x: Exam angle: "In 1961 census 1,652 languages were listed as mother tongues" is a true statement.
Census 2011 language returns were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues and grouped into 121 languages, consisting of 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India recorded
179 languages and 544 dialects
between 1903 and 1928.
Grierson's survey was conducted during 1903–1928, followed by the 1961 Census, the 2011 Census and completion of the Mother Tongue Survey in November 2022.
Hindi, Bengali and Tamil accounted for 43.6 percent, 8.0 percent and 5.7 percent respectively in the Census 2011 ranking table.

secs.t: Eighth Schedule - number of languages, additions by amendment, pending inclusion demands

x: Exam angle: "which language is NOT in the Eighth Schedule" (Bhojpuri, English) and amendment-to-language matching.
Santhali is written in the
Ol Chiki
script, which was created by Pandit Raghunath Murmu.
No fixed constitutional criteria exist for inclusion, and the Ashok Pahwa and Sitakant Mohapatra Committees are associated with the years 1996 and 2003 respectively.
The digital editions included Santhali in Ol Chiki and, for the first time, Kokborok and Kashmiri; there are also fresh demands for Bhojpuri’s inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.

secs.t: Classical languages - list, order of recognition, criteria

x: Exam angle: "more than one of the above" (Telugu, Marathi, Bengali are all classical).
The criteria relate to antiquity, a rich ancient literary tradition and originality; exclusive composition in prose is not a criterion.
Granth Kutir holds approximately
2,300 books and 50 manuscripts
in the 11 classical languages.
One of the criteria for classical-language status is
1,500 or more years of recorded history

secs.t: States - main/official language (Goa, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Sikkim)

x: Meghalaya has English as an official language, with
Khasi and Garo
also declared official languages.
Sikkim has Nepali, Sikkimese (Bhutia), Lepcha, English and other languages among its official languages.
States may choose their own official language or languages, while Hindi and English are the Union’s official languages.
Telugu belongs to the
Dravidian
language family and is one of the 22 languages referred to in the Eighth Schedule.

secs.t: Bilingualism and trilingualism - Census 2011 levels, three-language formula

x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on
14 September 1949
, a date now observed as Hindi Diwas.
Article 343
deals with the official language of the Union, including Hindi in Devanagari script and the international form of Indian numerals.
Article 351 places a duty on the Union to promote and develop Hindi, drawing on Sanskrit and the other languages included in the Eighth Schedule.
The Ladakh Official Languages Regulation, 2025 lists English, Hindi, Urdu, Bhoti and Purgi.
The Meghalaya ordinance of 2026 gave Khasi and Garo
associate official-language status
alongside English, under the State’s language framework.

secs.t: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries

x: Odisha
published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series for preserving vanishing tribal languages.
Bhasha Sangam encouraged school students to learn simple sentences in all 22 scheduled languages.
Adi Vaani is associated with Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santhali;
Koya
is not included in the listed group.

Jago is the Ministry’s AI assistant, TribeX teaches languages and crafts, dictionaries are being compiled for Mavila and Malaveduvan in Kerala, and Odisha teaches 21 tribal languages in 1,483 schools.

secs.t: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status

x: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy is regarded as the father of the Vyavaharika, or colloquial, Telugu movement.
The
Kalamalla inscription of 575 CE
, associated with the Renati Cholas of Kadapa, is regarded as the first fully Telugu inscription.

secs.t: Languages of AP - Telugu dialects, tribal languages, Urdu speakers

x: Koya and Kui/Kuvi are Dravidian; Savara is Austro-Asiatic-Munda; and Gor Boli is Indo-Aryan.
Gor Boli is an Indo-Aryan language of the Banjara community; it has no native script and is written using Telugu, Devanagari or Kannada scripts.
Deccani Urdu dates to the Qutb Shahi period, when
Persian was the official language and Telugu was spoken by the people

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Constitution was released in Sindhi in Devanagari and Persian scripts, while the digital Santhali edition used Ol Chiki.
The criticism specifically concerns the Census understating bilingualism in English, indicating a problem in adequately capturing bilingual language use.
The criticism refers to the Census cutoff of 10,000 speakers, which may contribute to smaller languages being absorbed into broader linguistic categories.

rows.title: Migration - types, streams, causes and consequences; internal migration in India
sub: Group-II S2-57: Migration - types, causes, streams and consequences; migration in Andhra Pradesh

secs.t: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share

x: Exam angle: GCM statement questions test "all countries", "legally binding" and "internal migration". All three are false.
The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at
Marrakech in December 2018
The report records more than 120 million forcibly displaced people and 65.8 million internal displacements caused by disasters.
The MEA’s PDOT, initiated in January 2018, had trained 1,72,220 emigrant workers by December 2024.

secs.t: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

x: Distance corresponds to short- or long-distance migration; number to individual or mass; cause to economic, social, political or religious; and will to voluntary or forced.
A
refugee
is forced to leave and cannot return because of fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or social or political group.
The Census uses both place of birth and place of last residence, while PLFS and NSO apply the Usual Place of Residence criterion of at least six months.

secs.t: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

x: Rural-to-rural migration has historically linked agricultural areas, often from low-potential to higher-potential regions, and women form the dominant group mainly because of marriage.
Urban-to-rural migration is the smallest stream and occurs in special circumstances such as return migration and retirement.
For inter-state female migrants by last residence in 2011, the migration pattern began with the
urban-to-urban
stream.

secs.t: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

x: All three conditions encourage rural-to-urban migration: cities generate labour demand, regional development is uneven, and rural areas may offer few employment opportunities.
About
of India’s population is aged 10–24, and job search among this group can contribute to rural-to-urban migration.
Drought in the Sahel
is an example of an environmental factor influencing migration, generally by pushing people away from affected areas.

secs.t: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

x: Among the 455.8 million migrants,
141.2 million
had moved during the period 2001–11.
The listed leading in-migration destinations include
Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
The correct sequence is
A, C, B, D
: December 2025, the 2026 report reference, July 2026 commencement of the NSO survey, and the July 2026 start of the MoSPI survey period.

secs.t: Consequences - demographic, economic (remittances), social, environmental

x: Migration often removes working-age men from source areas, resulting in ageing and a relatively higher proportion of women.
“Son of the soil” hostility denotes opposition to migrants by local populations in destination areas, including hostility expressed against groups such as “Bihari bhaiya”.
About
122 million
jobs were reported to have been lost during the COVID-19 lockdown, exposing the vulnerability of migrant workers.

secs.t: Indian diaspora - destination countries and remittance ranking

x: India was the top remittance recipient in 2024, receiving
USD 137 billion
and becoming the only country to cross the USD 100 billion mark.
India received a record USD 135 billion in FY 2024–25, with an increasing contribution from skilled professionals in developed countries rather than mainly from West Asia.

secs.t: Distress migration and inter-state migrant workers (Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, e-Shram)

x: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (RECS) Act, 1979 is now subsumed in the
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
The OSH Code covers workers who migrate on their own, provides for annual travel allowance and supports portability of PDS and social security.
Rural distress, informal employment, lack of job security and rising LPG prices in 2026 were identified as factors associated with distress migration and return migration to villages.
Despite portability initiatives,
biometric failures and data mismatches
continue to create problems in accessing benefits across States.

secs.t: Migration theories and terms → proponent

x: Ravenstein’s laws of migration were published in 1885 and 1889, followed by Griffith Taylor’s migration zone theory, Lee’s 1966 push-pull theory and Zelinsky’s mobility transition model.
Everett S. Lee is associated with migration theory, not demographic transition theory.

secs.t: Migration from AP - Gulf source districts, seasonal labour regions, Telugu diaspora

x: Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain are the Gulf destinations listed.
The AP Non-Resident Telugu Society
, or APNRT, ran the help desk for Telugus stranded in the Gulf.
Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor
are identified as drought-prone Rayalaseema districts from which many migrate to Gulf countries as domestic and unskilled workers.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three are identified concerns: migrants may miss social security and voting opportunities, while portability through ONORC and EPF remains patchy.
Migration is the main component of the rural-urban growth difference because
natural increase differs little between rural and urban areas
Census 2027
is expected to produce fresh migration data, alongside the MoSPI Migration Survey for July 2026–June 2027.

rows.title: Urbanisation in India - trends, class-size of towns, million-plus cities, urban agglomerations
sub: Group-II S2-55: Urbanisation in India - trends, urban agglomerations and problems

secs.t: Functional classification of towns - examples; towns by historical period

x: Chandigarh is an administrative town, Bhilai an industrial town, Digboi a mining town and Guntur a transport or trade town.
Gandhinagar is administrative, Ahmedabad industrial, Rameswaram religious or cultural, and Kodaikanal a resort town.
All three statements are correct: Tirupati and Puri are pilgrim towns, Shimla and Darjeeling are resorts, and Kandla and Kochi are port or transport towns.
Madurai is ancient, Lucknow medieval, Mumbai modern or British, and Gandhinagar a post-1947 planned town.

secs.t: Million-plus cities and urban agglomerations - Census count, cities in order of population

x: Chennai
ranked fourth with an approximate population of 8.7 million, followed by Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Ahmedabad.
All four statements are correct: Class I cities hold about 70% of the urban population, India has roughly 9,000 towns, only about 500 are large cities, and most towns have fewer than one lakh people.
The dominance of Class I cities in urban population indicates a
top-heavy
pattern of urban growth.

secs.t: States by number of towns and urban population share

x: The descending order is Delhi (97.50%), Chandigarh (97.25%), Lakshadweep (78.08%) and Puducherry (68.31%).
Himachal Pradesh
has the lowest listed urbanisation level at 10.04%, compared with Bihar at 11.30% and Assam at 14.08%.
Goa
is the most urbanised State in the cited comparison, with approximately 62% urban population, followed by Mizoram, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
Himachal Pradesh, Bihar, Sikkim and Uttar Pradesh are listed among the States with high rural population shares;
Goa
is not in that group.
The approximate urban populations were Sikkim 0.15 million, Arunachal Pradesh 0.31 million, Mizoram 0.56 million and Maharashtra 50.8 million.
The cited 2001 position described Goa and Maharashtra as having just over half of their people living in villages.

secs.t: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes

x: Urban areas added about 91.0 million people, compared with a rural increase of about 90.4 million, making it the first such decade since Independence.
Natural increase, rural-urban migration and reclassification or creation of new towns are the three identified components of urban growth.
Growth of industry and trade, pressure on rural land, low farm productivity, services and transport are identified causes.

secs.t: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities

x: Chandigarh
is the planned city associated with the architect Le Corbusier.
Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar, Gandhinagar, Navi Mumbai and Jamshedpur are all listed as planned cities or planned urban settlements.
Amaravati is run by the
Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority
, commonly abbreviated as APCRDA.
Every million-plus city is expected to have a statutory 20-year City Spatial and Economic Plan.

secs.t: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population

x: Exam angle: the reason for the 2001-11 urban jump (reclassification), and ordering the census years by urban share.
The urban shares were 10.84% in 1901, 11.99% in 1931, 17.97% in 1961 and 27.81% in 2001.
The urban shares were 10.84% in 1901, 11.99% in 1931, 17.97% in 1961 and 31.16% in 2011.
The medium phase extended from 1931 to 1961, during which the number of towns rose from 2,049 to 2,330.
The rapid phase began in 1961 and continued thereafter; urban population rose from 78.94 million in 1961 to 377.11 million in 2011, an increase of about 262%.
The World Cities Report 2026 was issued by
UN-Habitat
and released at the World Urban Forum in Baku.

secs.t: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

x: Class II towns have populations ranging from 50,000 to 99,999.
Class IV towns have populations between 10,000 and 19,999.
Class I is 1,00,000 and above, Class II is 50,000–99,999, Class V is 5,000–9,999 and Class VI is below 5,000.

secs.t: Urban schemes - Smart Cities, AMRUT, HRIDAY, PMAY-Urban

x: AMRUT initially covered 500 cities; the number became 485 after 15 mergers.
All four statements correctly describe AMRUT 2.0, including its period, financial structure, water-security coverage and sewerage target.
AMRUT 2.0 is associated with 2.03 crore tap connections and 1.50 crore sewer connections provided.
AMRUT covers ULBs of cities with one lakh or more population, State capitals and HRIDAY cities, representing about 65 per cent of the urban population.
PMAY-U seeks to provide
pucca houses to all eligible urban households
The SPM Rurban Mission is administered by the
Ministry of Rural Development
and focuses on rural clusters showing urban traits.
SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021 with the objective of creating
Garbage Free cities

secs.t: Census towns growth and hidden urbanisation

x: The EAC-PM estimate of possibly 63 per cent urbanisation in 2015 was based on
satellite data
A statutory town is a place notified with a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee and run by a ULB.
An urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread consisting of a town and its outgrowths or two or more contiguous towns.

secs.t: Urban planning institutions - FIRST UDA, 74th Amendment ULBs

x: A Nagar Panchayat serves an area in transition, a Municipal Council serves a smaller urban area, and a Municipal Corporation serves a larger urban area.
The 74th Amendment added Part IXA, Articles 243P–243ZG and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
Two-thirds
of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee are elected by the elected municipal members and panchayat chairpersons of the area.
Municipal bonds and the Urban Challenge Fund
are identified as finance tools for strengthening urban finances.

secs.t: Causes and problems of urbanisation - push/pull, industry, slums, housing, water, transport

x: Rural unemployment
is a push factor, whereas jobs, health and education facilities attract people towards urban areas.
The listed urban problems include housing shortage, solid waste, water and sewerage problems, traffic congestion, pollution and urban floods.
Peri-urban areas fall outside both rural and urban water-governance systems, yet they serve as recharge zones for cities.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India's urbanisation appears slow under the Census definition because peri-urban areas may not be adequately captured.
The UN Degree of Urbanisation method would include peri-urban areas, thereby potentially producing a higher estimate of urbanisation.
The
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
told the Parliamentary Standing Committee that the 1981 Census town criteria are outdated.
The Delhi Development Authority was established in 1957, UN-Habitat in 1978, the first APMCHUD meeting took place in 2006, and Habitat III was held in 2016.

rows.title: Metropolitan regions and megacities of India; problems of large cities

secs.t: National Capital Region - constituent states and towns, NCR Planning Board

x: The four Namo Cities are distributed across Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and are planned around Namo Bharat RRTS corridors using Transit-Oriented Development.
PARIVARTAN is funded at ₹9,585 crore and targets the replacement of approximately 2.07 lakh BS-IV or older trucks and buses.
The UN treats Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad as one agglomeration, while the Census counts them separately.

secs.t: Urban geography terms - meaning/coiner (megalopolis, umland, conurbation, primate city)

x: A megalopolis is a chain of merged metropolitan areas; umland is a town's surrounding hinterland; a conurbation is a continuously merged urban area; and a primate city dominates the next city by several times.
The concept of the primate city is associated with
Mark Jefferson
Rakesh Mohan identified metropolitanisation, commercialisation and rural or subsistence urbanisation.

secs.t: Megacities of India - population threshold, rank among the world's largest cities

x: The World Urbanisation Prospects 2025 places
Jakarta
as the world's most populous city, followed by Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi.
The change is attributed to the new city-definition method adopted in World Urbanisation Prospects 2025, rather than a sudden demographic collapse of Tokyo.
Older lists placed
Tokyo first, Delhi second, Mumbai seventh and Kolkata tenth
among the cities mentioned.

secs.t: Metropolitan regions - MMR, Kolkata and Chennai Metropolitan Areas: planning authorities

x: MMR is planned by MMRDA established in 1975; Kolkata by KMDA established in 1970; Chennai by CMDA established in 1974; and Delhi by DDA established in 1957.

The delegation studied MMRDA, CIDCO and the Slum Rehabilitation Authority to develop self-financing growth for the Vizag Economic Region through land monetisation, FSI premiums and Transit-Oriented Development.

secs.t: Problems of large cities - slums, housing, congestion, water supply, waste, pollution

x: India generates about
62 million tonnes
of municipal solid waste every year.
Groundwater stress occurs when extraction exceeds the rate of recharge.
Slums, migrant pressure, crime and informal jobs are identified as major housing and social problems.
The Economic Survey favours integrating informality rather than eradicating it and recommends land-market reforms involving issues such as dead capital and Bhu-Aadhaar.

secs.t: Slum population - Census 2011 states/cities with highest slum share

x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share of its urban population living in slums
, at about 36%.
Greater Mumbai
had the largest slum population among million-plus cities.
The World Bank estimate uses a broader definition than the Census count and places India's slum-dweller population at 177 million, the highest for any country.

secs.t: Urban flooding and heat island effect

x: Concrete reduces soil permeability, causing a larger proportion of rainwater to flow as surface runoff and increasing flood risk.
A UEA study covering 104 cities found that
Patiala
could warm at double the rate projected by climate models.
Visakhapatnam
has experienced flash floods after only a few hours of rain, illustrating the vulnerability of rapidly urbanising cities.

secs.t: City rankings and indices (Ease of Living Index, Swachh Survekshan)

x: The four categories correspond respectively to Indore–Surat–Navi Mumbai; Noida–Chandigarh–Mysuru; Ahmedabad–Bhopal–Lucknow; and Mira-Bhayandar–Bilaspur–Jamshedpur.
The theme of Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 was “
Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel - Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath
Pune, Navi Mumbai and
Tirupati
are identified among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the Ease of Living Index.
The theme of the 10th edition, 2025-26, is “
Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel - Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The
National Capital Region Planning Board
approved Namo Cities in June 2026.
Andhra Pradesh set up Project Management Units in 46 Urban Local Bodies for Swachh Survekshan 2026.
Vijayawada
is aiming for the top rank in Swachh Survekshan.
The suggested reform is to establish
stronger Metropolitan Waste Management Authorities
for megacities rather than rely only on simplified compliance.

rows.title: Human development - concept, HDI components and India's position
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I D-71

secs.t: HDI dimensions and indicators - included and excluded, goalposts, calculation

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT an HDI component" (inequality, military spending, MPI).
The logarithmic transformation reflects diminishing returns: additional income contributes progressively less to human development as income rises.
The income cap prevents exceptionally high incomes from disproportionately influencing the overall HDI.
Literacy and gross enrolment were replaced by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling in 2010.

secs.t: India's HDI rank, value, category, and neighbours

x: Exam angle: always pair the rank with the Report year and the total countries.
For India, HDR 2025 records life expectancy of 72 years, expected years of schooling of 13 years and GNI per capita of $9,046.76.
China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan
were listed above India, with ranks 78, 89 and 125 respectively.

secs.t: Human Development Reports - UNDP, first report, Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen

x: Human Development Reports are published by
the United Nations Development Programme
, or UNDP.
The first Human Development Report was issued by UNDP in 1990.
The framework was conceived by Pakistani economist
Mahbub ul Haq
with Amartya Sen.
The approach evaluates people and their capabilities rather than national income alone.

secs.t: Global comparison - life expectancy, literacy, overall HDI

x: Japan
is identified as having the highest life expectancy in the stated comparison.
The HDI no longer uses literacy as its education measure; it was replaced by years of schooling in 2010.

secs.t: Related indices - IHDI, GDI, GII, MPI and India's position

x: GDI is the female-to-male HDI ratio; GII covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market; MPI covers multidimensional deprivations; and PQLI uses literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy.
The Gender Development Index is the ratio of female to male HDI; a value close to 1 indicates parity.
The GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in health, education and earned income.

secs.t: Capability approach - human development vs economic growth

x: Amartya Sen
defined capabilities as the substantive freedoms people possess to lead lives they value.
Amartya Sen’s Development as Freedom was published in 1999.
Literacy, health and non-discrimination are constituents of development as well as possible instruments.

secs.t: State-level human development - top and bottom states

x: Kerala
is associated with the Kerala Model, characterised by strong health and education outcomes despite modest income.
Assam is 24th of 29 with an HDI of 0.699; West Bengal has 0.719; Kerala has the lowest MPI of 0.002; and Bihar has the highest MPI of 0.16.
The sub-national series gives an India average of 0.732 for 2023, whereas the UNDP figure stated for India is 0.685.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a headcount ratio of 6.06%, less than half the national 14.96%, ranked ninth best, and West Godavari recorded the lowest ratio at 2.42%.
The simulation estimated a possible loss of 0.03–0.12 years of HDI progress and an increase in poverty from 23.9% to 24.2%.
The top 10% are reported to earn approximately
13 times
the income of the bottom 10%.

4.96 crore
Andhra Pradesh is the eighth largest State by area, covers about 1,62,970 sq km, has the third longest coastline and possesses a coastline of approximately 974 km.
Undivided Andhra Pradesh accounted for
7.00 per cent
of India’s population and ranked fifth in that comparison.

secs.t: Density of AP - state figure, highest/lowest density districts

x: The density increased successively from 208 in 1981 to 252 in 1991, 279 in 2001 and 304 persons per sq km in 2011.
Under the 28-district arrangement,
Visakhapatnam
had the highest density at 1,870 persons per sq km.
Polavaram
had the lowest density among the 28 districts, at 54 persons per sq km.

was the most populous district in the 13-district structure, with about 51.5 lakh people.
Kurnool
had the highest share of child population in the 0–6 age group among the 13 districts.
Visakhapatnam
had the highest urban proportion, with 47.45 per cent of its population living in urban areas.
SPSR Nellore
was the most populous of the 28 districts, with about 24.17 lakh people.

secs.t: Decadal and compound growth - AP vs India, district variations

x: The rates in ascending order are 9.21 per cent, 12.32 per cent, 18.88 per cent, 20.53 per cent and 21.13 per cent, corresponding to E, D, A, B and C.
The highest growth rate was 21.13 per cent during
The decline was associated with falling fertility, higher literacy and female education, urbanisation and family planning.

secs.t: Regional distribution - Coastal Andhra vs Rayalaseema vs Uttarandhra

x: Rest of Coastal Andhra
included East Godavari, the most populous district, and Krishna, the densest district with 518 persons per sq km.
The sex ratio increased by
14 points
, from 983 to 997.
Rayalaseema is dry and drought-prone, Uttarandhra has a history of out-migration, and Rest of Coastal Andhra includes Krishna, the densest district in the 13-district structure.

secs.t: Fertility trend of AP (TFR) and population policy debate

x: The reported Andhra Pradesh indicators are CBR 15.0, CDR 6.9, child sex ratio 944 and IMR 19.
The policy aims to raise Andhra Pradesh’s TFR from 1.5 to the replacement level of 2.1 and prepare for an ageing society by 2047.
“Pillale Sampada”, meaning “children are wealth”, represents a shift from
population control to population promotion

secs.t: Households and average household size

x: The 2011 average household size was about
, derived from 495.77 lakh people divided by 127.19 lakh households.
Households increased from 57.52 lakh to 127.19 lakh, while average size declined from about 5 to about 3.9.
JJM data records 95.44 lakh rural households in Andhra Pradesh, with 74.72% having tap connections; the target is March 2028.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: For Census 2027, self-enumeration was followed by house listing in Andhra Pradesh from
The data is relevant to the post-2026 delimitation debate, in which low-fertility southern States are concerned about losing parliamentary seats.
The debate includes concerns about fiscal burden, women’s autonomy and the undercounting of urban spread by Census Town criteria.

of Andhra Pradesh’s workers according to PLFS 2023–24.

, compared with 45.6% for Andhra Pradesh.

, based on 24,72,092 learners appearing out of 25,06,696.

, with full literacy set as the following year’s target.

rows.title: Andhra Pradesh - SC and ST population; major tribal groups (Chenchu, Koya, Savara, Yanadi, Yerukula) and PVTGs
sub: Group-II S2-60: Tribal groups of Andhra Pradesh - Chenchu, Koya, Savara, Yanadi, Yerukula and PVTGs

secs.t: Major tribes of AP → district/habitat, and odd-one-out tribes from other states

x: Exam angle: "which is not a tribe of AP", with a central-Indian tribe as the answer.
The Dhimsa dance is associated with
Bagata, Valmiki, Konda Dora, Gadaba, Porja, Savara and Jatapu
tribes.
The Koyas are concentrated in the
Godavari valley agency
, including the Chintoor and Polavaram areas, and call themselves Koyi Toor.
The
Konda Reddi
s inhabit the hill tracts of East and West Godavari, particularly the Rampa region, practise podu cultivation and are classified as a PVTG.

secs.t: Number of notified Scheduled Tribes in AP - ST Orders amendments

x: Exam angle: "how many STs notified in AP under the 1976 Act" - answer 33.
Gowdu, Nayak and Valmiki
carry area restrictions and are Scheduled Tribes only in the Agency Tracts of the erstwhile State.
The stated Scheduled-area districts are Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli and Eluru.
The Scheduled Areas cover 16,267.63 square kilometres, or 10.15% of the area, and include 3,512 villages.
Polavaram district holds the
Rampachodavaram and Chintoor
Integrated Tribal Development Agencies.

secs.t: Districts with highest SC and ST population/share

x: Visakhapatnam district had approximately
6.18 lakh
Scheduled Tribe persons in Census 2011.
Visakhapatnam
had the lowest stated SC share at 7.68%, compared with 23.19% in Prakasam and 22.49% in Nellore.

secs.t: PVTGs of AP - number and names

x: All three statements are correct: 35,970 houses and 24,691 electrified PVTG households were reported, and APSES counts 12 PVTGs for PMAY-JANMAN.
The Araku Valley or Visakhapatnam agency is associated with Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba, Bondo Porja, Khond Porja and Parengi Porja.
Bondo Porja, Khond Porja and Konda Savara
were added as PVTG variant entries in February 2024.
The approved hostel locations were in Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), Eluru, Palnadu, Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.

secs.t: Tribal livelihoods - podu cultivation, NTFP collection, GCC

x: Podu plots are cropped with
jowar or maize
before being left when fertility declines.
The GCC procures minor forest produce and agricultural produce, operates the PDS in interior areas and undertakes value addition.
The GCC put
Rs 250.76 crore
into the tribal economy during 2024–25 up to November.
There are 415 sanctioned Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, of which 258 are working.

secs.t: Tribal languages, scripts and festivals (Savara, Koya)

x: Koyas speak Koya Bhasha, celebrate Bhumi Panduga at the start of farming, and observe Mamidi Panduga.
Dhimsa is danced by Bagata, Valmiki, Konda Dora, Gadaba, Porja, Savara and Jatapu communities.
Dhimsa is danced during Chaitra Purab, also called Eetela Panduga, and is traced to Koraput.
The Koyas replaced bison horns with palm leaves in the Permakore flute
to protect the gaur

secs.t: Tribe → traditional occupation (food gathering, podu, pastoralism)

x: Among the Yerukula, Beedari refers to basket and rope making, Kunchi to fortune-telling, and pig-rearing is also a traditional occupation.
Podu is practised in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam, can cause erosion and forest fires, and FRA pattas with horticulture are suggested as remedial measures.
Konda Reddi, Koya Dora and Valmiki
tribal farmers of Maredumilli grow annatto on about 10,000 acres and are forced to sell it to middlemen.

secs.t: Tribal welfare in AP - Girijan Cooperative Corporation, tribal university, Scheduled Area mandals

x: The GCC buys minor forest produce and agricultural produce, runs PDS depots, provides credit and sells products under the Girijan brand.
‘GCC Araku Valley Coffee’ is a trademark of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation.
The Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum is being built at Tajangi in Chintapalli, within the Alluri Sitarama Raju region.
Adivasi Talli Bata roads involve Rs 1,000 crore, cover 905 km and link 2,336 habitations.

secs.t: Tribal movements and issues in AP - bauxite mining, Polavaram displacement, land alienation (1/70 Regulation)

x: The bauxite deposits lie in the
Araku, Paderu and Chintapalli agency
areas and raise concerns relating to PVTG rights.
All three statements are correct: surveys were allowed, soil sampling occurred in Chintapalli and G.K. Veedhi, and the CPI(M) alleged that PESA Gram Sabhas and the TAC were bypassed.

About 276 villages, mostly tribal and situated in ASR and Eluru, are to be submerged; Koya and Kondh groups oppose displacement, and the CPI(M) reported rehabilitation for only 21% of displaced families.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: “Pander Valla” is identified as the Koyas’
river-fishing tradition
, which is threatened by Polavaram submergence.
The Tribal Sub Plan allocation for Andhra Pradesh for 2024–25 was
The annual NSTR closure cuts the Chenchus off from
forest produce
The debates concern the clash between development projects and protections embodied in the 1/70 Regulation, PESA and the Forest Rights Act.

fourth
in India in 2011, after Hindi, Bengali and Marathi, and accounted for about 6.7%.

121 languages and 270 mother tongues
Savara, Gadaba and Koya
dialects occur in tribal pockets of the Eastern Ghats and are being documented by the Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Border districts → neighbouring language spoken (Chittoor, Srikakulam, Kurnool, Anantapur)

x: All four pairs are correct: Srikakulam has an Odia pocket; Chittoor has a Tamil pocket; and Anantapur and Kurnool have Kannada pockets.
In 1953, Bellary taluk was divided linguistically: Telugu-speaking areas went to Andhra and Kannada-speaking areas went to Mysore.
Yanam, a part of Puducherry, is a Telugu enclave located next to East Godavari.

secs.t: Telugu - classical language status and mother tongue data

x: Telugu was granted Classical Language status by the Union Government in 2008, together with Kannada.
Tamil and Sanskrit were declared in 2004/2005, Telugu and Kannada in 2008, Malayalam in 2013, and the five-language group in 2024.
The 2024 additions were
Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
There are 11 classical languages, and Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Pali and Prakrit are included in the stated classifications.

secs.t: Urban centres of AP - largest cities, cities above one lakh (2011), municipal corporations

x: Visakhapatnam is governed by the
Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation
, commonly abbreviated as GVMC.
All four statements are correct: 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 municipalities and 30 nagar panchayats together make 123 urban local bodies.
The listed growth poles include Vijayawada, Guntur, Nellore, Kurnool, Rajamahendravaram, Tirupati and Kakinada, together with Visakhapatnam and Amaravati.

secs.t: City nicknames → city

x: Visakhapatnam is the City of Destiny, Tenali is Andhra Paris, Tirupati is the Temple City and Rajamahendravaram is the Cultural Capital of the Andhras.
Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, received the title in connection with Rajaraja Narendra’s Eastern Chalukya court.
Amaravati
is known as the People’s Capital of Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Urban schemes in AP → cities covered (HRIDAY, Smart Cities, AMRUT, SBM-Urban, Garbage Free Cities)

x: AMRUT covers urban local bodies with a population of one lakh or more, as well as capitals and HRIDAY cities.
Andhra Pradesh ranked first, followed by
Odisha and Madhya Pradesh
in the AMRUT Ease of Living Index 2018.
Tirupati and Vijayawada
were included in the top-ten ease-of-living cities listed in the Economic Survey 2025-26.
PMAY-U in Andhra Pradesh covers 18,01,840 houses across 125 urban local bodies and 21 Urban Development Authorities.

secs.t: Urban development authorities → area (VMRDA, APCRDA, TUDA)

x: APCRDA plans the Amaravati capital region, while VMRDA plans the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region and was formed from VUDA in 2018.
Town and Country Planning officials are deputed between APCRDA and VMRDA.
Andhra Pradesh has 21 urban development authorities, and VMRDA is associated with the Green Triangle project and master-plan roads.

secs.t: Growth corridors and urban clusters (Visakhapatnam-Kakinada, Vijayawada-Guntur-Tenali-Mangalagiri)

x: The Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali–Mangalagiri area was chosen as the capital area because of its
central location
The
Visakhapatnam Economic Region
consists of 10 districts and has a target of USD 750–800 billion by 2047.
Kopparthy in Kadapa is a node of the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (
VCIC
Orvakal in Kurnool and Kopparthy in YSR Kadapa are nodes on the
Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor

secs.t: AP urban share - Census 2011 percent, southern rank, rural-urban trend

x: The urban shares were 18.35% in 1971, 22.14% in 1981, 24.13% in 2001 and 29.47% in 2011.
Urban population increased from 109.56 lakh to 146.10 lakh, about 33%, whereas rural population rose from 344.41 lakh to 349.67 lakh, about 1.5%.
The 16th Finance Commission's Urbanisation Premium rewards the merger of peri-urban villages into Urban Local Bodies.

secs.t: Urban problems in AP - slums, urban flooding in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada

x: RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar
developed the AI flood-forecasting system.
The system provides 48-hour rainfall forecasts and 6-hour flash-flood warnings, and is intended to be extended to all ULBs.
The stated sewage-treatment capacity or quantity is
613 MLD
, while water supply is 2,048 MLD.
Door-to-door collection covers 94.62% of wards, while 49.32% achieve 100% source segregation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated Census criteria are at least 5,000 people, at least 75% of male workers outside agriculture, and at least 400 persons per square kilometre.
MA&UD has cut about 45 archaic levies, including a charge referred to as a tree guard fee.
The AP–UN-Habitat MoU of July 2026 proposed a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at
Amaravati

secs.t: AP HDI vs national HDI - NHDR comparison, AP HDR editions

x: Exam angle: "AP's HDI in NHDR 2001 was... India's" → less than.
The HDI was conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with the intellectual contribution of Amartya Sen.
HDI uses the geometric mean of life expectancy, education based on mean and expected years of schooling, and log GNI per capita measured at purchasing power parity.

secs.t: AP in national indices - SPI, SDG India Index, Mission Antyodaya, NITI MPI, NFHS-5

x: The MPI of Andhra Pradesh was
in 2019–21, compared with 0.053 in 2015–16, representing an approximately 50% decline.
Mission Antyodaya is the Ministry of Rural Development's convergence framework and ranks gram panchayats through an annual survey.
West Godavari
had the lowest listed multidimensional poverty percentage at 2.42%, followed by Guntur, Krishna and Chittoor.
India's multidimensional poverty headcount declined to

secs.t: AP social composition - SC share and SC-heavy districts

x: Scheduled Castes account for 17.08% and Scheduled Tribes for 5.53% of Andhra Pradesh's population.
The Scheduled Caste population was
84.69 lakh
, constituting 4.21% of India's Scheduled Caste population.

secs.t: District-level variation - literacy, urbanisation, density (28 districts)

x: SPSR Nellore
had the highest population at 24.17 lakh; Polavaram had the lowest at 3.49 lakh.
Visakhapatnam recorded the highest literacy, 79.05%, and Alluri Sitarama Raju the lowest, 44.67%.
Krishna
had the highest density under the old 13-district arrangement, at 518 persons per sq km.
YSR Kadapa and Prakasam
had densities below 200 persons per sq km in the old 13-district pattern.

secs.t: AP welfare schemes linked to human development

x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly Aarogyasri, provides cashless care to 1.43 crore families and covers 3,257 procedures.
The Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust, associated with Aarogyasri, received
₹4,000 crore
in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27.
Amma Vodi provided ₹15,000 annually to the mother or recognised guardian of a poor child attending
school or college

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The comparative figures given are MMR 30 and IMR 19 for health, while the lowest district literacy figure cited is 44.67 percent, indicating relatively better performance on health than literacy.
HDI can conceal inequalities within a State; therefore, the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index and district-level indices provide a more differentiated assessment.

rows.title: Sectors of the economy - primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary; global patterns

secs.t: Sector classification - activities → sector (mining, transport, fishing, manufacturing, research, top decision-making), primary to quinary

x: Mining
is a primary-sector activity because it directly uses natural resources.
Cement manufacturing is a secondary-sector activity.
The
quinary sector
comprises top decision-making activities, including government leadership and top executives.
By the nature of the activity, mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature.
Mining has a weight of
in the revised IIP.

secs.t: Primary activity types - gathering, hunting, extractive vs genetic industries

x: Hunting and gathering
are regarded as the oldest primary activities because they involve direct dependence on nature for subsistence.
Animal husbandry
is a genetic industry because it involves breeding and rearing animals.
Agriculture, fish farming and animal husbandry are genetic industries, while mining, capture fishing, hunting and lumbering are extractive industries.

secs.t: Collar-colour terms for workers (red, green, blue, pink, white, gold collar)

x: Red-collar workers are associated with primary-sector outdoor work.
Blue-collar workers are associated with manual work, including factory and construction activities.
Pink-collar occupations traditionally include service jobs such as nursing, teaching and clerical work that were long held mostly by women.
The
United Arab Emirates
overtook Saudi Arabia in 2025 as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers.

secs.t: Sectoral shares - GVA vs employment in India and AP

x: The reported AP GVA shares were approximately 33% for agriculture and allied activities, 24% for industry and 43% for services.
AP employment was distributed as 45.6% in the primary sector, 22.8% in the secondary sector and 31.6% in the tertiary sector.
The new GDP series placed GDP levels 3–4% lower, measured manufacturing at 14.7% of the economy and reported FY26 growth at 7.6%.

secs.t: Structural transformation - Fisher-Clark thesis, service-led growth debate

x: Allan Fisher advanced the thesis in 1935, while Colin Clark developed the argument further in 1940.
The thesis states that as income rises, labour and output generally move from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector.
Premature deindustrialisation indicates that India did not pass through a large mass factory-employment phase before the expansion of services.

secs.t: Global patterns - developed vs developing country sector shares

x: Services account for about
of GDP in developed countries, while quaternary and quinary activities are also growing.
Developing countries generally retain a large primary-sector employment share, while their services sector is growing faster than industry.

secs.t: Organised vs unorganised sector distinction

x: The organised sector consists of registered establishments with regular terms of employment and applicable labour laws, including provisions related to PF, minimum wages and leave.
Small scattered units, irregular pay and lack of security are features of the unorganised sector.
Public versus private is a separate sectoral division based on ownership.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The GDP base year was moved to
in the new series released in February 2026.
The revised IIP added a
water supply and waste management
sector.
Agriculture accounts for about 33% of AP GVA against about 21% nationally, and AP’s agricultural and allied sector is led by livestock and fisheries.

rows.title: World agriculture - types of farming, major crop belts and agricultural regions

secs.t: Types of farming - features and regions

x: Commercial grain farming, especially mechanised wheat cultivation, is associated with the
Prairies, Steppes, Pampas and Downs

Plantation farming is associated with Malaysia, Brazil and India; mixed farming with north-west Europe and eastern North America; commercial grain farming with the listed grassland regions; and intensive subsistence farming with monsoon Asia.
Intensive farming applies high labour and capital input to a unit of land, while extensive farming operates over larger areas with comparatively low input per unit of land.

secs.t: World leading producers → crop, and crop varieties (Robusta, Mocha)

x: India ranks second in tea, seventh in coffee and sixth in natural rubber production.

All four statements are correct: Kerala dominates Indian rubber production, Karnataka dominates coffee production, Araku gives Andhra Pradesh an important coffee position, and India has a virtual world monopoly in castor.
Robusta is Coffea canephora, a hardier lowland coffee containing more caffeine than Arabica.

secs.t: Agricultural regionalisation methods → geographer and indices

x: J. C. Weaver
introduced the crop-combination method in 1954.

Crop diversification is associated with Bhatia, Jasbir Singh and Gibbs-Martin; crop concentration with Bhatia; agricultural efficiency with Kendall, Enyedi and Shafi; and the four macro agricultural regions with Sengupta and Sdasyuk.
Kendall’s ranking coefficient is associated with the measurement of
agricultural efficiency

secs.t: Sustainable agriculture practices - crop rotation, organic, permaculture, IPM, natural farming

x: Natural farming does not require compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides.
Integrated Pest Management combines biological and ecological measures such as bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and natural predators to control pests.
APCNF, described as the world’s largest agro-ecological programme, covered 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares as of July 2026.

secs.t: Global Green Revolution - pioneers and institutes (CIMMYT, IRRI)

x: Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico with support from the American Rockefeller Foundation, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970, and William Gaud coined the term in 1968.
The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), established at Los Baños in the Philippines in 1960, released
IR8
, popularly called miracle rice.

secs.t: Whittlesey's agricultural regions - Mediterranean agriculture areas, oriental intensive farming

x: Derwent Whittlesey mapped 13 agricultural regions in 1936.
The Mediterranean agricultural region includes the Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the south-western Cape and south-western Australia.
Mediterranean agriculture is characterised by winter rainfall and crops such as grapes, citrus fruits and olives.
Oriental intensive farming belongs to monsoon Asia.

secs.t: Crop domestication - Old World vs New World crops

x: Wheat, barley, rice and sugarcane
are classified as Old World crops.
Coffee is an Old World crop, while cocoa, rubber and chilli are New World crops.
Maize and cassava are New World crops, whereas tea and barley are Old World crops.
Groundnut is a New World crop of the Americas, not an Old World crop.

secs.t: Agricultural terms → meaning

x: Sericulture is the practice associated with silk production, particularly the rearing of silkworms.
Viticulture means grape cultivation and floriculture means flower cultivation.
Horticulture
covers the cultivation of fruits, vegetables and flowers.
Horticulture output is stated to be approximately 362–367 million tonnes and has surpassed foodgrain output.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as India’s largest fruit producer and as ranking first in oil palm, papaya, cocoa and chillies.
The shift from paddy to drought-hardy crops in Andhra Pradesh is being promoted amid
a rain deficit
Podu cultivation persists in the agency tracts, not exclusively in the coastal plains.

rows.title: India - agriculture: major food crops (rice, wheat, maize, pulses) and their regions
sub: Group-II S2-33: Agriculture in India - cropping seasons, cropping pattern and major food crops

secs.t: Green Revolution - crops benefited, HYV seeds, father figures, regional spread, limitations

x: Exam angle: "Green Revolution mainly increased..." (wheat and rice); father in world vs father in India.
All three statements correctly describe the regional pattern: irrigated rice deltas benefited, the eastern belt initially lagged, and the second phase spread eastward and westward in the 1980s.
The gains were captured disproportionately by farmers with more than 10 hectares, while rainfed and hilly areas and crops such as pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
The Green Revolution refers to the mid-1960s surge in foodgrain production through HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation.
The New Agricultural Strategy began in 1965 and combined HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation and minimum support price with the objective of foodgrain self-sufficiency.
The Green Revolution reinforced rice-wheat monoculture and groundwater over-use particularly in
north-western India

secs.t: Crops → leading producing states and state production order

x: Rice is mainly a kharif crop requiring temperatures above 25°C, high humidity and rainfall above 100 cm or assured irrigation.
Wheat is a rabi crop requiring a cool growing season, about 50–75 cm rainfall and warm, sunny conditions during ripening.
Rajasthan is the leading bajra-producing state, and bajra is suited to the driest conditions and sandy soils.
India is the largest millet producer, accounting for 42.75% of world output; bajra contributes about 60% of India's millet output.
The cited figures are 18.59 million metric tonnes of millet production from 12.86 million hectares.
Tur or arhar is identified as a Kharif pulse, whereas gram or chana is identified as a Rabi pulse.

secs.t: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season

x: Rice grows best under high humidity, temperatures above 25°C and rainfall exceeding 100 cm, or equivalent irrigation.
Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.
Wheat generally requires about
of rainfall and is also supported by irrigation in major producing regions.
Millets are mostly kharif crops and are climate-resilient, low-input crops of dryland and rainfed tracts.

secs.t: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state

x: Jhum is practised in North-East India, Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia, Milpa in Central America and Mexico, and Roca in Brazil.
Tamrai is associated with Thailand, Chena with Sri Lanka, Bewar with Madhya Pradesh and Kumari with the Western Ghats.
In Andhra Pradesh, shifting cultivation is practised by the
Konda Reddi, Koya and Savara
communities.
Shifting cultivation generally involves clearing and burning vegetation, cultivating the plot for a period and then moving to another site when soil fertility declines.
Pama Dabi, Koman and Bringa are names used in Odisha, while Ponam or Poonam is associated with Kerala.

secs.t: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports

x: India's rice production is stated as about 150.18 MT, placing it first in the world and ahead of China's 145.28 MT.
India leads in dry onions, is the largest rice exporter with about 40% of global trade, and was stated by the Union Agriculture Minister to be the world's largest rice producer, ahead of China.

secs.t: Eastern India and food security programmes - BGREI, NFSM crops and components

x: BGREI, or Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India, was launched in 2010-11 for the rice-based rice-wheat cropping system of Eastern India.
Coarse cereals and commercial crops, including cotton, jute and sugarcane, were added to NFSM in
NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission in
NFSNM covers rice, wheat, pulses, maize, barley, Shree Anna, cotton, jute and sugarcane.
Edible-oil import dependence fell from 63.2 per cent in FY16 to
56.25 per cent
in FY24.

secs.t: Cropping systems - dominant systems, intercropping, parallel cropping

x: Rice-wheat is the dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, with paddy followed by wheat as double cropping.
Intercropping involves
growing two or more crops together in definite rows
, such as tur with jowar or maize.
Parallel cropping involves two crops of different growth habit and duration growing without competition; maize plus green gram is the stated example.
Leguminous pulses fix atmospheric nitrogen and leave fixed nitrogen in the soil for the succeeding cereal crop.
Andhra Pradesh is diversifying from food grains towards fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm.

secs.t: Millets and dryland farming - millet groups, Shree Anna, dryland rainfall limit

x: Kodo millet is also called kodon; ragi is finger millet and belongs to the major millet group.
Dryland farming is practised in areas receiving less than 750 mm rainfall and lacking assured irrigation.
Rainfed areas, which constitute about 51 per cent of net sown area, produce most of India's
millets, pulses and oilseeds

secs.t: Agricultural regionalisation - agro-climatic zones, macro regions

x: The 15 agro-climatic zones were subdivided into
72 sub-zones
The agro-climatic regionalisation was based on
soil, climate and cropping pattern
The Trans-Gangetic Plains include Punjab, Haryana and Delhi and are associated with wheat, rice and the highest productivity.
The
Upper Gangetic Plains
, particularly western Uttar Pradesh, constitute the core Green Revolution belt.
The Southern Plateau and Hills region includes
interior Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

secs.t: India in world agriculture - area and rice rank

x: India's net sown area was 141 million hectares and gross cropped area was 219.16 million hectares in 2021-22.
All three figures are correct for 2021-22: net irrigated area 77.9 million hectares, gross irrigated area 120.3 million hectares and gross irrigated area equal to 54.9 per cent of GCA.
The India Year Book figure for 2021–22 was 120.3 million hectares, equal to 54.9% of gross cropped area.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated shift is towards bajra and jowar in response to El Nino and conflict-related pressures, not a concern affecting rice and wheat alone.
Diversifying procurement across crops and regions is advocated as a measure of climate-proofing and to reduce excessive dependence on rice, wheat and a few regions.
From Kharif 2026, PMFBY coverage was reported to include
wild-animal attacks and paddy inundation
Both statements are true, and the stated advantages of MSP and free power explain why rice–wheat cultivation, particularly paddy in Punjab, continues to be favoured.
