rows.title: India - agriculture: commercial crops (cotton, sugarcane, oilseeds, jute, tea, coffee, rubber, spices) and their regions
sub: Group-II S2-34: Agriculture in India - commercial and plantation crops and their regions

secs.t: Commercial crops → leading states

x: Gujarat accounts for about
44.3 percent
of India’s groundnut production in the cited figure.
Gujarat contributes approximately
86.6 percent
of India’s castor production in the cited figure.
India is stated to be second in tea and cotton production and the largest producer of raw jute.
The
Jute Corporation of India
undertakes MSP procurement of raw jute.

secs.t: Tea and coffee - plantation history, hills, varieties

x: The first tea plantations were begun in the first half of the nineteenth century in the
Brahmaputra Valley
of Assam.
These crops are high-value plantation crops requiring substantial labour and capital, and the colonial plantation sector was dominated by Europeans and oriented towards exports.
Kodagu is in Karnataka, Araku and the ASR district are associated with coffee clusters in Andhra Pradesh, and the Nilgiris are in Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Commodity boards → headquarters

x: Exam angle: Tobacco Board at Guntur is the AP link in board-HQ matching questions.
All five listed boards—Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Spices and Tobacco Boards—are statutory Commodity Boards under the Department of Commerce.
The Coconut Development Board is headquartered at Kochi and is under the
Ministry of Agriculture
, unlike the five statutory Commodity Boards under the Department of Commerce.

secs.t: Oilseeds - kharif vs rabi, leading states, odd-one-out

x: Mustard
is identified as a Rabi-only oilseed in the given classification.
Sunflower
is grown in both Kharif and Rabi seasons.
The listed order for groundnut and oilseeds is
Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
Seven oilseeds are listed under MSP: groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower and nigerseed.
The two missions aim at nearly
70 million tonnes

secs.t: Sugarcane - tropical vs sub-tropical productivity, sugar bowl

x: The tropical advantage is attributed to cool nights with clear skies, favourable latitudinal position and long hours of sunshine.
The northern concentration is supported by fertile alluvium rich in lime and potash, level land, dense markets and sugarcane grown in compact blocks.
Sugarcane is a long-duration crop requiring hot and humid conditions and growing well in alluvial or black soils.

secs.t: Crop-specific apps and schemes → crop

x: Paat-Mitro was launched in 2023 for
jute
farmers.
All four pairs are correctly matched.
The Technology Mission on Cotton is associated with the
Silver Fibre Revolution

secs.t: World leading producers → crop

x: India is placed second or among the top two in cotton production, not first.
All four statements are correct in the stated production-position assessments: India is second in tea and groundnut, first in spices and coconuts, and fifth in rubber in the older assessment.

secs.t: Growth conditions and water-efficient crops

x: Tea grows well at about 20–30°C with 150–300 cm rainfall on deep, well-drained, acidic hill slopes.
Coffee requires about 15–28°C, shade, 150–250 cm rainfall and deep, well-drained, humus-rich soil, especially in the Western Ghats.
Sugarcane in Maharashtra and paddy in Punjab are cited as examples where subsidies can distort cropping patterns away from pure climate suitability.

secs.t: Horticulture - India's world rank, leading states, research institutes

x: The recent figures given are approximately 18.57 lakh hectares and 406.38 lakh metric tonnes.
MIDH follows a 60:40 ratio generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and covers the listed horticultural sectors.
MIDH is stated to have raised horticultural productivity to approximately
12.56 MT per hectare
IIHR is at Bengaluru, CISH at Lucknow, IIVR at Varanasi and NRC Banana at Tiruchirappalli.

secs.t: Crop nicknames and commercial-crop revolutions

x: The Golden Revolution is associated with
horticulture and honey

secs.t: Jute sector initiatives - Paat-Mitro, Jute ICARE, National Jute Board

x: JUTE-ICARE, or Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise, involves
certified seed and the microbial retting consortium SONA
The Act requires 100% of food grains and 20% of sugar to be packed in jute, subject to the stated provisions.
The Jute Corporation of India buys raw jute at
the minimum support price
when market prices fall.

secs.t: Cash crops - tobacco, chillies, turmeric → states and markets

x: All four statements are correct in the stated assessment.
Lakadong turmeric of
Meghalaya
is known for its high curcumin content.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All five pairs are correct: ICAR released 24 cotton, 13 oilseed, 6 sugarcane, 1 jute and 1 tobacco variety or varieties in the stated release.
Both statements are correct: synthetic materials compete with cotton, while Bangladesh competes with Indian jute goods in export markets.
Andhra Pradesh is associated with leadership in oil palm and with Araku coffee, Guntur chillies and tobacco.

rows.title: India - horticulture, plantation crops, livestock and fisheries geography
sub: Group-II S2-36: Agro-based activities - dairying, poultry, sericulture, fisheries and agro-processing

secs.t: India's world rank - milk, fruits, vegetables, silk, meat; leading fruit states

x: India ranks second in fruits, vegetables, potatoes, wheat and sugarcane
India is stated to rank first in dry onions and to have overtaken China in
rice
production.
Horticulture output was stated as 362.08 MT in 2024–25, exceeding foodgrain output, and it contributed about 33% of agricultural GVA from under 14% of cropped area.

secs.t: Fisheries types - inland vs marine, capture vs culture, leading states

x: Capture fisheries involve harvesting wild stocks, whereas culture fisheries refer to aquaculture or the controlled farming of fish and other aquatic organisms.
Aquaculture includes freshwater, brackish-water and marine farming of fish, shrimp, prawns, molluscs and seaweed.
Andhra Pradesh led India in inland fish landings in 2019-20 and is the largest producer of farmed shrimp, mainly Vannamei.

secs.t: Sericulture - silk types → state, largest producer

x: Muga silk
is endemic to Assam and is produced by Antheraea assamensis.
Mulberry silk feeds on mulberry; Tropical Tasar on Terminalia and Sal; Eri on castor and tapioca; and Muga on Som and Soalu.
AP Tasar is a forest-based activity concentrated in East Godavari and the ASR district, particularly around Rampachodavaram.

secs.t: Livestock breeds → native region and species

x: Ongole is a cattle breed native to the Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh.
Barbari is a goat breed of Uttar Pradesh, not a poultry breed.
Kadaknath is a black-meat poultry breed native to the Jhabua region of Madhya Pradesh.
Bhadawari is a buffalo breed associated with Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

secs.t: Regions → specialised produce

x: Kinnaur in Himachal Pradesh is associated with
apples
and forms part of the temperate fruit belt of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.
Tripura is noted for pineapple and true potato seed, while Meghalaya is associated with pineapple and Lakadong turmeric.

secs.t: Plantation crops - coconut, arecanut, cashew, cocoa regions

x: Coconut cultivation is concentrated in the listed coastal and eastern regions, and India ranks first in coconut production.
Andhra Pradesh is first in cocoa productivity, and cashew is identified as a Rayalaseema/Andhra Pradesh growth-engine crop.
The Portuguese introduced
cashew, tomato, chilli, potato and tobacco
, among other crops, into India.

secs.t: Dairying - India's world rank, Rashtriya Gokul Mission, Gokul Grams in AP

x: Per capita milk availability was
471 grams per day
The Andhra Pradesh Gokul Gram cattle-breeding farm is located at
Chadalawada in Prakasam district
All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh was seventh with 139.46 lakh tonnes in the current assessment and had ranked fifth in 2022–23.
Milk production reached 239.30 MT in 2023–24, up from 146.31 MT in 2014–15, representing a CAGR of 5.62 per cent.

secs.t: Agro-processing - processed food share, PM Kisan Sampada, mega food parks, PMFME

x: PM Kisan SAMPADA was approved in 2017 as a Central Sector scheme and includes integrated cold chain among its components.
The PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises scheme was launched in 2020 under Aatmanirbhar Bharat on a
One District One Product
basis.
APEDA operates under the 1985 Act, promotes processed-food exports, and its BHARATI cohort of 100 start-ups exported GI Jardalu mangoes and millet products.

secs.t: Allied activities → product

x: Apiculture is the rearing of bees and yields honey and bee-wax.
Lac culture produces lac obtained from lac insects.
Honey bees pass through the stages egg, larva, pupa and adult.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Horticultural output of about 362–367 million tonnes has exceeded foodgrains output of 357.73 million tonnes.
MIDH funding follows a 60:40 pattern generally and a 90:10 pattern for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
Ongole and Punganur are important cattle breeds associated with Andhra Pradesh, while Chadalawada is the location of the Gokul Gram.

sub: Group-II S2-35: Agriculture in Andhra Pradesh - cropping pattern, major crops and irrigation
Group-II S2-37: Aquaculture and fisheries in Andhra Pradesh - marine and inland

secs.t: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes

x: Exam angle: "AP ranks first in ___" (fish and shrimp) and the share figures - check which base (fish production / shrimp exports / seafood exports) the option uses.
India is the world’s second-largest fish producer, contributing about 9%, and leads in inland capture fisheries according to FAO SOFIA 2026.
India's preliminary 2024–25 seafood export was 16,98,170 MT, valued at ₹62,408.45 crore, or about US$7.45 billion.
The correct matching is 2023–24 with 52.55 and 51.58 LMT, 2024–25 with 56.62 and 55.39 LMT, and 2025–26 with 66.62 and 47.28 LMT up to December 2025.

secs.t: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use

x: Paddy is concentrated in East Godavari and the Godavari–Krishna deltas; groundnut in Anantapur; tobacco in Prakasam and Guntur; and coffee in the ASR–Araku region.
Rayalaseema leads Andhra Pradesh's horticulture sector with about 7.8 lakh hectares and a gross value added of ₹76,458 crore.
About 49.55 lakh hectares, or
of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area, was under cultivation in 2024–25.

secs.t: Irrigation profile - main source, area, tanks, projects

x: The decline was associated with the 2023-24 monsoon deficit, when rainfall was 718.2 mm against the normal 860 mm.
Kothakota Lift Irrigation Scheme is associated with the Tungabhadra in Kurnool, while Akkajamma Cheruvu LIS is in Nandyal.
Tube wells
account for 47.3 per cent of India’s net irrigated area, compared with 24.7 per cent for canals and 2.8 per cent for tanks.

secs.t: Livestock breeding - Gokul Gram, native breeds

x: Ongole and Punganur are cattle breeds, Godavari is a buffalo type and Nellore is associated with sheep.
Aseel is a native poultry type.
There are 10,606 Rythu Seva Kendras delivering veterinary services.

secs.t: Rayalaseema cropping - black and red soils, rainfed crops

x: Black or regur soil in Rayalaseema is suitable for
cotton
, along with jowar, chillies, tobacco and oilseeds.
Red soils support groundnut, ragi and tobacco, while rice and sugarcane can be grown in them only with irrigation.
Black gram, green gram and groundnut are among the rainfed shift crops.
The listed Rayalaseema fruit group comprises
mango, banana, tomato, papaya and citrus

secs.t: Externally aided agriculture projects → funding agency

x: APDMP is funded by
the International Fund for Agricultural Development
(IFAD).
Andhra Pradesh
Community-managed Natural Farming
received the Gulbenkian Prize in 2024.
All three statements are correct: both projects support drought-proofing, while APIIATP is World Bank-funded and APDMP is IFAD-funded.

secs.t: Cropping pattern - kharif vs rabi, dominant crop

x: The 17 growth engines cover 11 crops including paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, pulses, groundnut, sunflower and sesamum.
The cropping pattern is shifting towards oilseeds, millets, horticulture and oil palm, with productivity improvement initiatives for 11 crops.
Total foodgrain output was 161.86 lakh tonnes, paddy output 127.15 lakh tonnes, kharif foodgrain output 88.10 lakh tonnes and rabi output 73.76 lakh tonnes.

secs.t: Agricultural schemes of AP - Annadatha Sukhibhava, RSKs, APCNF

x: Annadatha Sukhibhava is the Andhra Pradesh state top-up to PM-KISAN’s ₹6,000 assistance.
The first Kharif 2026 instalment under Annadatha Sukhibhava was
per farmer.
APMIP, in operation since 2003, covered 2.05 lakh acres and 75,035 farmers with a subsidy of ₹793.67 crore in 2024–25.
Rythu Seva Kendralu are 10,606 village one-stop centres in all gram panchayats and include veterinary services.

secs.t: AP fisheries welfare - fishing-ban relief (Matsyakara Bharosa/Sevalo), diesel subsidy, insurance

x: PM-MKSSY runs from 2023–24 to 2026–27, has an allocation of ₹6,000 crore and promotes aquaculture insurance and credit.
A total of 4,155 transponders were installed: 1,376 on mechanised boats and 2,779 on motorised boats.
National Group Accident Insurance covers 33.15 lakh fishers annually, and the Kisan Credit Card facility has been extended to fishers since 2018-19.

secs.t: Inland fisheries - reservoir, tank, brackish-water aquaculture; leading districts

x: All three statements are correct: 2,07,765 ponds covering 5,79,697 acres were mapped into 3,725 clusters and 69 mega clusters.
The Integrated Aqua Park at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla district is being developed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
West Godavari
recorded 9.64 lakh MT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26.

secs.t: Marine fisheries - fishing harbours and fish landing centres → district

x: Juvvaladinne is in SPSR Nellore, Uppada in Kakinada, Nizampatnam in Bapatla and Machilipatnam in Krishna district.
Juvvaladinne
had the highest reported progress at 97.98 percent, followed by Uppada at 84.29 percent, Nizampatnam at 81.61 percent and Machilipatnam at 71.45 percent.
The Phase I fishing harbour works were estimated at
in the 2025–26 survey.
Phase II includes Biyyaputhippa, Kothapatnam, Pudimadaka, Budagatlapalem and Vodarevu.

secs.t: Fisheries institutions in AP → location

x: The ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre at Lawsons Bay Colony, Visakhapatnam, is associated with
open-sea cage farming
The AP Fisheries University was established under the AP Fisheries University Act, 2020, and is located in West Godavari district.
The MPEDA Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Aquaculture brood multiplication centre at Visakhapatnam is associated with P. monodon.

secs.t: Fishing-ban period and marine fishing regulation

x: The uniform ban is for 61 days, from 15 April to 14 June on the East Coast.
Traditional non-motorised craft
are exempt.
Penalties for the relevant fishing-ban violations are imposed under the
AP Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1995
The proposal concerns IUU fishing in Andhra Pradesh’s territorial waters, extending up to
12 nautical miles

secs.t: Kolleru lake aquaculture - encroachment issue

x: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is a breeding ground of the
spot-billed pelican
and also supports painted storks.
The sanctuary boundary is defined by the +5 ft contour, and Kolleru has been a Ramsar site since 2002.
Aquaculture ponds and fields have occupied portions of the lake bed, causing the lake to shrink and become eutrophic.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The value-chain plan covers mango, banana, tomato, pomegranate, sweet lime and papaya;
sugarcane
is not included in the listed plan.
Polavaram rehabilitation and resettlement stood at 45 percent against 88 percent progress of works, while Vamsadhara and Krishna waters involve sharing with Odisha and Telangana respectively.
FAO’s SOFIA 2026 report
stated that aquaculture had exceeded 100 million tonnes and formed 53 percent of aquatic animal output.

rows.title: Industrial location - factors and theories (Weber); world industrial regions

secs.t: World iron and steel regions → country

x: The Atlantic Coast iron and steel region, including Baltimore and Bethlehem, is in the
USA
Anshan is located in
Liaoning in north-east China
; Benxi is another important centre in the region.
Steel is weight-losing: about four tonnes of iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite produce one tonne of steel.

secs.t: Footloose industries and agglomeration economies

x: Diamond cutting
is a footloose industry because it is light, high-value and not tied to a specific raw-material location.
Agglomeration economies arise when firms cluster and benefit from shared infrastructure, specialised suppliers and a common skilled-labour pool.
Mumbai–Pune, Chennai–Bengaluru and Delhi-NCR are all examples of industrial clusters benefiting from agglomeration economies.

secs.t: World industrial regions and centres → country and industry

x: Kinki is in Japan, Po Valley in Italy, Flanders in Belgium and the Great Kanawha Valley in the USA.
The Po Valley, with centres such as Milan and Turin, is associated with
engineering, automobiles and textiles
Kinki is a dense industrial belt of Japan associated with textiles and heavy industry.

secs.t: Industrial city nicknames → city/region

x: Osaka
in Japan is known as the ‘Manchester of the East’.
Chennai
is referred to as the ‘Detroit of India’.
Chotanagpur
is known as the ‘Ruhr of India’.
Rust Belt or Rust Bowl denotes the old manufacturing belt of the north-eastern United States and the Great Lakes region.

secs.t: Leading producers - steel ranking, shipbuilding centres

x: India’s crude steel production is 168.4 MT, capacity is 220 MT and the target for 2030 is 300 MT.
Rourkela was established with German collaboration, whereas Bhilai was established with Soviet collaboration.
The policy targets 300 MT capacity and 255 MT crude steel production by 2030–31, requiring 437 MT iron ore and 161 MT coking coal.

secs.t: Weber's theory - locational triangle, material index, materials

x: Alfred Weber’s 1909 least-cost theory considers the combined
transport, labour and agglomeration
costs.
An MI greater than one indicates that localised raw materials weigh more than the finished product, favouring a raw-material-oriented location.
Isodapanes help explain how labour or agglomeration savings can draw a firm away from the least-transport-cost location.

secs.t: Other location theories

x: Edgar Hoover dealt with transport-cost structure and terminal costs; Walter Isard proposed the substitution principle; August Losch developed the maximum-profit and market-area approach; and P. Sargant Florence introduced the Location Quotient.
Walter Isard's substitution principle
explains the trade-off between transport costs and other costs in selecting an industrial location.
August Losch's approach
explains industrial location through maximum profit and the market area shaped by demand.

secs.t: Industrial shift to Asia and newly industrialising regions

x: Steel leadership has moved to China and India, while the older Western industrial regions of Ruhr, Lorraine and the US Rust Belt have declined.
The Asian Tigers are
South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Hong Kong
, recognised as newly industrialising economies.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Iron ore was added to the revised Index of Core Industries, bringing the number of industries to nine.
Chotanagpur is compared with Germany's Ruhr industrial region, while Chennai is compared with Detroit because of its industrial and automobile significance.
Samara's industrial region was reported to have been affected by
the Ukraine conflict
in August 2026.

rows.title: India - industrial regions and industrial belts; factors of localisation
sub: Group-II S2-39: Major industrial regions of India and factors of industrial location

secs.t: Industrial corridors - DMIC, CBIC, VCIC, AKIC, BMEC, Defence corridors, NICDC nodes

x: CBIC is associated with Japan through JICA, VCIC with ADB, AKIC with the Eastern DFC and NW-1, and BMEC with the United Kingdom.
The programme comprises 11 corridors; approval of 12 new industrial smart cities raised the project count to 20, and implementation involves NICDC and NICDIT.
The integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor proposed in Budget 2026-27 includes a node at
Durgapur
under the Purvodaya initiative.
The Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor has Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli; Madurai is not listed among its five nodes.
VCIC has nodes at Visakhapatnam, Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy; CBIC has the Krishnapatnam North Node; HBIC has the Orvakal node.

secs.t: Industrial centres → industry

x: Exam angle: UPPSC matching sets (Muri-aluminium, Gurgaon-automobiles, Vizag-shipbuilding, Panki-fertilisers; Aonla-fertilisers, Modinagar-rubber).
Muri is associated with aluminium, Aonla with fertilisers, Koyali with an oil refinery, and Singrauli with coal and thermal power.

The listed association is Modinagar with rubber, Barabanki with polyfibre and Panki with fertilisers; the notes associate explosives with Kanpur in the combined Modinagar-Barabanki-Kanpur industry listing, but the option is not a direct centre-industry pairing as stated.

secs.t: Major industrial regions of India → centres and specialisation

x: Jamshedpur, Ranchi, Dhanbad and Bokaro are major centres of the
Chotanagpur industrial region
, known as the ‘Ruhr of India’.

Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu is associated with IT and advanced industries; Visakhapatnam-Guntur with steel and petroleum-related industries; Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut with automobiles and electronics; and Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram with cashew, coir and rubber.
Navi Mumbai, Thane and Pimpri-Chinchwad
are centres of the Mumbai-Pune industrial region, noted for engineering, petrochemicals, automobiles and pharmaceuticals.

secs.t: Factors of localisation in India

x: The east-coast ports of
Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip and Tuticorin
serve mineral and petroleum hinterlands.
The steel belt lies on the Chota Nagpur Plateau because the principal raw materials are weight-losing and are therefore advantageously processed near their source.
The steel belt occupies parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal and is centred on steel production supported by mineral resources.

secs.t: Minor industrial regions and industrial districts

x: Mumbai-Pune
is a major industrial region, whereas Adilabad-Nizamabad, Allahabad-Varanasi-Mirzapur and the Brahmaputra valley are listed among minor industrial regions.
Ambala-Amritsar, Saharanpur-Muzaffarnagar-Bijnor, Jaipur-Ajmer and Durg-Raipur are all listed as minor industrial regions or districts.
The sequence from the north-western part of the listed regions towards the east is Jaipur-Ajmer, Allahabad-Varanasi-Mirzapur, Adilabad-Nizamabad and Brahmaputra valley.

secs.t: Regional imbalance - backward area incentives

x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 recognised
balanced regional growth
as an important objective and supported locating public-sector units in backward regions.
Salem
in Tamil Nadu, Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and Vijayanagar at Hospet in Karnataka are examples of public-sector plants located away from the principal raw-material areas.

of the fuel used by road transport per tonne-kilometre.

The stated RCS-UDAN figures are
657 routes and 93 airports, including heliports and water aerodromes

six metro airports

915.17 million tonnes

The CPPI 2024 placed two Indian ports in the global top 30 and seven Indian ports in the top 100.

Indian Airlines and Air India International
UDAN stands for Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik and operates through viability gap funding.

secs.t: East vs west coast port distribution - physical reasons

Mumbai, Mormugao and Kochi
are sheltered natural harbours on the western coast.
Eastern coast ports mainly handle
minerals, ore and petroleum
The eastern coast has mostly
artificial harbours
, including Chennai, described as the oldest, and VOC Tuticorin.

The five pillars are port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping with inland water transport.
Sagarmala 2.0 covers
shipbuilding, ship repair, ship breaking and recycling
The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets
10 billion tonnes per annum
of port capacity.

Union List Entry 27
and are governed under the Major Port Authorities Act.
PPP and captive operators are expected to handle about
80 percent
of major-port cargo by 2030.

Galathea Bay is located in
Great Nicobar
and is proposed to host an International Container Transshipment Terminal.
Galathea Bay is near the
Malacca Strait
, enhancing its strategic importance for transshipment.

Criticism of the Great Nicobar Project includes concerns that

secs.t: Regulators and bodies - TRAI, DoT, Prasar Bharati, TDSAT - functions

x: Exam angle: "regulator of telecom and broadcasting" = TRAI (not Prasar Bharati, which is the broadcaster).
TRAI regulates telecom and broadcasting matters including tariffs, quality of service and recommendations on spectrum and licensing.
TDSAT adjudicates telecom disputes and hears appeals against orders of TRAI.
Disputes and appeals were moved to TDSAT, which was created by the
TRAI (Amendment) Act, 2000
and set up in May 2000.

secs.t: Postal network - PIN code, IPPB, Speed Post, network size

x: Digi PIN is a 10-digit alphanumeric code intended for precise delivery and forms part of the Advanced Postal Technology platform.
The APT platform was built by CEPT, hosted on MeghRaj 2.0 cloud and piloted in Karnataka circle.
The APT platform had migrated 1.64 lakh offices and handled approximately 32 lakh bookings and 37 lakh deliveries per day.

secs.t: Telecom milestones and reforms - first telephone, liberalisation, MNP, teledensity, 5G

x: C-DOT was set up in 1984 during the Rajiv Gandhi era, when Indian telecom moved towards private-sector orientation.
The correct order is 1882, 1975, 1984 and 1994: first telephone exchange, SITE, C-DOT and National Telecom Policy 1994.
Bharat 6G Vision targets 2030, 100 academic 5G labs are identified, and TTDF sanctioned ₹275 crore for 104 projects by July 2025.

secs.t: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

x: Exam angle: "fastest form of data transmission" = optical fibre.
Optical fibre uses total internal reflection, has low loss, resists electromagnetic interference and forms the backbone of modern internet and data connectivity.
Copper media carry electrical signals, have lower bandwidth than optical fibre, suffer loss over distance and are comparatively interference-prone.

secs.t: Submarine cables and cable landing stations

x: CANI
stands for Chennai–Andaman & Nicobar Islands and connects Chennai with Port Blair and other islands.
The CANI submarine cable was inaugurated on
10 August 2020
KLI is the Kochi–Lakshadweep Islands submarine cable, inaugurated in January 2024.

secs.t: Digital connectivity - BharatNet, Digital India, NBM, PM-WANI, railway Wi-Fi

x: BharatNet was earlier called NOFN, targets Gram Panchayat connectivity, is funded by USOF and uses the fibre infrastructure of BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
The Amended BharatNet Programme includes PPP implementation, a larger State role, 100 Mbps scalable to 1 Gbps per Gram Panchayat and an approved outlay of ₹1.39 lakh crore.
Digital India has nine pillars, telephone connections exceeded 120 crore by April 2025, and the cited data cost declined from ₹308 to ₹9.34 per GB.

secs.t: Mass media - AIR, Doordarshan, community radio, newspaper registration

x: Community Radio Stations are licensed by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for
rural and remote areas
The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 law, the Press Registrar General administers registration, the earlier office was RNI, and the Press Council Act dates from 1978.
PIB, the Central Bureau of Communication and Publications Division are MIB media units.

last-mile connectivity to 3,942 villages and broadband to every household within 18 months

₹9,417 crore
. ₹10,134 crore refers to another reported railway allocation figure, while the other values relate to works or highway expenditure.

₹1.40 lakh crore

gives natural protection to Visakhapatnam harbour.

Visakhapatnam Port handled
5.12 lakh tonnes
of seafood and remained India’s top seafood-export port.

Buckingham Canal

Airport has DIGI YATRA and a new terminal costing ₹408.06 crore.

Juvvaladinne recorded 97.98%, Uppada 84.29%, Nizampatnam 81.61% and Machilipatnam 71.45% progress in Phase-I.

The line links Krishnapatnam Port to the Rayalaseema hinterland and includes the Cherlopalli–Rapuru tunnel.
Ramayapatnam is next to NH-16 and Thettu station.

x: The total road network was
, comprising 45,433 km of State roads and 8,744 km of National Highways.

The plans include 750 PM e-Bus Sewa buses, 300 for Tirupati–Tirumala and 8,819 over five years; the accident rate was 0.06 per lakh km.

x: Andhra Pradesh has three national industrial corridors, one major port, 17 non-major ports and NH-16, supporting its role as an east-coast gateway to South-East Asia.
Andhra Pradesh has set a target of achieving a
US$20 billion
blue economy by 2035.
The identified challenges include logistics cost, lack of dedicated freight rail to clusters, water-short inland nodes, CBI-stalled ports and land-acquisition delays.

secs.t: India's export composition - top items, destinations, largest world-market share

x: India's merchandise exports reached
US$ 441.78 billion
in FY 2025–26, an all-time high and an increase of 0.93%.
Goods plus services exports amounted to
US$ 860.09 billion
Petroleum products
were the largest listed export item, accounting for 14.48% of exports in 2024–25.
Electronics
was India's third-largest export category in FY 2025, after engineering goods and petroleum products.

secs.t: Import composition - top items and source countries

x: India's import dependence is about 88–89% for crude oil, 47–51% for natural gas and 26% for coal.

Bulk imports include petroleum, cereals and pulses,
edible oils
, sugar, fertilizer, metals and ores.

secs.t: India's trade policy evolution - import substitution, liberalisation, FTP 2023

x: FTP 2023 shifted from incentives to remission of duties and emphasized ease of exporting, e-initiatives and Districts as Export Hubs.

Export Promotion Mission
for 2025–26 to 2030–31 is run by DGFT through Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha.

Special Rupee Vostro Accounts
, or SRVAs.

corporate bonds and commercial papers

compared with the route around the Cape of Good Hope.

The
Cape of Good Hope
at the southern tip of Africa provides the long alternative route when the Suez Canal or Red Sea is unavailable.

, in the Netherlands, is Europe’s largest port.

in China is identified as the world’s busiest container port.

is the largest rice exporter and shipped 20.1 million metric tonnes in 2024–25.

The principal cotton exporters listed are the
USA, Brazil and Australia

x: USMCA comprises the USA, Mexico and Canada and replaced NAFTA.

the eight SAARC states
: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
BIMSTEC includes
Thailand
along with Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
RCEP comprises the ten ASEAN countries along with
China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand

secs.t: Trade balance and India's top trade partners

x: India’s merchandise trade deficit rose to
US$333.2 billion
in FY 2025–26, from US$282.5 billion in FY 2024–25.

India’s deficit with ASEAN rose from 10.4 billion US dollars in 2012 to
51.2 billion US dollars in 2025

secs.t: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

x: SAFTA, the successor to SAPTA, comprises
the eight SAARC countries
: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.

non-agricultural market access
; India, Brazil and South Africa are among its members.
SAPTA was signed in 1993, SAFTA in 2004, the India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement in 2009, and the India-UAE CEPA in 2022.

The India-Oman CEPA took effect on 1 June 2026, the India-New Zealand FTA was signed in April 2026, and the India-EU negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026 while formal ratification and signing remained pending.

JNPA
), also known as Nhava Sheva, is India’s largest container port and its first 100 per cent landlord major port.
Vadhavan Port is being developed through an SPV in which JNPA holds 74% and the Maharashtra Maritime Board 26%; the estimated cost is about ₹76,220 crore.
Deendayal Port
at Kandla is a tidal port in the Gulf of Kachchh and is associated with a Free Trade Zone and Asia’s first EPZ in 1965.

secs.t: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports

x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) functions as a decongestion or satellite port for Mumbai.

10 nautical miles
from the East-West shipping corridor.

was India’s largest export destination and continued to receive about one-fifth of India’s exports in April–July 2026-27.

Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
(MoPSW), renamed in 2020, is the nodal ministry for Sagarmala.

handled the highest volume among the specified non-major ports, with 41.09 million metric tonnes during April–November 2025.

in March 2026 as a result of the West Asia war.

after the FTAs, a point raised in debates about trade performance.

of Andhra Pradesh’s exports go to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together.

of India's shrimp exports, particularly white-leg shrimp produced in West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore.

NSHIP-AP Ltd
is building the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster.
The cluster aims to secure a
share of national shipbuilding capacity by 2047.

DGFT
) is the nodal agency for the Districts as Export Hubs initiative.
The September 2026 phased rollout merged One District One Product (ODOP) into Districts as Export Hubs and provided Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras for postal exports.

The Phase-I Visakhapatnam District Export Hub covers marine products, engineering goods and health services.

at concessional duty
The Baba Kalyani Committee proposed the term “3Es”, meaning
Employment and Economic Enclaves
, for SEZs.

trade hubs that lack logistics
; it is not an unconditional relaxation for every proposed dry port.

The amended policy permits temporary, eco-friendly beach shacks in CRZ-III and CRZ-IV areas.

Belum Caves are in Nandyal, Andhra Pradesh; Erra Matti Dibbalu are near Bheemunipatnam; Kalinjar Hill is in Banda; and National Fossil Wood Park is at Tiruvakkarai, Tamil Nadu.

, an NGO established in Paris in 1965, evaluates cultural and mixed World Heritage nominations.

Andhra Pradesh's draft MICE policy identifies Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada as hubs; its plans include two sea-cruise, four river-cruise and one seaplane circuit, while Travel for LiFE promotes eco-responsible travel.
MICE tourism is characterised as high-yield, low-volume tourism and includes meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.

Direct jobs are created at tourism-service points, while indirect employment is generated through supply chains and tax-linked economic activity.

The total sanction was

, comprising ₹127.40 crore under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and ₹79.37 crore under PRASHAD.

colonial summer retreats

The project involves Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli, an investment of US$15 billion, and groundbreaking in April 2026.

The Char Dham of Uttarakhand comprises Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri.

” because of its near-freezing winters.

Etikoppaka toys of Anakapalli are known for lacquer work and the use of natural dyes.

sub: Group-II S2-31: Energy resources of India - coal, petroleum, natural gas, hydel, nuclear, renewable

secs.t: Energy source classification - renewable vs non-renewable, fossil fuels, power-plant fuels, petroleum products

x: Exam angle: "which is not a fossil fuel / which is renewable" one-liners.
Solar and wind
are identified as energy-transition sources because they support the shift towards cleaner, non-fossil energy.
India’s installed-capacity mix has crossed the 54% non-fossil level, while coal continues to dominate primary energy and electricity generation.
Natural gas
is a non-renewable fossil fuel formed over millions of years from organic matter.
Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels; nuclear energy is non-renewable, while solar and wind energy are renewable.
The non-fossil capacity share was reported as
by December 2025, exceeding the 50% milestone ahead of schedule.

secs.t: Coal - grades, Gondwana vs Tertiary, lignite, mining methods, coal PSUs

x: Peat contains less than 40% carbon, lignite about 40–50%, bituminous coal 40–80%, and anthracite 80–95%.
Gondwana coal is 250–300 million years old, Tertiary coal is 15–60 million years old, and peat represents the first stage in coal formation; present production is the latest item.
Rat-hole mining involves very narrow pits, sometimes extending up to 400 feet, dug with primitive tools by small, often family-run groups.
SCCL mines Godavari Valley coal in Telangana and is jointly owned in a 51:49 ratio by Telangana and the Centre.
The GSI estimate placed India's coal resources at
389.421 billion tonnes
as on 1 April 2024.
Gondwana coal is 250–300 million years old, constitutes about 98% of reserves, contains coking coal and occurs in the four stated valleys.

secs.t: Nuclear power - reactors → district and state, three-stage programme, breeder concept

x: Kaiga
nuclear power plant is located in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka and uses PHWR technology.
Kudankulam is located in Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu and uses Russian VVER-1000 reactors.
Tarapur, located in Palghar district of Maharashtra, was commissioned in 1969 and was India’s first commercial nuclear power plant, using US BWRs.
Stage II uses plutonium from Stage I in fast breeder reactors, while AHWRs belong to the thorium-based third stage.
The SHANTI Act, 2025 repeals the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010, and permits the admission of private companies.
India’s stated thorium resource is 3,60,000 tonnes, approximately 25 per cent of the world’s total, while natural uranium is 70,000 tonnes.

secs.t: Thermal power stations → state or district

x: NTPC’s Simhadri is a coal-based thermal station in the Visakhapatnam area of Andhra Pradesh and uses seawater.
Coal plants generally operate at a 60–85% plant load factor, can run continuously and consume substantial industrial water.
Tanda in Uttar Pradesh lies to the north, followed broadly by Ramagundam in Telangana, Kudgi in Karnataka and Simhadri in Andhra Pradesh toward the south-east coast.

secs.t: Leading states - reserves and installed capacity

x: The Barmer basin in
Rajasthan
is an important onshore oil-producing region containing the Mangala, Bhagyam and Aishwariya fields.
Gujarat
led renewable-energy capacity with 42.58 GW, or 16.5 per cent of India's total.

India's wind-energy potential at 120 metres is assessed at approximately

NP Kunta, also called the Ananthapuramu Ultra Mega Solar Park, is located in Sri Sathya Sai district.

secs.t: Renewable energy - national targets, Green Energy Corridor, Green Hydrogen Mission, rooftop solar, budget

x: The Budget proposed CCUS at scale in all five listed sectors: power, steel, cement, refineries and chemicals.
The Budget provided no basic customs duty on capital goods used for processing critical minerals and nil duty on monazite.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets production of 5 million metric tonnes per year.
The Jind–Sonipat hydrogen train entered service, and India signed long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements with Japanese companies.
The mission aims to make India a global green hydrogen hub and supports energy independence by 2047 and net zero by 2070.

secs.t: Petroleum and gas - first oil well, oilfields and refineries → state, shale gas basins

x: Guwahati is the first public-sector refinery, Numaligarh is operated by NRL, Jamnagar is the largest refining complex and Visakhapatnam is operated by HPCL.
Assam contains Digboi and Naharkatiya, Gujarat contains the Cambay Basin fields, and the KG Basin extends across offshore and onshore areas of Andhra Pradesh.
The listed shale gas basins include Cambay, Assam-Arakan, Gondwana or Damodar, KG, Cauvery and Indo-Gangetic basins.
The Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga pipeline is identified by the
Jagdishpur–Haldia–Bokaro–Dhamra
route.
Digboi and Ankleshwar are onshore locations, followed by the offshore locations Mumbai High and the offshore KG Basin fields.
All four statements are correct: the bill rose 41 per cent year-on-year, volume was 21.4 MMT, product exports rose 10 per cent to 5.5 MMT, and India has been a net product exporter since 2001–02.

secs.t: Hydroelectric potential - Himalayan vs Peninsular, pumped storage

x: The Brahmaputra, Indus and Ganga basins possess most of India’s hydroelectric potential because Himalayan rivers have perennial snow-fed flow and steep gradients.
Pumped storage stores surplus daytime electricity, particularly solar power, and releases it during night-time peak demand.
Andhra Pradesh plans 7,370 MW of pumped storage capacity and 3,931 MW of battery storage capacity by 2035–36.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Raniganj was associated with the first coal mine in 1774, Digboi with the first oil discovery in 1889, Tarapur with the first nuclear plant in 1969, and Pinnapuram is the later integrated renewable-energy storage project.
All four associations are correct: Tummalapalle is associated with uranium, Kurnool with a solar park, Kovvada with a nuclear project site and the KG Basin with oil and gas resources.

of National Highway corridors and aims to improve freight and passenger efficiency.

The last-mile rail links to Kopparthy and Orvakal are incomplete, increasing dependence on road transport.

railway carries Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through tunnels in the Eastern Ghats.

in specified tribal districts of Andhra Pradesh.
